pages.title: The State of Aviation 2025
Can the aviation industry soar to new heights, or will headwinds slow its progress?

pages.abstract: This page discusses the current state of the aviation industry, highlighting its recovery from pandemic impacts and addressing challenges like economic trends and geopolitical events. It emphasizes the importance of strategic decision-making based on thorough analysis for achieving commercial and operational goals.
pages.title: The State of Aviation 2025

pages.abstract: This page highlights key statistics about the aviation industry in 2024, including airline performance, pricing influence on traveler decisions, operational costs due to delays, and the global aircraft shortage.
pages.title: The State of Aviation 2025

pages.abstract: This chapter explores the potential for continued growth in the global airline industry, examining factors that could influence its trajectory.
pages.title: Can the global airline industry continue its climb?

pages.abstract: The airline sector faced numerous challenges in 2024 due to weather, infrastructure issues, and economic uncertainties. Despite historical struggles with negative economic profits, recent data shows improvement, with 41% of airlines earning their cost of capital. This shift raises questions about structural changes and future sustainability.
pages.title: The airline sector had a decent year in 2024. Is it finally cracking the value creation formula?

pages.abstract: The global airline industry's ROIC approached its cost of capital in 2023 and 2024, with regional variations and notable improvements in value creation compared to pre-pandemic levels. Despite some lagging performers, several airlines consistently earned their cost of capital over the past decade.
pages.title: The global airline industry’s ROIC approached its cost of capital in 2023 and 2024.

pages.abstract: The document discusses how a significant portion of global airlines generated value in 2023 and 2024 despite varying jet fuel prices. It highlights factors contributing to airline value creation, including balancing capacity and demand, generating ancillary revenue, maintaining reliability, and offering unique routes.
pages.title: A relatively high share of global airlines created value in 2023 and 2024.

pages.abstract: The document discusses how OEM and supply chain issues led to reduced aircraft availability in 2024, impacting airline capacity. Airlines responded by extending leases and using older planes, leading to higher ticket prices due to undersupply. However, increased manufacturer orders suggest future supply growth, while factors like GDP and sustainable fuels may affect demand.
pages.title: OEM and supply chain challenges resulted in fewer available aircraft in 2024, meaning that airlines had less capacity than they perhaps would have liked.

pages.abstract: This page discusses the impact of economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions on the aviation industry, highlighting improved returns from ancillaries, the value of loyalty programs, the importance of reliability in airline performance, and the concept of network privilege in generating higher yields.
pages.title: Recent economic uncertainty posed by global trade developments

pages.abstract: This page discusses how airlines' on-time performance correlates with financial performance, highlighting the role of hubs in creating privileged offerings and tapping into secondary markets. It also covers strategies for increasing capital productivity through efficient aircraft utilization and strategic purchasing.
pages.title: Airlines' on-time performance correlates with their financial performance.

pages.abstract: This page discusses how airlines can manage demand seasonality by adjusting their aircraft fleets and highlights the increasing capital productivity over time. It emphasizes the importance of healthy organizational structures in airlines, which facilitate cross-functional decision-making and employee motivation. The text introduces McKinsey's Organizational Health Index as a tool to measure organizational health and its correlation with better airline performance. A scatter plot illustrates the relationship between ROIC and OHI scores, showing that healthier organizations tend to achieve better ROIC.
pages.title: Airlines with better organizational health tend to achieve better ROIC.

pages.abstract: This page highlights the importance of healthy airline organizations in effectively integrating various functions to achieve cross-functional trade-offs, emphasizing their superior capability compared to others.
pages.title: Healthy airline organizations are better able than others to bring disparate functions together to make cross-functional trade-offs.

pages.abstract: The document discusses potential challenges facing airlines in 2025, including demand uncertainty, economic factors, and trade tensions. It highlights the importance of adaptability and strategic planning for airlines to maintain financial health amidst these uncertainties.
pages.title: What could halt airlines' progress in 2025?

pages.abstract: This page introduces Chapter 2, questioning whether low-cost airlines are facing challenges. It features an image of a cabin crew member, symbolizing the airline industry's operational aspects.
pages.title: Are low-cost airlines losing altitude?

pages.abstract: This page discusses the categorization of airlines based on their business models, highlighting the superior financial performance of low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers (U)LCCs compared to legacy carriers globally. However, it notes a recent decline in U.S. (U)LCCs' performance relative to legacy carriers, prompting an investigation into the underlying causes and broader business model implications.
pages.title: Low- and ultra-low-cost airlines have tended to earn better returns than full-service carriers, but their performance has slowed in the United States. Are there lessons here for global airline leaders?

pages.abstract: This page discusses how low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers (U)LCCs outperformed legacy carriers before the pandemic due to leaner cost structures, streamlined operations, and effective revenue generation strategies. However, recent trends show legacy carriers leading in ROIC in North America.
pages.title: Low-cost airlines generally outperformed full-service carriers prior to the pandemic.

pages.abstract: The document illustrates the growing market share of low-cost airlines (LCCs) across various regions from 2009 to 2024. In North America, however, LCCs have recently underperformed compared to legacy carriers in terms of Return on Invested Capital (ROIC).
pages.title: Low-cost airlines have steadily increased share across most regions.

pages.abstract: North America's (U)LCCs face challenges due to rising labor costs, divergent spending patterns, and competition from legacy carriers. Post-pandemic labor shortages have significantly impacted (U)LCCs' operational costs, reducing their cost advantage over legacy airlines.
pages.title: What happened to North America’s discount airlines?

pages.abstract: This page discusses how North America exemplifies a significant shift in aviation trends, but similar changes are also occurring in other regions like Latin America, where legacy carriers outperform low-cost carriers in terms of Return on Invested Capital (ROIC).
pages.title: While North America presents the clearest example of this shift, recent data suggest it is not the only region where changes are afoot. In Latin America, for instance, legacy carriers are now leading (U)LCCs with respect to ROIC.

pages.abstract: The document discusses how post-pandemic US consumer spending is shifting towards premium travel options among high-income households while lower-income households reduce discretionary spending due to inflation. Legacy carriers are adapting by launching budget-friendly products to compete with ultra-low-cost carriers (ULCCs), combining low prices with premium experiences. Despite this, ULCCs continue to grow faster than legacy carriers outside North America.
pages.title: Growth in premium demand—paired with softer demand for budget options

pages.abstract: This page discusses global airline trends, emphasizing cost control, customer value, and segment-specific strategies. It highlights North America's influence on airline competition and suggests adapting business models for sustained success.
pages.title: Global airline trends and lessons from North America

pages.abstract: This chapter discusses the eight common misconceptions in airline retailing, highlighting how these myths impact the industry. It includes an image of a person holding a smartphone with a 'BOOK NOW' button and travel time details, emphasizing modern booking practices.
pages.title: The eight myths of airline retailing

pages.abstract: This page discusses the airline industry's efforts to adapt to changing consumer expectations by improving retailing approaches. It highlights challenges such as siloed structures and legacy systems, and introduces a global survey aimed at understanding traveler preferences and debunking common myths in airline retailing.
pages.title: Airlines are rethinking how they sell their offerings and service their customers. Understanding common misconceptions about airline retailing could help accelerate growth.

pages.abstract: This page discusses how airlines can better capture customer preferences by offering customizable bundles beyond static airfare options. It highlights various traveler priorities, such as price, baggage allowance, and seat selection, and emphasizes the need for airlines to adapt to diverse consumer segments.
pages.title: Myth #1: Airlines have already captured the full value of customer preferences

pages.abstract: This page discusses the myth that more personalization always leads to better experiences for travelers. It highlights the importance of clarity and control in personalization, emphasizing that travelers prefer practical value over excessive customization. The text also explores the gap between airline offerings and customer preferences, suggesting that airlines should tailor their products dynamically to meet genuine traveler needs.
pages.title: Myth #2: More personalization always equals better experiences

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of personalization in airline travel, highlighting real-time assistance and AI's potential role. It also addresses the myth that travelers prefer separate bookings, emphasizing the value of well-designed travel bundles.
pages.title: Airline passengers value personalized, real-time travel assistance.

pages.abstract: This page discusses the effectiveness of well-designed travel bundles tailored to customer needs and sensibly priced, highlighting regional and generational preferences. It emphasizes the importance of modern airline merchandising techniques, including behavioral nudging and immersive content, to enhance sales and customer satisfaction.
pages.title: Myth #4: Basic digital presence and traditional promotions are enough to sell airline products effectively

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of visual merchandising in aviation, emphasizing its impact on consumer decision-making and airline revenue. It highlights the need for an omnichannel approach in merchandising and explores the myth that direct channels will dominate flight bookings. Despite growth in direct channels, intermediaries remain strong, and new players are entering the market, diversifying the distribution landscape.
pages.title: Myth #5: Recent growth of direct channels means they will soon dominate flight bookings

pages.abstract: This page discusses various factors influencing air travelers' choice of booking platforms, highlighting convenience, best prices, and trust in brands as key considerations. It also addresses traveler preferences for direct booking and the importance of improving digital experiences. Additionally, it debunks the myth that booking frustrations are primarily due to legacy technology, emphasizing instead concerns about pricing transparency and flexibility.
pages.title: Air travelers cite a variety of reasons for choosing which channel to book tickets through.

Content

pages.abstract: This page introduces the growing trend of global travel in 2024, highlighting challenges in trip planning due to overwhelming options. It discusses research findings on traveler dissatisfaction and the potential of generative AI to streamline the travel experience, offering personalized solutions and significant industry opportunities.
pages.title: Introduction
The traveler experience today

pages.abstract: Travelers predominantly use desktops or laptops for trip planning, starting preparations early—domestically one to three months ahead and internationally up to a year in advance. They focus on finding the best value through monitoring deals and prices.
pages.title: The traveler experience today

pages.abstract: This page discusses what inspires today's travelers, highlighting the importance of travel reviews, social media, and influencers. It emphasizes the role of multi-modal content and personal connections in influencing travel decisions.
pages.title: What inspires today's traveler?

pages.abstract: This page discusses how personal contacts and various media influence travelers' decisions. It highlights the rise of 'bleisure' trips post-pandemic and emphasizes the role of online reviews and videos in trip planning. Additionally, it underscores the importance of rich media like interactive maps and visual content in inspiring and informing travelers.
pages.title: The traveler experience today

pages.abstract: The page discusses traveler preferences for planning trips, highlighting reliance on offline agents for 28% and extensive online research for others. It emphasizes challenges faced by travelers with fixed budgets and the variety of tools used for managing trip details.
pages.title: Getting down to planning

pages.abstract: This page discusses traveler experiences, highlighting the challenges of planning trips due to complex website redirections and personal efforts. It also presents survey results showing who plans travel and the main difficulties faced, such as managing variables and decision fatigue.
pages.title: The traveler experience today

pages.abstract: Travelers prioritize safety (27%) in initial trip planning, followed by destination/trip experience (22%) and flexibility (13%). Specific criteria at the destination include quality of service, cleanliness, food options, and safety/security assurances.
pages.title: The traveler experience today

pages.abstract: This page discusses traveler dissatisfaction with current planning options, highlighting issues like complexity, lack of customization, and privacy concerns. It explores desires for seamless booking experiences, subscription-based platforms, and personalized features, summarizing these in a 'Travelers' Wish List'.
pages.title: The great disconnect: Travelers' expectations versus reality

pages.abstract: This page outlines the subcategories of traveler experiences across different stages of travel, highlighting AI capabilities such as natural language search, personalized content, real-time assistance, and post-journey feedback. It emphasizes how AI can enhance the travel sector and introduces Saudia's AI-powered Travel Companion.
pages.title: The Traveler Experience Today
How gen AI can reinvent travel

pages.abstract: The page discusses how generative AI can revolutionize travel by enhancing user experiences through dedicated travel apps and superapps. It highlights the benefits of AI in providing personalized, integrated travel services and managing complex stages like inspiration and booking.
pages.title: How gen AI can reinvent travel

pages.abstract: Gen AI tools enhance personalized travel planning by simplifying complex tasks like collaborative planning and price comparison. Despite current limitations, future advancements in natural language processing and responsible data usage can significantly improve user experience.
pages.title: How gen AI can reinvent travel

pages.abstract: Gen AI can revolutionize travel booking by offering a centralized interface for payments, rewards, and itineraries, automating research and planning with real-time data-driven recommendations, enhancing traveler experiences, and maximizing revenues for the travel industry.
pages.title: How gen AI can reinvent travel
Where travel providers stand

pages.abstract: Travel executives recognize gen AI's value for cost savings, efficiency, and growth. Priorities vary by sector, with airlines focusing on top-line growth and OTAs on brand perception.
pages.title: Executives' gen AI priorities

pages.abstract: The page discusses the implementation of generative AI in various business functions within the travel industry, highlighting key use cases like chatbots, market forecasting, and personalized travel planning. It emphasizes the need for enterprise-wide adoption and measurement of AI's impact.
pages.title: Use cases underway

pages.abstract: The page discusses the importance of prioritizing the workforce in the travel industry, highlighting the need for continuous training and upskilling initiatives. It mentions various methods like MOOCs, gamification, and apprenticeships, emphasizing the role of executives in addressing workforce readiness challenges.
pages.title: Prioritizing the workforce

pages.abstract: Travel companies are recognizing the importance of responsible AI adoption, focusing on transparency, ethics, and governance. They are building foundational elements for AI-specific applications but are still largely in the planning and assessment stages. Few have implemented AI at scale across their operations.
pages.title: Tech readiness

pages.abstract: This page highlights how various travel companies are leveraging generative AI to enhance traveler experiences through advanced planning tools, personalized assistance, and adaptive solutions, improving efficiency and user interaction.
pages.title: Some travel companies have already started using gen AI to provide new services and experiences for travelers.
Building the data foundations to take generative AI to scale

pages.abstract: The page discusses the need for enterprise reinvention in the travel industry to leverage gen AI, emphasizing the importance of a digital core and data sharing ecosystems. It highlights challenges such as limited access to industry data partnerships and outdated data systems. The content also presents data on various types of accessible data and future investment trends in gen AI within the industry.
pages.title: Building the data foundations to take gen AI to scale

pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges travel leaders face in adopting gen AI, such as technology capability gaps, data management issues, and integration with legacy systems. It highlights the proactive measures being taken, including investments in data security, talent acquisition, system integration, risk mitigation policies, and change management strategies.
pages.title: Barriers to adoption
Key principles for executives seeking to unlock the power of generative AI

pages.abstract: This page outlines key principles for leveraging generative AI in the travel industry, emphasizing quick wins, data integration, and responsible AI deployment to enhance customer experiences and operational efficiency.
pages.title: Key principles for executives seeking to unlock the power of gen AI

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of continuously evaluating successful working experiences through identifying skill gaps, establishing feedback loops, and fostering collaboration across various teams. It highlights the role of a gen AI center of excellence in improving processes and emphasizes the value of strategic alliances for accessing tools and insights.
pages.title: Continuously evaluate what a successful working experience is and how to support it
Let's move people

pages.abstract: This page discusses the transformative potential of generative AI in the travel industry, emphasizing the need for investment in advanced technologies and the benefits of enhancing customer experiences. It highlights the challenge of selecting appropriate AI models and introduces Accenture's Switchboard tool for streamlined model selection.
pages.title: How can Accenture help?

中东地区税负较低，吸引跨国公司投资。企业所得税和增值税税率因国家而异，如巴林企业所得税为0%，以色列为23%；增值税方面，阿曼和阿联酋为5%，以色列为17%。各国对特定行业有特殊税率规定。
该页面详细介绍了中东十国的关税政策，包括以色列、埃及、沙特、约旦、伊拉克、阿曼、科威特、卡塔尔、阿联酋和巴林的关税税率和特殊税收政策，涵盖了不同商品类别的税率差异和特定商品的免税或高税率情况。
本章节探讨了普华永道如何支持中国企业拓展海外市场，提供专业服务和策略指导，助力企业成功‘出海’。
普华永道全球网络广泛覆盖149个国家和地区，在45个国家设有中国业务组，并外派100余名中国同事常驻30多个国家，助力中国企业开拓国际市场。
普华永道在中东地区运营40多年，拥有12,000多名员工和30个办事处，提供专业服务并覆盖多个行业，助力客户应对挑战与机遇。
普华永道利用全球网络和专业服务支持中资企业拓展中东市场，借助‘一带一路’倡议下的机遇，提供全面的管理咨询、交易、税务和审计服务，助力中国企业与中东地区深化经贸合作。

pages.title: The State of Fashion 2025

pages.abstract: The authors express gratitude to various contributors from McKinsey and The Business of Fashion for their roles in creating the State of Fashion 2025 report, including survey participants, interviewees, and team members.
pages.title: ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
CONTENTS

pages.abstract: This page introduces key contributors to The State of Fashion 2025, detailing their roles, expertise, and contributions to the fashion industry. It highlights their backgrounds, professional experiences, and specific areas of focus within the industry.
pages.title: CONTRIBUTORS
CONTRIBUTORS

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces significant challenges in 2025, including consumer price sensitivity, economic uncertainty, and regional disparities. Growth opportunities exist but require adaptability. Sluggish revenue growth is expected, with non-luxury driving economic profit. Geographic shifts in revenue drivers are also occurring, with Europe, the US, and Asia playing key roles.
pages.title: Challenges at Every Turn

pages.abstract: The fashion industry is adapting to changing consumer priorities by localising go-to-market models, broadening price ranges, and focusing on brand positioning. Brands are also reevaluating consumer cohorts, with the 'Silver Generation' of over-50 customers becoming more significant. Improving the in-store shopping experience and leveraging AI for product discovery are key strategies. Supply chain agility, sustainability, and embracing new technologies are essential for future success.
pages.title: Acting on Opportunities

pages.abstract: This page introduces the industry outlook, focusing on the market share dynamics and how the game is leveling up. It highlights the evolving landscape and competitive shifts in the fashion industry.
pages.title: Industry Outlook The Market Share Game Levels Up

pages.abstract: The BoF-McKinsey State of Fashion 2025 Executive Survey reveals that uncertainty remains the dominant sentiment among fashion leaders. Only 20% expect conditions to improve in 2025, while 39% anticipate worsening conditions. Key concerns include consumer confidence, geopolitical instability, and economic volatility, with inflation becoming less of a concern as central banks lower interest rates.
pages.title: Uncertainty persists as executives enter 2025 with less optimism for the year ahead

pages.abstract: The fashion industry is expected to experience low single-digit growth in 2025, with a structural deceleration following the post-pandemic boom. Brands will focus on capturing market share due to muted consumer confidence. Retail sales growth forecasts by geography and segment are provided for Europe, US, and China, showing varying growth rates for non-luxury and luxury segments.
pages.title: Fashion industry growth is expected to remain low, but increase slightly from 2024

pages.abstract: The document outlines the macroeconomic challenges facing Europe, the US, and China, with projections for GDP growth and market growth in the luxury and non-luxury sectors. Europe faces economic uncertainty, while the US sees rising consumer power. China experiences a structural slowdown. Luxury demand varies by region, influenced by factors like consumer confidence and UHNWI population growth.
pages.title: The macroeconomic climate will continue to challenge growth across regions

pages.abstract: Fashion executives anticipate modest growth in 2025, driven by volume rather than price increases. A shift from price to volume growth is expected, with nearly two-thirds of executives predicting volume growth in the low single digits. Consumers' sensitivity to price hikes, especially among middle- and lower-income shoppers, is influencing this trend.
pages.title: Fashion executives expect volume, rather than price, to drive modest growth in 2025

pages.abstract: Fashion executives are prioritizing differentiation through localization, assortment variety, and AI innovation while reducing focus on cost improvements. Sustainability is less emphasized as executives seek growth opportunities. The biggest opportunities in 2024 and 2025 include sustainability objectives, AI leverage, and differentiation strategies.
pages.title: To capture market share, fashion executives are focusing on differentiation

pages.abstract: The page discusses global economic shifts and consumer trends impacting the fashion industry, including trade reconfiguration, emerging growth in Asia, AI-driven product discovery, the rise of older consumers, and cost-conscious shopping behaviors.
pages.title: The State of

pages.abstract: This page discusses key trends in the fashion industry for 2025, including enhancing in-store experiences, challenges faced by online marketplaces, the rise of challenger sportswear brands, inventory management issues, and the need for collective sustainability efforts.
pages.title: Fashion 2025

pages.abstract: This page introduces the reconfiguration of trade, featuring an image of container ships at a port, symbolizing the evolving dynamics of global trade logistics.
pages.title: 01. Trade Reconfigured

pages.abstract: Global trade is shifting due to political alignment, rising costs, and sustainability targets. Fashion brands will diversify sourcing in Asia and focus on nearshoring. Key insights include increased trade barriers, diversification of US imports away from China, and growth in nearshoring investments. Executive priorities involve assessing sourcing, collaborating with suppliers, and partnering with stakeholders for sustainability.
pages.title: 01. Trade Reconfigured

pages.abstract: The page discusses the diversification of global trade sourcing and reduction in geopolitical distance of trade flows. It highlights the shift from a US-China-centric trade relationship to a multi-polar structure due to geopolitical tensions and market changes. Key points include the decrease in US imports from China, EU's efforts to diversify supply chains, and major economies reducing trade risks by aligning with geopolitically similar countries.
pages.title: Global economies are diversifying sourcing and reducing the geopolitical distance of trade flows

pages.abstract: The document discusses the diversification of apparel and textile sourcing, highlighting a shift away from China towards other Asian markets and nearshoring. It details the percentage changes in imports for the US and Europe from 2019 to 2030E, emphasizing the decline in China's share and the rise of other regions. The text also explains the reasons behind this trend, including supply chain resilience, cost competitiveness, and nearshoring strategies.
pages.title: Diversification of apparel and textiles sourcing will likely continue at pace in the years to come

pages.abstract: The page discusses the impact of rising sourcing costs, tariffs, and sustainability targets on sourcing diversification. It highlights a 165% increase in Asia-to-US shipping costs, a 5x increase in trade restrictions, and 63% of fashion brands needing to accelerate emission reduction efforts. The text also mentions labor cost shifts, EU import duties, and investments in decarbonization.
pages.title: Rising sourcing costs, tariffs and sustainability targets may accelerate sourcing diversification

pages.abstract: Fashion brands are increasingly looking to Asian countries like India and Bangladesh for manufacturing due to their growing capabilities and incentives. India is expected to play a prominent role, with government investments and reforms. However, challenges in production and quality control persist. Bangladesh faces disruptions, leading to order shifts. The trend is expected to continue as Asia becomes a top sourcing hotspot.
pages.title: Fashion brands will look to Asia growth markets such as India for manufacturing

pages.abstract: Nearshoring interest has surged, with investments increasing in the US and Europe. Despite challenges like limited capacity and higher costs, nearshoring offers benefits such as improved productivity, faster lead times, and reduced environmental impact. Government incentives and strategic initiatives further support this trend.
pages.title: Renewed interest in nearshoring is leading to increased capacity and improved capabilities

pages.abstract: Latin America is becoming a key nearshoring hub for US fashion companies due to advantageous trade agreements and cost-effective shipping routes. Turkey is emerging as a crucial sourcing location for European brands, offering reduced order-to-fulfilment times and increased supply chain traceability.
pages.title: Latin America is emerging as a key nearshoring hub for the US, as is Turkey for Europe

pages.abstract: This page outlines executive priorities for flexible supply chains and close supplier relationships, emphasizing footprint assessment, strategic partnerships, and industry collaboration for efficiency, resilience, and sustainability.
pages.title: Flexible supply chains and close supplier relationships will be critical to success

pages.abstract: A fashion show in Mumbai, featuring models in yellow floral outfits walking along a decorated runway, set against the backdrop of the Gateway of India, symbolizing Asia's growing influence in fashion.
pages.title: 02. Asia's New Growth Engines

pages.abstract: This page discusses Asia's new growth engines in the fashion industry, highlighting India's strong growth and Japan's luxury market boom. It provides key insights and executive priorities for fashion executives to adapt to changing consumer preferences and market dynamics in Asia.
pages.title: 02. Asia’s New Growth Engines

pages.abstract: China's economy, now worth $18 trillion, is projected to grow by 4.5% in 2025, but this reflects a slowdown from previous years. The IMF forecasts a further decline to 3.3% by 2029. This economic deceleration impacts the fashion market, with apparel sales growth halving compared to 2019 levels. Consumer confidence and property transactions are at all-time lows, and the debt-to-GDP ratio has reached a historic high.
pages.title: As China’s sizeable GDP growth slows, so will its fashion market’s growth

pages.abstract: The non-luxury segment sees domestic brands gaining share, while the luxury segment faces a slowdown due to changing consumer preferences and government policies. Domestic brands in non-luxury grew by 6 percentage points from 2013 to 2023, while international brands declined. In the luxury market, despite some brands' growth, overall luxury spending in China slowed, with consumers shifting towards more affordable products and spending abroad projected to increase.
pages.title: This deceleration, coupled with changing consumer preferences, is challenging growth

pages.abstract: Fashion executives are optimistic about growth prospects in Asia, particularly India and Japan. The sentiment is especially high for mature APAC regions like Japan and Korea, and emerging markets like Indonesia and Thailand are also gaining prominence. The BoF-McKinsey survey shows a positive outlook for these regions in 2025.
pages.title: Fashion executives have a positive outlook for other Asian countries, particularly India and Japan

pages.abstract: India's fashion market is set to grow significantly, driven by a strong middle class and digitisation in non-luxury, and demographic and structural factors in luxury. The middle class is expected to reach 1 billion by 2050, while the UHNWI population is projected to grow 50% by 2028. Aspirational luxury consumers are also increasing, and new luxury malls are emerging in tier-one cities.
pages.title: India is poised to become a key fashion market due to a strong mid-market and potential in luxury

pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges and considerations for fashion brands entering the Indian market, including infrastructure limitations, the importance of local partners, unique consumer preferences, and regulatory requirements. It highlights the growth plans of brands like Mango, Decathlon, and Bulgari, and the need to adapt to regional nuances and cultural influences.
pages.title: Fashion brands looking to succeed in India need to consider its unique obstacles and nuances

pages.abstract: Japan's luxury market surged in 2024 due to yen depreciation, attracting global shoppers and boosting duty-free sales. Tourism also recovered, with a significant increase in visitors from various countries, contributing to the growth in tax-free shopping spend compared to 2019.
pages.title: The yen’s weakness made Japan a major international shopping destination in 2024

pages.abstract: The Japanese luxury market is projected to grow between 8-12% by 2025, driven by both international and domestic demand. Brands are expanding their presence, and tourism spending is expected to reach $100 billion by 2030. Domestic sales are robust, supported by a growing number of ultra-high-net-worth individuals.
pages.title: International and domestic luxury spend continue to propel the market in Japan

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of a localised go-to-market strategy for fashion brands in Asia, highlighting the need to tailor product portfolios, supply chains, and marketing to local preferences. It also emphasizes the development of strong omnichannel propositions, leveraging both owned and third-party channels, with specific examples from China, India, and Japan.
pages.title: A go-to-market fashion strategy that accounts for local nuances is crucial to success in Asia

pages.abstract: Myntra, led by CEO Nandita Sinha, is a key player in India's fashion e-commerce market, targeting young, aspirational consumers. It leverages influencer content, premium offerings, and global sourcing to attract over 60 million monthly active users. The platform uses AI for styling services and collaborates with Bollywood celebrities, catering to Gen-Z trends and global fashion awareness.
pages.title: Myntra: An Online Gateway to India’s Fashion Market

pages.abstract: India's unique combination of sourcing and consumption capacity makes it an attractive market for international fashion brands. E-commerce platforms like Myntra play a crucial role, with traditional and western wear both growing. Luxury and bridge-to-luxury brands are finding a place, with accessories and watches leading the luxury market. Gen-Z customers drive growth in affordable, trend-forward merchandise.
pages.title: India's Attractive Growth for International Fashion Brands in 2025

pages.abstract: This page discusses the shopping behaviors of India's Gen-Z consumers, highlighting their increased purchase frequency and preference for digital and social media-driven shopping experiences. It also covers Myntra's strategies, including the use of influencers, short videos, and collaborations, to engage this demographic effectively.
pages.title: India’s Gen-Z Consumers and Shopping Trends

pages.abstract: India faces challenges in retail infrastructure and brand building, but technological innovations like AI-led product discovery and assistance tools are improving consumer engagement and business performance.
pages.title: India's Retail and Fashion Challenges and Opportunities

pages.abstract: This page introduces the concept of 'Discovery Reinvented,' featuring a woman actively searching on a laptop, symbolizing modern methods of information discovery and innovation in digital exploration.
pages.title: 03. Discovery Reinvented

pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges faced by fashion shoppers due to overwhelming choices and introduces AI-powered solutions for brand and product discovery. It highlights key insights from fashion executives and customer preferences, emphasizing the role of AI in enhancing engagement and conversion rates. Executive priorities include building AI foundations, prioritizing high-value use cases, and implementing guidelines for AI use.
pages.title: 03. Discovery Reinvented

pages.abstract: The page discusses how choice paralysis and search dissatisfaction negatively impact customer experience in online shopping. Retailers are addressing this by reducing product offerings and utilizing AI for better search results, though challenges remain.
pages.title: Choice paralysis is negatively impacting customer experience; brands are struggling to address it

pages.abstract: The page discusses the potential of generative AI in fashion, highlighting product discovery as the top use case. It covers growing customer demand for AI-powered shopping, increased competitiveness in AI quality and cost, greater accuracy of AI tools, and emerging commercial success stories.
pages.title: Reinventing product discovery will be a key focus area for fashion players in 2025

pages.abstract: This page discusses industry shifts expected in 2025, focusing on AI-driven personalization in fashion search and content. It highlights the transition from non-personalized to highly personalized experiences, emphasizing contextual searches, real-time recommendations, and integrated social commerce journeys.
pages.title: This new era will provide customers with increased curation across search and content

pages.abstract: The page discusses how emerging AI challengers are redefining product search in the fashion industry. It highlights AI-powered shopping platforms like Daydream, which has onboarded over 2,000 brands and retailers, and AI-powered discovery partners like Capsule, which achieved a 99% match rate of user images with shoppable links. It also mentions Constructor’s AI product search, which has seen a 20x increase in return on investment for some brands. The page emphasizes the use of natural language, image recognition, and machine learning to enhance the online shopping experience.
pages.title: Emerging AI challengers are redefining product search for the fashion industry

pages.abstract: Multi-brand retailers like Alibaba and Zalando are leveraging vast product data and AI technologies to enhance content curation. Alibaba's Wenwen chatbot improves click-through rates with personalized recommendations, while Zalando's AI assistant and generative AI tools enhance user experience and content relevance.
pages.title: Multi-brand retailers with vast product data are driving change in content curation

pages.abstract: Social media is transforming fashion discovery and purchase, with social commerce markets in the US and UK expected to double by 2027. Predictive algorithms, content tools, and integrated shopping journeys are key drivers, with TikTok and Pinterest leading the way through AI and shoppable content.
pages.title: Social media will continue to change the way shoppers discover and purchase fashion

pages.abstract: Fashion players should adopt a value-focused approach to AI-enabled discovery by building AI foundations, prioritising value and accuracy, and managing risks and ethics. This involves embedding AI literacy, establishing a technology backbone, identifying tech partners, and optimising product data. It also requires applying a prioritisation framework, employing a test-and-learn approach, and consistently monitoring AI models to ensure customer trust and authenticity.
pages.title: Fashion players should adopt a value-focused approach to AI-enabled discovery

pages.abstract: This page features an image of Jane Fonda on the L'Oréal Paris runway, highlighting the concept of 'Silver Spenders' and their influence in the fashion industry.
pages.title: 04. Silver Spenders

pages.abstract: The page discusses the growing importance of the 'Silver Generation' in fashion sales, highlighting their significant contribution to global spending and wealth. It advises brands to rethink marketing strategies, assess product appeal, and establish KPIs to engage this demographic effectively.
pages.title: 04. Silver Spenders

pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges fashion brands face in targeting younger generations, highlighting Gen-Z's financial pressures, brand exploration tendencies, and feeling overwhelmed by brand exposure. Despite these challenges, Gen-Z remains a key focus for fashion brands.
pages.title: It will be increasingly difficult for fashion brands to drive growth from younger generations alone

pages.abstract: The global population aged over 50 is growing faster than any other cohort due to longer life expectancies and declining birth rates. By 2050, this age group will represent more than a third of the global population. This trend is particularly strong in advanced economies like the US, China, and the EU5, where the share of the population aged over 50 will exceed 40% by 2050. Even in emerging markets like India, the older cohorts are expected to grow significantly.
pages.title: Meanwhile, there is a growing “Silver Generation” cohort of fashion customers

pages.abstract: The Silver Generation, with greater wealth and resilience, is driving significant global spending growth, particularly in fashion. Their higher disposable income and changing attitudes towards age stereotypes contribute to increased fashion expenditure compared to younger generations.
pages.title: The Silver Generation is disproportionately wealthier and spends more on fashion

pages.abstract: The Silver Generation prioritizes functionality, comfort, and value over trends and style. They are brand loyal, prefer timeless designs, and seek versatile products. Brands should focus on creating out-of-home experiences to capture their attention.
pages.title: Fashion brands need to address the needs of the Silver Generation in order to capture their spend

pages.abstract: The Silver Generation prefers multi-brand retail stores for fashion shopping, is less likely to embrace omnichannel shopping, and is less inclined towards resale and sustainability-focused brands. They are more likely to seek inspiration in physical stores and use social media for fashion discovery in China.
pages.title: Knowing where and how the Silver Generation discovers and shops for fashion is crucial

pages.abstract: This page discusses how brands like New Balance, J.Crew, and Uniqlo achieve inter-generational appeal through strategic branding, marketing, and product assortment. New Balance revives retro styles and collaborates with icons, J.Crew focuses on timeless designs and digital marketing, and Uniqlo emphasizes functional, high-quality pieces with technical features.
pages.title: Inter-generational appeal is achievable with branding, marketing and product assortment

pages.abstract: This page outlines executive priorities for brands targeting the Silver Generation, emphasizing the need to rethink customer segmentation, diversify product portfolios, and define data-driven channel strategies. It highlights the importance of leveraging data, offering innovative products, and adapting KPIs to ensure long-term ROI and customer loyalty.
pages.title: Brands that tailor their marketing, channel and product strategies will be positioned to win

pages.abstract: J.Crew, an American retailer, is projected to hit record sales in 2024 under CEO Libby Wadle's leadership. Wadle and her team reversed the brand's decline by balancing product strategy and adapting to post-pandemic consumer behavior, without losing its core customer base.
pages.title: J.Crew: How to Build an ‘Ageless’ Brand

pages.abstract: J.Crew's turnaround strategy focuses on creative leadership, design excellence, and customer experience. The brand aims to balance heritage with modernity, appealing to multi-generational customers while inspiring new ones. Key actions included bringing in new design leaders and relaunching the catalogue. The core customer is style-focused and ageless, and the brand strives for timeless, ageless products.
pages.title: J.Crew's Strategy and Customer Focus

pages.abstract: J.Crew maintains a balance in design through customer data and product insights, offering heritage items in modern iterations. They adapt their supply chain for creative processes, using Italian fabrics with long lead times, and establish a dynamic cycle to react to business and world trends while preserving product integrity.
pages.title: J.Crew Design and Supply Chain Strategy

pages.abstract: The document discusses the evolving role of distribution channels in reaching diverse customer segments, emphasizing the importance of store experiences and online convenience. It highlights the resurgence of catalogues as a storytelling tool and the significance of connecting with customers through meaningful brand experiences.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: This page introduces the concept of a value shift, likely related to the changing value of secondhand clothes. It features an image of a person browsing through a rack of various secondhand clothing items, highlighting the shift in consumer preferences towards sustainable and affordable fashion options.
pages.title: 05. Value Shift

pages.abstract: Macroeconomic pressures lead to cost-conscious shopping behaviors, with 64% of US shoppers trading down. Over 70% plan to buy from off-price retailers. Brands must emphasize value in communications and product strategy to capture customer wallets.
pages.title: 05. Value Shift

pages.abstract: Fashion customers are increasingly looking to spend less and smarter, driven by low consumer confidence and economic uncertainty. Over 60% of consumers in the US and UK are trying to save money on fashion, with varying strategies across income levels, including trading down and seeking better value.
pages.title: Fashion customers are looking to spend less and spend smarter

pages.abstract: The page discusses how value-oriented consumer behaviors are likely to persist even as economies improve, with shoppers planning to spend the same or less on fashion. It highlights the prioritization of experiences and travel over fashion and the stickiness of value-seeking behavior. The survey data shows various behaviors consumers would continue even with more money, emphasizing cost-saving strategies.
pages.title: Even as economies improve, value-orientated behaviours are likely to persist

pages.abstract: Off-price retailers, including TJX and Ross, are experiencing significant revenue growth and profitability improvements, outpacing the broader market. This trend is driven by consumer demand for value and affordability. Traditional off-price retailers and e-commerce brands are both benefiting from this dynamic, with Zalando's B2C channel and BestSecret showing notable growth.
pages.title: Affordability is propelling growth for off-price retailers and outlets

pages.abstract: The resale market is rapidly growing, driven by consumers seeking value in secondhand apparel. By 2025, it is expected to account for 10% of the global apparel market. Brands like Sandro and Shein are capitalizing on this trend by offering resale programs and platforms, enhancing customer loyalty and attracting new users.
pages.title: Consumer search for value is driving wins in the resale market

pages.abstract: The pursuit of affordable alternatives, known as 'dupe mania,' has gained popularity among Gen-Z and nearly one third of US adults. Brands like Shein, Lululemon, and Quince have capitalized on this trend by promoting dupes through influencers, hosting pop-ups, and offering high-quality replicas at affordable prices. The #dupe hashtag on TikTok has nearly 6 billion views, and UK shoppers frequently buy dupes for savings or as great alternatives.
pages.title: The pursuit of affordable alternatives has given rise to “dupe mania”

pages.abstract: Brands must identify customer value drivers, communicate value effectively through campaigns and channels, and integrate value into their channel and product strategies to attract and retain value-conscious shoppers while maintaining brand equity.
pages.title: Brands looking to differentiate will need to convince shoppers that they are worth the price

pages.abstract: Ralph Lauren has successfully pitched the idea of 'Ralph's World,' a preppy wonderland, to consumers at various price points. Despite higher prices, the brand remains popular, with busy stores and rising stock prices. However, it now faces challenges due to global economic factors, and is focusing on storytelling and core products for longevity.
pages.title: Ralph Lauren: Selling a Dream at Every Price

pages.abstract: The document discusses the strategy of brand elevation through storytelling, product quality, and shopping experience, aiming to connect with diverse consumer groups from the ultra-rich to aspirational buyers. It emphasizes the importance of value, timeless style, and a unique brand experience across all touchpoints.
pages.title: Value Shift

pages.abstract: The document discusses the evolution of stores and consumer engagement strategies, emphasizing brand-cultural moments, direct-to-consumer focus, and the integration of technology and lifestyle experiences in retail.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: This page discusses Ralph Lauren's strategy in China's luxury market, emphasizing core products, brand recognition, and long-term growth potential. It highlights the company's focus on iconic items, consumer trust, and strategic category expansion, while addressing market challenges and opportunities.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts in China's Luxury Market

pages.abstract: This page highlights the human side of sales, focusing on the interaction between a sales assistant and a customer in a clothing store. It emphasizes the personal and relational aspects of sales, showcasing a collaborative moment where the assistant assists the customer in selecting an item.
pages.title: 06. The Human Side of Sales

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of enhancing the in-store experience through empowering store associates, highlighting key insights and executive priorities for improving customer and employee satisfaction.
pages.title: 06. The Human Side of Sales

pages.abstract: The page discusses the importance of maximizing customer engagement in stores as in-store sales growth slows in 2025. It highlights the need for high-quality service and staff engagement to prevent missed sales and emphasizes the evolving role of stores in the digital age.
pages.title: It will be imperative to maximise customer engagement amid slowing in-store sales in 2025

pages.abstract: Store associates significantly influence shopper satisfaction and loyalty. Human interactions, like styling advice and assistance, are key differentiators, boosting conversion and delight. Non-human elements, such as store atmosphere and checkout efficiency, are essential but do not differentiate experiences. Younger and aspirational shoppers value human interactions more.
pages.title: Store associates are crucial in differentiating the store experience

pages.abstract: This page highlights the critical challenges of human capital in the retail sector, emphasizing the high turnover rate, rising costs, and customer dissatisfaction due to poorly trained staff. It discusses the labor shortage, wage growth, and the financial impact of losing employees, urging retailers to address these issues to retain associates and improve store experiences.
pages.title: Solving human capital challenges is essential to retaining associates in today’s labour market

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of upskilling store staff and investing in tech support tools to enhance customer interactions. It highlights the need for efficient training methods like AI-powered learning and micro-learning. The page also emphasizes the role of digital tools in facilitating omnichannel sales and improving customer engagement through CRM technologies. Case studies from Reiss, Aritzia, Kering, and Target illustrate successful implementations of these strategies.
pages.title: Upskilling staff and investing in tech support tools will enable better customer interactions

pages.abstract: Employee incentives should focus on customer lifetime value and modern shopping habits. Examples include Frasers Group's employee festivals and awards, Dior's performance-based points for tailored experiences, and Nordstrom's Style Board emails for digital sales commissions. These incentives enhance employee satisfaction and align with meaningful work aspects.
pages.title: Employee incentives should reward customer lifetime value and reflect modern shopping habits

pages.abstract: Retailers are adopting data-driven staff deployment and leveraging technology like RFID to streamline manual tasks, enhancing customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. Examples include Aritzia's data-informed scheduling, Faherty's gig staffing, BJ’s Wholesale's automated inventory tasks, and Uniqlo's RFID self-checkout.
pages.title: Store staff should be freed up to focus on customer-satisfaction drivers

pages.abstract: Retailers should prioritize career development and compensation to improve employee retention. Employees value career growth, inspiring leadership, and meaningful work. High employee satisfaction leads to better customer experience and reduced turnover costs.
pages.title: To improve employee experience, retailers should prioritise development and human interactions

pages.abstract: This page outlines executive priorities for retailers to develop an end-to-end employee value proposition, including enabling staff with training and tools, motivating store associates with broader incentive structures, optimising processes for high-value activities, and retaining employees through coaching and one-to-one interactions.
pages.title: It will be crucial for retailers to develop an end-to-end employee value proposition

pages.abstract: Aritzia, a Canadian retailer, experienced hypergrowth post-pandemic due to its minimalist wardrobe staples and CEO Jennifer Wong's strategic retail and employee development programs. With 124 locations, Aritzia emphasizes customer service, premium real estate, and a tight product strategy.
pages.title: Aritzia: Redefining Shopping One Store at a Time

pages.abstract: This page discusses Aritzia's retail strategy, emphasizing personalized customer service, store format evolution, and the importance of location and in-store experience. It highlights the role of style advisors in building relationships and the impact of visual merchandising on customer engagement.
pages.title: What's the role of retail at Aritzia?

pages.abstract: The page discusses the sales associate recruitment and retention process at Aritzia, highlighting the opportunities for growth, the rewarding work environment, and the company's commitment to promoting from within.
pages.title: The Human Side of Sales

pages.abstract: The page discusses Aritzia's employee retention strategies during Covid-19, retail expansion plans in the US, and the factors contributing to its growth, including product innovation, store experience, technology, and infrastructure investment.
pages.title: The Human Side of Sales

pages.abstract: This page illustrates the disruption in marketplaces, specifically focusing on the shift towards mobile shopping. A woman is depicted browsing and purchasing clothes through a mobile app, highlighting the convenience and accessibility of online marketplaces.
pages.title: 07. Marketplaces Disrupted

pages.abstract: Non-luxury marketplaces face significant challenges post-Covid-19, with share prices plummeting. Europe's online fashion marketplaces suffered substantial economic losses. Despite Amazon's resilience in the US value segment, department stores and fashion pure-players are adapting. China's social commerce and low-cost players are thriving. Executive priorities include enhancing assortment, customer lifetime value, profitability, tech modernisation, and cost efficiency.
pages.title: 07. Marketplaces Disrupted

pages.abstract: Online fashion marketplaces face challenges due to increased customer acquisition costs, high return rates, and production complexity. Consumers demand flexible experiences and tech upgrades, impacting growth expectations and requiring strategic investments.
pages.title: Online fashion marketplaces are facing existential business model challenges and disruptions

pages.abstract: The first wave of online marketplaces experienced a surge in stock prices due to inflated valuations during the Covid-19 pandemic but have since faced sharp declines. Specialised fashion players are particularly vulnerable, while diversified companies like Zalando have managed better. Investors now prioritize profitability over sales growth, impacting unprofitable businesses like Asos and Boohoo.
pages.title: The “first wave” of online marketplace players have struggled to sustain share price growth

pages.abstract: European online fashion marketplaces face challenges from low-cost competitors and traditional retailers. McKinsey data shows significant value destruction in 2023. To adapt, marketplaces are focusing on profitable orders, exploring new value pools, building scale, and leveraging generative AI. These strategies aim to enhance profitability and competitive positioning in the evolving fashion landscape.
pages.title: In Europe, online fashion marketplaces will need to evolve their business models

pages.abstract: Amazon Fashion dominates the US online fashion market with over 40% of total revenue in 2023, while Shein and Temu face challenges. Mid-market and premium segments remain fragmented, with department stores and fashion pure-players expanding their reach.
pages.title: Amazon Fashion leads the US value segment; the mid and premium segments remain fragmented

pages.abstract: The page discusses the importance of social and live commerce in China's online fashion market, highlighting the competition between traditional platforms and social platforms. It emphasizes the need for brands to manage profitability with livestreamers and balance branded and value items. The growth of monthly active users for major platforms is also presented.
pages.title: In China, managing social commerce profitability and the blend of branded vs value products is key

pages.abstract: This page outlines five key actions for first-wave marketplaces to ensure longevity: making assortment competitive, maximising customer lifetime value, creating new profitability avenues, modernising tech and talent, and leveraging AI for cost reduction. Each action includes specific strategies to enhance competitiveness, customer engagement, and operational efficiency.
pages.title: Five actions will support the longevity of first-wave marketplaces

pages.abstract: Mytheresa, under CEO Michael Klider, has become a leader in online luxury retail by focusing on top-spending customers and innovating. Despite a sector-wide slowdown, the company remains profitable and is acquiring Yoox-Net-a-Porter to strengthen its position. Klider anticipates a slow but steady recovery in 2025 and emphasizes the importance of customer loyalty and strategic expansion.
pages.title: Mytheresa: Staying Ahead in Luxury E-Commerce

pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges faced by luxury e-commerce, particularly in China, and the expectation of continued stabilization in the sector. It highlights the importance of economic growth, women's participation in the workforce, and regulatory permits for emerging growth opportunities. It also emphasizes the need to understand customer desires and redefine luxury in the digital age.
pages.title: Luxury E-commerce and Market Opportunities

pages.abstract: Mytheresa employs a mix of in-person events, digital marketing, and strategic advertising to acquire and retain high-value customers. They focus on building customer loyalty through personalized experiences and product recommendations, emphasizing the importance of customer satisfaction in driving repeat business.
pages.title: Mytheresa's Customer Acquisition Strategies

pages.abstract: The document discusses strategies for luxury e-tailers like Mytheresa to maintain dominance in a competitive market. It emphasizes the importance of operational excellence, full-price selling, excellent customer service, and strategic marketing to ensure profitability and customer loyalty. The text also addresses the challenges of managing costs and maintaining brand partnerships in an evolving retail landscape.
pages.title: Fashion System: Staying Ahead in Luxury E-commerce

pages.abstract: This page showcases a tennis player in a sportswear showdown, highlighting the player's attire and action during a match. The sportswear includes a white headband, a white long-sleeve shirt under a white short-sleeve shirt, and a white short. The player is captured mid-swing, hitting a tennis ball with a racket against a green background.
pages.title: 08. Sportswear Showdown

pages.abstract: The sportswear market is witnessing a significant shift with challenger brands expected to dominate economic profits by 2024. Key insights highlight the rapid growth of sportswear compared to the broader fashion market, with specific regional data. Executive priorities emphasize innovation, marketing, partnerships, and strategic distribution to enhance brand presence and profitability.
pages.title: 08. Sportswear Showdown

pages.abstract: Challenger sportswear brands are projected to surpass incumbent brands in economic profit by 2024, driven by faster revenue growth and improved profitability. This trend is supported by data showing challengers' increasing market share and economic profit compared to incumbents from 2018 to 2024.
pages.title: Challenger brands will generate the majority of economic profit in sportswear in 2024

pages.abstract: Challenger brands have successfully expanded market share by delivering visible innovations, targeting specialised categories, tapping into cultural marketing, and filling wholesale whitespace. They have reimagined running footwear, tailored offerings for niche sports, leveraged celebrity culture, and capitalised on the shift in distribution channels.
pages.title: Challenger brands have aggressively taken market share by targeting niches and expanding reach

pages.abstract: Sportswear is projected to grow faster than the overall fashion market in 2025, driven by health and wellness trends, increased sports content access, and generational shifts. Key regions like China, the US, and Europe will see significant growth, with China leading at 5-6 percentage points. The global sports tourism sector is also expected to grow by 18% by 2030.
pages.title: In 2025, sportswear is expected to continue to grow faster than fashion overall

pages.abstract: The document discusses the competitive landscape in the sportswear market, highlighting significant stock performance gains by challengers like Asics, On, and Deckers. Incumbents, except for Adidas, have faced challenges. The need for incumbents to innovate in product, marketing, and channel strategies is emphasized.
pages.title: The battle to capture share of this market growth will intensify in 2025

pages.abstract: Brands diversify their offerings to balance customer reach and cultural credibility. Performance and athleisure brands expand into new categories, while material and product innovations are crucial for building credibility. Fewer breakthrough innovations have emerged, but Nike leads in patents. The global fanbase for racket sports has grown significantly.
pages.title: To win share, brands will diversify their offerings, balancing reach and cultural credibility

pages.abstract: The sports sponsorship market is growing, with athletes partnering with smaller brands for more control. Brands are focusing on credible spokespeople and incorporating cultural elements into marketing. Examples include Zendaya with On, Rosé with Puma, and Adidas' local initiatives in China.
pages.title: Players are expected to create authentic messaging amplified by ambassadors

pages.abstract: Sportswear brands are balancing DTC and wholesale strategies. DTC focuses on customer experience and community building, while wholesale aims to increase reach and brand presence. Retailers are expanding stores and diversifying brand offerings to attract more customers.
pages.title: Sportswear brands must strike the right balance between DTC and wholesale customer touchpoints

pages.abstract: Brands should focus on product innovation, effective marketing strategies, and authentic partnerships to gain market share. They should invest in breakthrough innovations, diversify product offerings, and reintroduce styles. Marketing should convey innovation benefits clearly and target credible channels. Partnerships should be built with emerging athletes, celebrities, and local communities. A distribution strategy with distinct channel roles is crucial for customer engagement and profitability.
pages.title: Brands should prioritise product, marketing and distribution to gain share

pages.abstract: New Balance, aiming for $10 billion in sales, discusses its unique brand and athlete partnership strategies, focusing on innovation and maintaining strong relationships with partners to stay ahead in the sneaker market.
pages.title: New Balance: Disrupting the Sneaker Industry

pages.abstract: New Balance emphasizes controlling its destiny by staying close to consumers, understanding shopping trends, and delivering products at the intersection of sport and fashion. As a private company, it focuses on long-term strategies, domestic manufacturing for quality control, and innovation through investments in manufacturing and product innovation centers. It leverages its archive for authentic retro designs, ensuring innovation and performance.
pages.title: New Balance's Strategy and Innovation

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of authenticity in brand DNA, the competitive sneaker market, and the strategic balance between product quantity and sales maximization. It highlights the role of analytical teams and market understanding in managing the dynamic retail landscape.
pages.title: 08. Sportswear Showdown

pages.abstract: New Balance discusses its strategy of balancing direct-to-consumer sales with wholesale partnerships, emphasizing shared values and bespoke approaches in collaborations. The brand aims to be a premium sports brand by aligning with partners who share its vision.
pages.title: New Balance's Retail and Wholesale Strategy

pages.abstract: The page illustrates inventory excellence through a woman working in a warehouse, emphasizing the importance of efficient inventory management and handling.
pages.title: 09.Inventory Excellence

pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges of inventory management in the fashion industry, emphasizing the need for end-to-end planning excellence, tech adoption, and agile supply chains. It highlights key insights on excess stock and discount trends and outlines executive priorities for breaking down silos, incentivizing inventory excellence, and leveraging technology.
pages.title: 09. Inventory Excellence

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces unique inventory challenges due to rapid trend cycles, unpredictable seasonality, lengthy supply chains, and product/channel complexity, making it increasingly difficult for brands to manage seasonal stock and meet consumer demands.
pages.title: Getting the fashion “inventory equation” right has become increasingly challenging

pages.abstract: Fashion brands face significant challenges with excess stock and stock-outs, leading to financial losses and missed revenue opportunities. In 2023, the industry produced 2.5-5 billion excess garments, with excess stock valued between $70 billion and $140 billion. In 2024, despite stable inventory levels, many brands struggled with inventory management. Luxury brands saw inventory increases, and major companies like LVMH and Kering reported substantial excess inventory. Brands resorted to discounting, affecting profitability. Stock-outs due to inaccurate purchasing and forecasting resulted in up to 20% monthly profit loss.
pages.title: As a result, fashion brands continue to struggle with both excess stock and stock-outs

pages.abstract: Brands are prioritising profitability by optimising inventories due to flat sales and increased markdowns. Sustainability regulations, such as the EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products and California's Extended Producer Responsibility, are adding pressure to reduce over-production and waste. Managing inventory effectively can help brands achieve sustainability targets and maintain profitability.
pages.title: Managing inventory is key for brands to achieve profitability and address new regulation

pages.abstract: Fashion brands are adopting proactive tactics like data-driven planning, dynamic open-to-buy adjustments, and network optimisation using tech tools to improve inventory management. These strategies aim to reduce inventory levels, enhance forecasting accuracy, and control stock risk, with significant investments in digital intelligence expected by 2025.
pages.title: Fashion brands need to adopt proactive tactics to inventory management using tech-enabled tools

pages.abstract: This page discusses the need for end-to-end collaboration across the value chain to achieve sustained impact in inventory management. It highlights the inefficiencies of isolated solutions and emphasizes the importance of breaking down silos, setting up cross-functional teams, establishing clear review cadences, aligning incentive structures, and connecting systems for better inventory performance.
pages.title: Achieving sustained impact will require end-to-end collaboration across the value chain

pages.abstract: This page outlines executive priorities for brands to adapt to change through an updated operating model and mindset shift. It emphasizes embedding collaborative processes, widening accountability for inventory levels, and leveraging technology-enabled tools for better decision-making and data transparency.
pages.title: Brands must reflect this change through an updated operating model and a mindset shift

pages.abstract: This page introduces 'The Sustainability Collective,' featuring an image of wind turbines, symbolizing sustainable energy solutions and collective efforts towards environmental conservation.
pages.title: 10. The Sustainability Collective

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces significant sustainability challenges, with many brands lagging on decarbonisation goals and low prioritisation of sustainability risks. Collective action is essential to address these issues, focusing on dual mission commitments, supplier consolidation, and data-driven traceability.
pages.title: 10. The Sustainability Collective

pages.abstract: The page discusses barriers to sustainability in the fashion industry, including high investment costs, fragmented supply chains, and consumer behavior inconsistencies. It highlights the economic and operational challenges, the complexity of supplier and brand fragmentation, and the disconnect between consumer actions and values regarding sustainable fashion.
pages.title: Complexity, fragmentation and consumer sentiment are barriers to sustainability targets

pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges faced by brands, suppliers, and innovators in the fashion industry regarding sustainability. Many brands are scaling back their sustainability commitments, and suppliers are struggling to meet science-based targets due to feasibility and costs. Sustainable innovations face difficulties in scaling due to financing and volume requirements. The graph illustrates the yearly reduction in scope-three emission intensity across fashion brands, showing that many brands need to accelerate their efforts to meet 2030 targets.
pages.title: As a result, brands, suppliers and innovators are struggling to make progress

pages.abstract: The fashion industry must act swiftly to address rising apparel consumption and carbon emissions. Brands can achieve cost-effective decarbonisation through sustainability levers, supplier collaboration, and material innovation, reducing waste and overproduction while sharing costs and risks.
pages.title: Inaction is not an option. The fashion industry can focus on cost-effective decarbonisation

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of long-term brand-supplier collaboration in reducing industry emissions, highlighting key strategies for brands to consolidate supplier relationships, embrace long-term commitments, and address industry bottlenecks. It also presents case studies of H&M Group, Bestseller, CIP, the Future Supplier Initiative, and PVH Corp. in their efforts to promote sustainability through renewable energy projects and financing initiatives.
pages.title: Long-term brand-supplier collaboration is an integral part of reducing industry emissions

pages.abstract: Brands can foster sustainable-material innovation by making bold investments, de-risking commercial prospects, and building in-house expertise. Examples include H&M's partnership with Syre for polyester recycling and Inditex's collaboration with Ambercycle for next-gen materials.
pages.title: Brands can create favourable conditions for sustainable-material innovators to scale

pages.abstract: Brands can reignite progress by focusing on sustainability initiatives, rethinking supplier contracts, and getting granular on data. This involves adopting a dual mission, shifting to a collective model, committing to commercialisation, embedding new supplier sourcing processes, ensuring decarbonisation adherence, consolidating suppliers, partnering with traceability providers, and mapping the entire value chain.
pages.title: Brands can reignite progress if they focus on working with the broader fashion ecosystem
McKinsey Global Fashion Index

pages.abstract: The fashion industry's economic profit is reaching record levels, but market dynamics are shifting. Luxury players are losing ground to non-luxury brands, with the gap between top and bottom performers at its smallest since 2011. Key insights include a 16% growth in economic profit from 2022 to 2023, with expectations of record-high levels in 2024. However, the luxury segment faces margin pressure, while non-luxury brands, especially sportswear and mall brands, show strong profitability. The top 20% of players are expected to lose value, while the bottom 20% gain, closing the performance gap.
pages.title: McKinsey Global Fashion Index

pages.abstract: The fashion industry is projected to achieve record economic profit in 2024, driven by margin improvements and revenue growth. The McKinsey Global Fashion Index (MGFI) tracks financial growth and value creation through economic profit (EP), which is expected to stabilize at 2.8x pre-Covid levels. The industry's focus on profitability has led to significant margin gains, resulting in disproportionate value creation.
pages.title: The industry is expected to post record economic profit in 2024

pages.abstract: The fashion industry has seen record-high economic profit (EP) but investor uncertainty about future value creation has led to lower valuations. Companies need compelling strategies and narratives for sustainable growth. Luxury valuations are slightly higher in 2024 compared to 2022, while non-luxury valuations continue to decline.
pages.title: However, record-high EP is not enough to allay investor uncertainty which drives lower valuations

pages.abstract: The non-luxury segment is driving value creation in the fashion industry, with a significant shift from luxury. This trend is expected to continue, with non-luxury contributing more to economic profit than luxury in the coming years.
pages.title: The non-luxury segment is expected to buoy EP, marking a shift in industry dynamics

pages.abstract: The document discusses how consumer downtrading is impacting the luxury and non-luxury fashion markets. Luxury brands face challenges due to pricing and demand, while non-luxury brands, especially in the mid-market, are expected to see improved profitability. The data shows economic profit trends across different market segments from 2021 to 2024, highlighting shifts in consumer behavior and market performance.
pages.title: Consumer downtrading is driving non-luxury, while pricing and demand is challenging luxury

pages.abstract: The document discusses the impact of cost cuts and operational improvements on EBITA margins across different fashion segments. Luxury margins are expected to decline, while non-luxury segments, including premium/bridge and mid-market, have seen record-high margins. Specific examples include Inditex's inventory reduction, Levi Strauss & Co.'s cost savings, and Zalando's margin growth. The affordable luxury and value/discount segments are expected to see margin growth but remain below historical peaks.
pages.title: Cost cuts and operational gains have raised non-luxury margins, while luxury margins declined

pages.abstract: In 2024, the luxury segment faces challenges with 77% of companies expecting negative EP growth due to plateauing revenues and reduced margins. The remaining 23% anticipate modest positive EP growth driven by revenue increases, though overall EP growth remains limited.
pages.title: 23 percent of luxury players expect to generate more EP in 2024, driven by revenue gains

pages.abstract: In 2024, non-luxury segments will focus on profitability, leading to more evenly distributed value creation. Super Winners like Inditex and Fast Retailing will continue driving EP growth, while Mall Brands and Sportswear challengers improve performance. Pure online marketplaces face disruptions but show early signs of improvement.
pages.title: In non-luxury, value creation will be more evenly distributed across the segment

pages.abstract: Mall brands are undergoing transformations to boost profitability and investor confidence. Gap is enhancing its image, American Eagle Outfitters is regaining momentum with operational improvements, and Abercrombie & Fitch is targeting a broader audience. These efforts are expected to drive economic profit growth in the non-luxury segment.
pages.title: Mall brand turnarounds are expected to be one of the EP growth drivers in the non-luxury segment

pages.abstract: The gap between top and bottom performers in the fashion industry is narrowing, with bottom performers improving and top performers, particularly in luxury, declining. The top 20% of companies' contribution to economic profit is expected to decrease by 13 percentage points from 2022 to 2024, while the bottom 20% is expected to increase by 13 points.
pages.title: The gap between top- and bottom-performing brands is the smallest it has been since 2011
