pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_1.jpg
pages.title: Braced for shifting weather

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_2.jpg
pages.abstract: The report discusses the mixed conditions of global private markets in 2024, highlighting tepid dealmaking, low fundraising levels, and increased capital deployment. It also addresses challenges like geopolitical instability and technological advancements, emphasizing the resilience of stakeholders and shifts in fundraising, dealmaking, and LP strategies. The report analyzes asset class performance and pressing issues across private markets.
pages.title: Welcome to McKinsey’s Global Private Markets Report 2025

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_3.jpg
pages.title: Contents

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_4.jpg
pages.title: Asset classes in review

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the evolving landscape of private equity in 2024, highlighting the clarity emerging despite global uncertainties. It emphasizes a resurgence in dealmaking and distributions, signaling a positive outlook for the sector.
pages.title: Private equity emerging from the fog

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the nuanced picture of private equity in 2024, highlighting the resurgence in distributions, dealmaking, and exit activity despite challenges. It also notes the improvement in financing conditions and the resilience of the asset class, with plans for increased PE allocations.
pages.title: Private Equity in 2024: A Nuanced Picture

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: GPs are innovating by unlocking alternative capital sources, creating new fund structures, and expanding deal structures. Scale provides advantages, but challenges remain in fundraising, performance, and exits. The PE industry must address uncertainties and geopolitical risks.
pages.title: GPs' Evolving Strategies in PE

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: This page analyzes key metrics across private equity asset classes, focusing on interest rates, inflation, deal values, exit values, and fundraising trends from 2019 to 2024. It highlights the impact of macroeconomic factors on the private equity industry and provides insights into dealmaking, fundraising, and LP target allocations.
pages.title: The heat map shows key metrics across private equity asset classes.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: The document highlights the significant rebound in global private equity dealmaking in 2024, with a 14% increase to $2 trillion. It details regional trends and subasset class performance, noting a decline in Asia. The provided exhibits illustrate the deal value and count by region over time.
pages.title: Dealmakers: Bouncing back, especially at the top

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: Asia experienced a decline in private equity assets under management, fundraising, and performance, contrasting with growth in North America and Europe. The decline was driven by reduced fundraising and poor performance, affecting net asset value and dry powder levels.
pages.title: Asia's private equity slowdown

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the decline in PE deals across subasset classes due to reduced venture capital activity. It highlights a 16.9% year-over-year drop in deal count and a marginal 1.7% decrease in global buyout deals. However, larger deals in North America showed year-over-year growth. The bar chart illustrates the distribution of buyout deals by size in North America from 2009 to 2024, showing an increase in deals larger than $500 million as a share of total deal value in 2024.
pages.title: Buyout deal count as a share of total deal count and buyout deals larger than $500 million as a share of deal value increased in 2024.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: Venture capital fundraising and deal activity declined significantly in 2023 and 2024, with Asia experiencing notable challenges. Despite some marginal improvements in performance, buyout strategies outperformed venture capital. The decline in private equity assets under management was led by venture capital in 2024.
pages.title: Venture capital's continued crunch

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the increased confidence in buyout deals, highlighting the median global buyout entry multiple in 2024 as the second highest on record. It shows a rebound in deal value following a decrease in 2023, with EBITDA multiples reverting to 2021-22 levels. The increase in multiples is attributed to both improved valuations and changes in the quality mix of businesses.
pages.title: Median global buyout entry multiple in 2024 was the second highest on record, rebounding alongside deal value following a 2023 decrease.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the easing of PE financing costs and increased leverage in 2024, while noting that buyout leverage remains below historical averages. It highlights the decrease in global PE dry powder and the reduction in dry powder inventory, indicating a drawdown on committed capital.
pages.title: Global inventories of private equity dry powder decreased in 2024.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses global trends in dealmaking, highlighting the resurgence of large buyout transactions over $500 million in North America and Europe. It also notes the evolving preferences of PE investors, with technology outperforming and healthcare retreating post-COVID-19. The exhibit illustrates the increase in deal value and count for buyouts over $500 million across different regions.
pages.title: The rebound in private equity dealmaking was led by an increase in buyout transactions over $500 million.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: The chart illustrates the global private equity deal values across various sectors from 2015 to 2024, highlighting the significant recovery driven by technology, consumer, and financial services sectors. The data shows substantial growth in deal values, particularly in financial services and technology, with notable compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) for deals over $500 million.
pages.title: Technology, consumer, and financial-services sectors drove the recovery in large private equity deals.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the increasing attractiveness of public companies for private equity (PE) deals, particularly in Europe. It highlights the growth in P2P transactions, their challenges, and their growing share in global PE deals. The page also covers improvements in exit values and the growing backlog of assets in divestment periods, emphasizing the need for longer value creation horizons and thoughtful exit strategies.
pages.title: Public companies are becoming more attractive

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges of IPOs as an exit option for private equity-backed companies, highlighting the decline in IPOs and the increasing importance of sponsor-to-sponsor transactions. It also notes the need for sponsors to find long-term corporate acquirers for larger assets.
pages.title: IPOs remain tough

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the decline in private equity fundraising for the third consecutive year in 2024, with a 24% decrease to $589 billion. It highlights regional declines, with Europe experiencing a smaller drop compared to North America and Asia. The document also notes the decline in fundraising for buyout, growth equity, and venture capital, contrasting with the previous year's performance.
pages.title: Fundraisers: Enduring pressure, but the outlook is bright

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: The document highlights a significant decline in global private equity fundraising across buyout, venture, and growth categories, with a 24% drop in 2024 following a 12% decrease in 2023. The data shows a consistent downward trend in fundraising across various subasset classes. Additionally, it notes that funds are taking longer to close, with a record-high duration of 21.9 months in 2024, and the number of closed PE funds has reached a decade-low.
pages.title: Buyout, venture, and growth fundraising fell 24 percent in 2024 after a 12 percent drop in 2023.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: Midmarket funds, ranging from $1 billion to $5 billion, showed resilience in fundraising during a down year. The top 25 private equity fundraisers captured a smaller share in 2024 compared to 2023. Smaller funds faced challenges, with those under $1 billion in market for longer periods and first-time funds raising the lowest total since 2013.
pages.title: Midmarket fundraising appears more resilient

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: The page presents data on global private equity fundraising trends, showing that midmarket funds between $1 billion and $5 billion have resisted the overall decline. It includes a bar chart detailing fundraising by fund size and close year, and a line graph showing the global fund count. The data highlights the performance of different fund sizes from 2007 to 2024, with midmarket funds showing slight growth in 2023–24.
pages.title: Midmarket funds between $1 billion and $5 billion bucked the overall trend of decline in private equity fundraising.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: LPs have increased their target allocation to private equity despite fundraising challenges. Despite being overallocated, more LPs plan to increase allocations, showing long-term confidence. Factors like lumpy distributions, competition for funds, and multiyear commitments complicate fundraising.
pages.title: Traditional fundraising is getting harder, even as LPs are increasing allocations

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: Limited partners are increasing their private equity allocations due to higher relative performance. The top reasons include better risk-adjusted returns, expected increases in return rates, and portfolio diversity. While distributions exceeded capital calls in 2024, PE returns declined across subasset classes, with buyouts performing the strongest.
pages.title: Limited partners are increasing their private equity allocations, driven by its higher relative performance compared with other asset classes.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: The document highlights that private equity distributions surpassed contributions in the first half of 2024 for the first time since 2015. It includes a bar chart showing global private equity capital called and distributions from 2010 to H1 2024, with a ratio of distributions to capital called. Additionally, a line chart illustrates the percentage of capital called in excess of distributions. The data includes buyout, growth, venture capital, and other private equity types, sourced from Preqin and McKinsey analysis.
pages.title: Private equity distributions exceeded contributions in the first half of 2024 for the first time since 2015.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: In 2024, private equity returns declined to 3.8%, with public markets outperforming private equity for the third time in four years. The S&P 500 outperformed all private equity subasset classes, excluding the Magnificent Seven. However, over longer periods, buyout subasset classes have historically outperformed public equities, explaining LPs' continued support. Buyout multiples remained lower than public multiples, reflecting the illiquidity penalty.
pages.title: Private equity returns declined to roughly 3.8 percent in 2024.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: Private equity investments have consistently outperformed public equity investments over various time horizons since the year 2000. The gap between global buyout multiples and public equity multiples widened in 2024, indicating a growing disparity in valuation metrics.
pages.title: Private equity investment has outperformed public equity investment since the turn of the millennium.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the maturing industry structure and the rise of an ecosystem delivering solutions for LPs. It highlights two key trends: LPs becoming part of the liquidity solution through secondary markets and their growing interest in directly investing in GPs, reflecting their belief in the long-term value of GPs and the private equity industry.
pages.title: Trends in LPs' Liquidity Solutions and Investment Strategies

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the imperative for PE operators to focus on value creation due to increasing purchase prices and holding periods. It highlights that leverage and multiple expansion have driven 61% of returns, while revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion contributed 39%. The expansion in leverage and multiples has led managers to focus on operational improvements to maintain returns, with scrutiny on operators' ability to increase revenue and margins.
pages.title: Operators: The value creation imperative endures

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses four trends in private equity value creation, emphasizing the increasing involvement of investors through portfolio operations teams and the acceleration of add-on M&A deals. It highlights that nonplatform deals accounted for 40% of buyout deal value in 2024, indicating a shift in investment strategies.
pages.title: We see four trends shaping how operators are creating value within their portfolios.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_31.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of organic cash generation in managing leverage and highlights how portfolio companies are preparing for exits by investing in growth and operational improvements. It also draws an analogy between navigating through fog and the challenges faced by the private equity industry, emphasizing resilience and innovation.
pages.title: Organic cash generation is key to managing leverage

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_32.jpg
pages.title: Real estate reaches for daylight

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: The real estate industry experienced mixed recovery in 2024, with global deal value rising but fundraising declining. Asset values stabilized as investors reassessed risks. Fundraising issues persisted, with closed-end fundraising at its lowest since 2012. Returns for closed-end funds remained negative, while alternative sectors like data centers showed robust returns. GPs with operational expertise gained market share, and capital allocators focused on analytics and service delivery.
pages.title: Real Estate Industry Recovery in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: In 2024, global real estate deal value experienced growth for the first time since 2021, with notable increases in multifamily and industrial sectors. Asia-Pacific led with a 14% growth in transaction value, followed by the Americas and EMEA regions. The bar chart illustrates the global real estate deal value from 2007 to 2024, showing a significant rebound in 2024.
pages.title: Dealmakers: Capitalizing on renewed growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the partial recovery in global real estate deal values, driven by factors like increased issuance of commercial mortgage-backed securities and reduced borrowing costs. It highlights regional variations, supply constraints, and cap rate compressions, while noting challenges such as declining NAVs in open-end funds.
pages.title: The partial recovery in global deal value was driven by a few factors, including an increase in the issuance of commercial mortgage-backed securities and reduction in borrowing costs.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the moderation in rent growth across traditional sectors, highlighting the strong performance of data centers in 2024 due to tenant demand and constrained supply. It also explores value creation through operational capabilities and capital allocation in commercial real estate.
pages.title: Surging demand for data centers

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the exponential growth in data center demand due to digital and cloud revolutions, highlighting challenges like power shortages and the need for strategic partnerships. It emphasizes the importance of operational capabilities for investors to create value and achieve competitive differentiation.
pages.title: The race to build data centers

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how sophisticated capital allocators can leverage data and technology to enhance operational expertise in property management, leading to competitive advantages. It also highlights the looming maturity of commercial real estate loans and the opportunities and challenges this presents for investors and debt fund managers.
pages.title: Investors with operational capabilities can create value through improved end-user experiences, access to and use of data, and efficient delivery models, all underpinned by strong risk management.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the decline in global closed-end real estate fundraising, highlighting a 28% drop to $104 billion. It analyzes fundraising trends across different regions and strategies, noting significant decreases in opportunistic fundraising and the impact of large fund closures on overall statistics.
pages.title: Fundraisers: Navigating uncertain terrain

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_40.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the rising interest in real estate debt despite a decline in dedicated fundraising. It highlights the appeal of credit strategies, the role of alternative financing structures, and the structural complexities faced by LPs. Market dynamics and organizational factors also influence the pace of fund formation.
pages.title: Rising interest in real estate debt

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_41.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the pressures faced by open-end core funds in the US, highlighting the marginal improvement in net investor cash flows in 2024 despite remaining significantly negative. It explains the shift in investor sentiment and the rotation of capital into other real estate strategies, emphasizing the preference for capital appreciation over income generation.
pages.title: Open-end funds continue to face pressures

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_42.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the evolving fundraising strategies of GPs in real estate, expanding beyond traditional channels to include high-net-worth investors and insurance capital. It highlights the diversification of LP bases, unlocking new scales, and extending fundraising runways. The text also addresses LPs' repositioning in a shifting market, noting mixed real estate returns in 2024 and the performance of various indices and funds.
pages.title: Although investor sentiment remains cautious, confidence in real estate investing is beginning to improve.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: Alternative sectors, including data centers, manufactured housing, and senior housing, have outperformed traditional sectors in total returns for nine of the past ten years. These sectors offer compelling opportunities due to their operational complexity and specialized capabilities required. Despite historical underrepresentation in institutional portfolios, they are gaining traction among industry players.
pages.title: Alternative sectors are getting more mainstream

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_44.jpg
pages.abstract: LPs are shifting towards strategic capital deployment, favoring thematic investments in decarbonization, digital infrastructure, and demographic shifts. They prefer managers with integrated platforms and expect GPs to co-invest. Despite headwinds in commercial real estate, deal activity and alternative sectors show resilience and early signs of recovery.
pages.title: LPs continue to raise the bar

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights the resilience of private debt as an asset class in 2024, emphasizing its steady performance amidst challenging market conditions. The imagery of a cable car in a misty forest symbolizes stability and navigation through uncertain times.
pages.title: Private debt remains steady in the crosswinds

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the growth in private new-issue financing for leveraged buyouts in 2024, driven by robust transaction activity and a more favorable borrowing environment. It highlights the evolution of private debt, the strong investor interest, and emerging opportunities for managers. The report focuses on direct lending and adjacent strategies, excluding public credit and structured products.
pages.title: Private new-issue financing for leveraged buyouts (LBOs) increased in the United States and Europe in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the decline in financing spreads across various channels in 2024, highlighting the narrowing gap between direct lending and broadly syndicated loans. This trend suggests a more competitive financing market, potentially reducing private debt's premium. The analysis includes a detailed exhibit showing the spread of LBO financing in direct lending versus the BSL market.
pages.title: Financing spreads decline

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the shift in leveraged-buyout financing from direct lenders to syndicated lenders in 2024, highlighting the decline in direct lending's share of new-issue LBO financings. It also mentions the increasing prominence of insurance capital and other permanent capital sources for private debt GPs, emphasizing the suitability of private debt for insurers and the role of BDCs and interval funds in providing retail investors access to private debt.
pages.title: Leveraged-buyout financing shifts toward syndicated lenders

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_49.jpg
pages.abstract: Regulatory changes have constrained banks' lending, leading middle-market companies to seek nonbank financing. Basel IV reforms will increase capital reserves and limit flexibility in higher risk-weighted assets. Banks are partnering with private debt GPs to finance economic activities as originators and distributors. Private debt managers are deploying capital into a broader range of asset types for diversification.
pages.title: Private debt expands its footprint amid regulatory reform

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_50.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how GPs can remain competitive in private credit by acquiring specific origination and underwriting capabilities for new asset classes like asset-backed finance, project finance, and real estate debt. It also highlights the diversification of capital bases and broader participation across the risk/return spectrum. The exhibit assesses factors affecting nonbank penetration of US asset classes, showing that infrastructure, asset-backed finance, and higher-risk commercial real estate are most likely to transition to nonbanks.
pages.title: Infrastructure, asset-backed finance, and higher-risk commercial real estate are among the asset types most likely to transition to nonbanks.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_51.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the decline in global private debt fundraising by 22% to $166 billion in 2024, yet it was still the fifth-largest fundraising year. Direct lending grew by 2%, while mezzanine fundraising fell by over 80%. Fundraising declined across geographies, with North America experiencing a 18% drop, and Europe and Asia seeing sharper declines. The analysis highlights increased manager concentration and steady investor appetite as key themes.
pages.title: Fundraisers: Direct lending remains strong amid a cooling market

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_52.jpg
pages.abstract: The page presents data on global private debt fundraising from 2011 to 2024, showing a 22% decline in 2024. Direct lending has been the dominant substrategy, growing steadily as a percentage of total fundraising. Other substrategies experienced varying growth rates, with some showing significant declines.
pages.title: Private debt fundraising declined 22 percent in 2024.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_53.jpg
pages.abstract: The concentration of private debt fundraising is increasing, with the top five managers raising 38% of funds in 2024. Scale provides competitive advantages, including diverse financing solutions, liquidity, and reduced concentration risk. Larger lenders lead facilities through scaled commitments, enhancing deal access and terms. GPs with scale invest in capabilities to attract alternative capital sources.
pages.title: Private-debt fundraising is growing more concentrated

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_54.jpg
pages.abstract: Despite fundraising challenges in 2024, investor interest in private debt remains strong, driven by superior risk-adjusted returns and portfolio diversification. Private debt outperformed other asset classes in 2024, with a pooled net IRR of 6.6%. The performance gap between top and bottom quartile private debt funds is narrower compared to other asset classes, indicating low return dispersion.
pages.title: Investor appetite holds steady

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_55.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the low default rates in private debt, which increased slightly in 2024. It compares private credit default rates with syndicated loans, attributing the difference to superior risk management in private debt. It also warns of potential increases in default-driven losses and highlights the future role of private debt in lending against distressed assets and nontraditional sectors.
pages.title: Default rates remain low—for now

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_56.jpg
pages.abstract: The infrastructure asset class experienced a mixed year, characterized by robust deal activity and stronger relative performance, but also faced challenges with slower fundraising efforts.
pages.title: Infrastructure poised for clearer conditions

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_57.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges and opportunities in infrastructure investment in 2024, highlighting decreased fundraising but accelerated capital deployment. It explores the bullish investor sentiment, driven by global trade growth, energy transition needs, and demographic shifts. The text also notes the shift in investment strategies towards value-oriented initiatives and the importance of active ownership in a competitive market.
pages.title: Infrastructure Investment Trends in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_58.jpg
pages.abstract: Infrastructure dealmaking saw a significant rebound in 2024, with deal value increasing by 18% and deal count by 7%. The telecom sector notably grew, accounting for 16% of total infrastructure deals by value, driven by demand for fiber networks and data centers. Data centers alone made up 58% of telecom deals in 2024, compared to 2% in 2015.
pages.title: Dealmakers and operators: Regaining their stride

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_59.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses renewable energy as a core investment theme, highlighting trends such as the convergence of energy and digital, emphasis on value creation, and increased investment in services. It details the growing demand for data center power, the importance of strategic planning for value creation, and the recognition of service businesses in infrastructure investments.
pages.title: Renewable Energy and Infrastructure Trends

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_60.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges faced by fundraisers in the infrastructure and natural resources sector in 2024, with a 15% decrease in global fundraising to $106 billion. The definition of infrastructure assets is expanding, and Exhibit 2 illustrates regional fundraising trends, showing a decline in North America and growth in Europe and Asia.
pages.title: Fundraisers: Facing ongoing hurdles

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_61.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the decline in natural resources funds raised, the extended fundraising period, and the reduced proportion of dollars raised by first-time funds. It highlights the influence of larger funds on infrastructure fundraising and notes that two of the largest historical fundraisers did not close a fund in 2024. The page includes Exhibit 3, which shows global infrastructure and natural resource fundraising by fund size from 2011 to 2024, illustrating the significant impact of larger funds.
pages.title: The largest funds heavily influence infrastructure fundraising.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_62.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses 2024 infrastructure fundraising trends, highlighting a 40% increase in Europe and a 57% decline in North America. It emphasizes the growing demand for value-added strategies, with value-added vehicles accounting for 34% of fundraising, compared to a 10-year average of 19%. Core-plus and debt strategies saw decreased interest. The shift toward value-added investing suggests a move along the risk-reward spectrum, urging GPs to focus on active asset management.
pages.title: Infrastructure fundraising trends in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_63.jpg
pages.abstract: Infrastructure was the top-performing private asset class in 2024, with a one-year pooled net IRR of 6.1 percent. LPs are increasingly seeking higher-risk opportunities, with value-added strategies favored. Despite overallocation, 46 percent of respondents plan to increase infrastructure allocation over the next 12 months.
pages.title: LPs: Embracing more risk for superior returns

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_64.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses infrastructure investment trends, highlighting a 44% increase in allocations to value-added strategies. Pension funds and family offices show significant interest, driven by predictable returns and long-term investment appetites. Despite challenges, stakeholders remain committed, with expanding definitions of infrastructure and hybrid assets driving future success through active ownership.
pages.title: Infrastructure Investment Trends and Strategies

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_65.jpg
pages.abstract: This page introduces the section 'Industry deep dives', likely exploring detailed insights into various industries. The image of a snow-covered mountain peak symbolizes challenges and the need for resilience in shifting conditions.
pages.title: Industry deep dives

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_66.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the increasing role of nontraditional capital sources in private markets' assets under management (AUM). It highlights the rise of novel AUM forms and explains the reasons behind this trend.
pages.title: Alternative assets get more alternative: The rise of novel AUM forms

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_67.jpg
pages.abstract: This article discusses the shift in private market capital from traditional AUM to alternative sources, including higher-liquidity products, LP demand-driven products, and permanent capital. These sources contributed $7-8 trillion in AUM in 2024, increasing the overall private market size by nearly 50%. The proliferation of alternative capital is driven by democratization of access for retail investors and customized solutions for institutional investors.
pages.title: Why are alternative sources of capital proliferating?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_68.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the increasing traction of alternative capital pools in private markets, regulatory changes enabling greater retail access, and innovations in fund structures and services. It highlights customized investment solutions for large institutional investors and the expansion of the private market universe.
pages.title: Although traditional AUM remains the bread and butter of the typical GP, alternative capital pools are increasingly gaining traction.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_69.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the growth of alternative sources of capital in private markets, highlighting higher liquidity products, LP demand-driven products, and permanent capital. These forms are estimated to add $7 to $8 trillion to the global private capital AUM by 2024, representing nearly 33% of total private market assets under management. The analysis underscores the increasing importance of these alternative forms in the private market universe.
pages.title: What value is at stake?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_70.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the growth of nontraditional capital, which has outpaced traditional AUM growth. It highlights the factors considered in analyzing alternative capital, including the exclusion of certain funds to avoid double counting. The page also covers liquid-alternative funds and higher-liquidity products, detailing their characteristics and contributions to AUM.
pages.title: Growth in nontraditional capital

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_71.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses LP demand-driven offerings like SMAs and co-investments, their benefits for LPs and GPs, and the growth in AUM. It also covers the role of permanent capital from insurance companies and the strategies GPs need to adopt for successful fundraising and investor relations.
pages.title: Products driven by LP demand

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_72.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the shift from fundraising to a solution-oriented mindset in alternative investments, emphasizing the need for tailored products and efficient back-office operations. It highlights the importance of considering various sources of capital beyond traditional AUM to sustain and boost demand in the private market.
pages.title: Switch from a fundraising to a solution mindset

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_73.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges private equity firms face in exiting assets and suggests actionable steps for GPs to execute sales efficiently and profitably.
pages.title: Private equity’s path to clearing the historic exit backlog

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_74.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges faced by private equity sponsors in exiting their investments, highlighting a significant backlog of assets awaiting divestment. It provides statistics on the number of companies under PE ownership for extended periods and the mismatch in valuation expectations between buyers and sellers. The article aims to explore strategies for GPs to improve timely and profitable exits.
pages.title: Private equity sponsors' exit problem

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_75.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges faced by private equity sponsors in exiting their investments due to extended holding periods and lack of suitable exits. It highlights the increasing importance of distributed to paid-in capital (DPI) as a performance metric for limited partners, alongside internal rate of return (IRR) and multiple on invested capital (MOIC). The text also addresses the impact of higher buyout entry multiples on returns and the need for greater value creation.
pages.title: Private equity’s exit challenge

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_76.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges of exiting investments in the current market environment, highlighting a mismatch between buyer and seller price expectations. It analyzes the valuations of maturing assets compared to market-clearing prices, showing that in 2024, these valuations were significantly higher than in previous years. The data from Hamilton Lane illustrates that all PE subsectors had elevated marks in 2024, indicating a uniform consistency in elevated valuations.
pages.title: Near-maturity assets are increasingly held at valuations higher than the prevailing market price.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_77.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges in selling PE assets, especially for large sponsors, and emphasizes the importance of exit preparation. It outlines strategies for GPs to optimize exit preparations based on the asset life cycle stages, including diligence, holding, and divestment. The text highlights the need to consider exit potential during diligence and prioritize value creation initiatives early in the holding period. It also introduces two value creation plans: postclose VCP and midcycle VCP, aimed at sustaining performance improvement.
pages.title: Preparing for an exit

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_78.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for value creation in private equity assets, focusing on midcycle value creation plans, exit preparation, and likely exit pathways. It highlights the importance of aligning value creation efforts with potential buyers and explains approaches for strategic buyers, sponsor-to-sponsor exits, and IPOs.
pages.title: Value Creation Strategies for PE Assets

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_79.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of flexibility in GP exit strategies, emphasizing the need to avoid decisions that limit future exit options. It highlights the challenges of managing exits in the current market and the benefits of mastering the exit process throughout the asset life cycle. The page also introduces key contributors from McKinsey.
pages.title: GP Exit Strategies and Flexibility

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_80.jpg
pages.title: Secondaries and GP stakes: The next wave of private market innovation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_81.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the limitations of traditional commingled-fund approaches in private markets and introduces two emerging strategies: secondaries and GP stakes. It highlights the benefits of these strategies, such as providing liquidity and strategic capital sourcing, and their potential for deployment and additional capital sourcing within the private market universe.
pages.title: Securities sustain upward momentum

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_82.jpg
pages.abstract: The secondaries market benefits GPs by allowing them to retain control while selling assets through GP-led transactions. In 2024, deal volume increased by 45% to $162 billion, driven by LP-led and GP-led secondaries. Nearly 84% of GP-led deals involved continuation vehicles.
pages.title: Global secondaries market benefits for GPs

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_83.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the fundraising efforts of GPs in the secondaries market, highlighting a record $65 billion raised in 2024. It notes the concentration of fundraising among top GPs and the increasing role of managers outside the top ten. Pricing in secondary transactions is also addressed, emphasizing the importance of factors beyond discounts to NAV.
pages.title: Fundraising

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_84.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the rise in secondaries pricing as a percentage of NAV across various private market asset classes in 2024. Buyout secondaries reached the highest percentage at 94%, while private debt secondaries saw the most significant increase. Real estate secondaries remained the lowest at 72%. This upward trend in pricing is expected to encourage more transactions as LPs can exit positions while retaining a larger share of book value.
pages.title: Secondaries pricing increased across asset classes in 2024.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_85.jpg
pages.abstract: Secondaries funds offer liquidity and risk-adjusted returns, outperforming private equity in recent years. They provide diversification and act as a hedge, with higher returns during bear markets and reduced discounts in strong markets. The correlation between secondary stake pricing and fund performance is evident.
pages.title: Performance

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_86.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the performance of secondaries funds compared to other private capital asset classes, highlighting their higher median returns and stronger liquidity profile. It also introduces GP stakes as a growing strategy for investors to access private markets, with a focus on minority equity stakes. Exhibit 5 provides a visual comparison of median IRR and percentile spreads across different asset classes.
pages.title: GP stakes: A nascent but growing strategy

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_87.jpg
pages.abstract: LPs are increasingly investing in GP stakes due to the growth in the private capital industry, attractive risk/return profiles, and confidence in private market growth. This strategy offers new investment opportunities and has seen robust fundraising volumes in 2024.
pages.title: For LPs, investing in GP stakes can open new investment opportunities

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_88.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the fundraising trends for GP stakes funds, highlighting a significant increase in 2024 to $4.4 billion, though still below the peak of $31 billion in 2022. It notes the acceleration in fundraising pace over the past three years, with an average of $12 billion raised annually across nearly seven funds. The performance of GP stakes funds, with consistent returns and low dispersion, is a key factor driving interest. The document also includes a bar chart showing global GP stakes fundraising from 2014 to 2024.
pages.title: Fundraising

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_89.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the performance of general partner stakes funds compared to buyout funds, highlighting lower return dispersion and similar median returns. It also explores new opportunities for LPs and GPs in secondaries and GP stakes, emphasizing the need for building new capabilities such as effective due diligence, data strategies, and partnerships.
pages.title: General partner stakes funds exhibit a lower return dispersion and similar median returns compared with buyout funds.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_90.jpg
pages.title: Authors

pages.page_path: library_pages\Global Private Markets Report 2025_ Braced for shifting weather_McKinsey_2025_05_01\page_91.jpg
pages.title: Acknowledgments
