pages.title: M&A Annual Report

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_2.jpg
pages.abstract: This report discusses the global M&A market's performance in 2024, highlighting resilience and positive outlook for 2025. It emphasizes McKinsey's role in supporting business and financial executives through various M&A activities, leveraging expertise and global networks. The report also acknowledges contributions from colleagues and clients, expressing gratitude to readers for their interest.
pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_3.jpg
pages.title: Contents

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_4.jpg
pages.title: Peering around corners

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the moderate performance of global M&A markets in 2024, influenced by various pressures. It anticipates a strong upward trend in 2025, driven by receding challenges and favorable macroeconomic conditions. However, it notes that benefits will vary among regions, sectors, and dealmakers, with successful strategies requiring clear vision and distinct capabilities.
pages.title: Global M&A markets: The case for optimism

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the strong financial positions of corporations in the market for deals, the need for companies to adjust their portfolios for growth, and the successful pursuit of M&A programmatically. It also highlights the impact of political transitions and regulatory changes on various industries, shifts in national politics and international alliances, and the critical role of transactions in adapting to new requirements.
pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: Private equity plays a crucial role in boosting M&A activities in 2025, with substantial dry powder and extended exit hold times. Sponsor-led contributions are lower than in 2021, indicating growth potential. The private-investment industry's growth, especially in the US, encourages more dealmaking. However, geopolitical instability and trade policy changes pose significant risks to M&A activity.
pages.title: The special role of private equity

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the impact of trade policy changes on economic growth, highlighting concerns among business executives. It presents survey data showing that changes in trade policy are seen as the biggest risk in North America and Greater China. The page also touches on regulatory scrutiny as a potential drag on M&A activities.
pages.title: In North America and Greater China, respondents expect changes in trade policy to have the biggest effect on their countries' economies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: The global M&A market in 2024 saw a 12% increase in deal value to $3.4 trillion, with an 8% rise in the number of deals. Average deal value grew by 4%, reflecting improved macroeconomic conditions and dealmakers' resilience to geopolitical tensions. New antitrust regulations added complexity and time to deal preparations.
pages.title: Looking back at 2024 global M&A returns

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: The 2024 M&A landscape saw a decline in megadeals, with midsize deals becoming more popular. Corporate dealmakers dominated transactions, while financial investors reemerged. Energy, materials, tech, media, telecom, and financial services sectors were the busiest, accounting for nearly 60% of company value changes.
pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: The Americas experienced a significant increase in M&A activity in 2024, with deal value growing 12% and deal volume increasing 9%. The average deal size also rose to $648 million. This trend is expected to continue in 2025.
pages.title: Looking back at 2024 regional M&A returns

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: The economic outlook in the Americas is positive due to strong corporate profits, cooling inflation, and a normalizing labor market. Dealmakers closed major deals, and companies attracted global interest. However, policy changes and uncertainty around the new US administration's policies could impact growth. Rising confidence among US CEOs is supported by historical trends in merger volumes during second-term presidencies.
pages.title: With strong corporate profits, cooling inflation, a normalizing labor market, relatively low household debt, and other factors, the economic outlook in the Americas looks positive.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: The EMEA region saw a 15% increase in M&A activity in 2024, despite economic challenges and geopolitical risks. Companies focused on resilience, scale, and efficiency. The eurozone's growth is expected to be 1%, and PE firms accounted for 29% of M&A value.
pages.title: EMEA

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses M&A activity in EMEA and APAC regions in 2024, highlighting an 8% increase in average deal value in EMEA and a 10% rise in overall deal value in APAC. Despite these improvements, deal values and volumes still lagged behind 20-year averages. The page also notes regional disparities, with Greater China experiencing a 45% decline in activity since 2020, while Australia and New Zealand saw significant inflows due to large mining deals.
pages.title: M&A activity increased 10 percent in 2024 in the Asia-Pacific region.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses M&A trends in the APAC region, highlighting India's decline in M&A activity, cautious optimism for 2025, China's government-driven deals, interest in Indian firms from overseas investors, and rising valuations in Japan. It concludes with an overview of the 2024 deal value increase and underlying shifts.
pages.title: M&A Trends in APAC Region

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses effective M&A practices, emphasizing the importance of adapting tactics and investing in M&A capabilities. It highlights strategies like reducing global risks, integrating AI for deal origination, focusing on smaller deals, and creating a diligence advantage to enhance transaction value and mitigate risks.
pages.title: Looking ahead

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for capturing full synergies, sharpening integration approaches, and using transactions to drive transformations in M&A. It emphasizes the importance of balancing integration priorities, leveraging AI for problem-solving, and tailoring incentives to retain talent. The page also highlights the role of transactions in launching broad transformations and reshaping market structures.
pages.title: Capture full synergies, Sharpen integration approaches, Use transactions to forge transformations

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_18.jpg
pages.title: Industry deep dives

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how new technologies and supply chain shifts are influencing key portfolio and investment decisions in advanced industries. Trends such as reduced interest rates and the emergence of new technologies, software, and ecosystems are expected to increase M&A activity in this sector.
pages.title: Advanced industries

pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.abstract: The document discusses M&A activity in advanced industries, noting a decrease in total deal value but an increase in the number of smaller deals in 2024. It highlights trends such as reduced interest rates, new technologies, and the role of private equity. The subsector activity in automotive, aerospace and defense, industrials and electronics, and semiconductors is also analyzed, emphasizing opportunities and challenges in each area.
pages.title: The industry overview—and opportunities for 2025 and beyond

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses M&A trends in the automotive and aerospace sectors, highlighting the shift towards software and electrification in automotive, the expansion of Asia-Pacific companies into Europe, and the concentration of aerospace M&A in North America. It also notes the trend of aerospace companies moving away from traditional structures and the emergence of new space-related technologies.
pages.title: M&A Activity in Automotive and Aerospace Sectors

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the trends in industrials and electronics manufacturing, focusing on increased interest in acquisitions involving software, AI, sustainability, and decarbonization technologies. It highlights the importance of connected technologies in building technology ecosystems and the need for commercial and industrial companies to focus on software capabilities. The rapid transition toward sustainable technology is expected to accelerate equipment purchase cycles. The semiconductor subsector will likely experience strong demand due to AI and automotive trends, but will face talent shortages and geopolitical challenges. M&A will be a key strategy for diversification and capability enhancement.
pages.title: Industrials and electronics

pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

The capital-market, wealth-and-asset management, and fintech sectors are growing, while bank acquisitions have declined. Opportunities for 2025 include sector consolidation in banking and cross-border deals in Europe.

pages.title: M&A Trends in Financial Services

pages.abstract: This page discusses the potential for market expansion and growth in the consumer goods sector, driven by declining interest rates and strong financial positions of CPG companies, suggesting an active year for CPG deals.
pages.title: Consumer goods: Seeking market expansion and growth

pages.abstract: The page provides a comprehensive analysis of M&A activities in the consumer goods sector, highlighting regional deal values and volumes, private equity involvement, and subsector activity shares. It also shows trends in average deal sizes across various subsectors from 2020 to 2024.
pages.title: M&A in consumer goods

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_32.jpg

pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: The CPG industry faces challenges due to inflation, market saturation, and climate change. Companies have shifted from inorganic growth to a balanced approach, focusing on midsize deals and synergies. Recent acquisitions exemplify this strategy, aiming for growth and cost savings in adjacent product categories.
pages.title: The industry overview

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the potential for increased CPG deal activity in 2025, driven by low interest rates and strong balance sheets. It highlights three types of transactions: sector-shaping, horizontal, and targeted spin-offs. Strategic buyers have advantages in sector-shaping and horizontal deals, while financial buyers, especially PE funds, are expected to be active. The food-and-beverage sector is expected to lead deal activity, with heightened activity also anticipated in personal care and beauty sectors.
pages.title: Opportunities for 2025—and beyond

pages.abstract: The global energy and materials sector shows stable overall deal value, with certain segments gaining market share. Factors indicate rising M&A activity in 2025 despite sector uncertainties.
pages.title: Global energy and materials

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: The page provides a comprehensive analysis of M&A activities in the global energy and materials sector, highlighting regional deal values and volumes, private equity involvement, subsector activity shares, and average deal sizes across various years. The data covers the years 2020 and 2024, showing trends in deal sizes and cross-border activities.
pages.title: M&A Annual Report: Is the wave finally arriving?

pages.abstract: The document discusses the M&A activity in the global energy-and-materials sector in 2024, noting a 12% increase in deals but a 14% lower deal value compared to 2021. It highlights regional trends, the cautious approach of companies, and anticipates increased M&A activity in 2025 due to factors like interest rates and portfolio reshaping. It also analyzes subsector activities and cross-regional deals.
pages.title: The industry overview

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: The EPNG sector saw a 40% increase in deal value in 2024, with a focus on asset transfers and consolidation. Challenges persist due to macroeconomic factors, but interest in renewables is growing. Oil and gas companies are consolidating portfolios and exploring new regions, particularly in the U.S. Permian Basin.
pages.title: EPNG: Deal Value and Industry Trends

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_40.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses M&A trends in chemicals, agriculture, and materials sectors, highlighting decreased deal values, regional shifts in activity, and motivations such as portfolio optimization and consolidation. It also covers the impact of market conditions, government programs, and global trends on M&A activity in these sectors.

Purposeful M&A, despite challenges, offers higher excess TSR and no-regret actions for value creation.

The text underscores the need for early board clarity and addresses various concerns that boards consider during separations.

The text emphasizes the need for clear, data-driven arguments and thorough planning to ensure successful separation.
pages.title: Board concerns should be addressed early to avoid delays and resource overruns.

Tools like McKinsey’s myIMO are evolving to provide fast, smart answers and automate post-day-one activities.
pages.title: Expediting the diligence and negotiation process

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_107.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how senior leaders can enhance their M&A capabilities using Gen AI, focusing on assessing past deals, calculating deal impacts, and generating insights. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing AI use cases and deciding whether to develop or adopt solutions, while considering the company's M&A strategy and team resources.
pages.title: Senior leaders need to frankly assess their current level of M&A capabilities and consider where in the M&A process technology can be used to materially improve the M&A engine.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_108.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of establishing appropriate guardrails for generative AI (Gen AI) in business, highlighting risks such as security breaches and intellectual property infringement. It emphasizes the need for human oversight and ethical standards in AI applications. The text also mentions the strategic opportunities that Gen AI presents, such as focusing on high-value activities like relationship building. Finally, it notes the growing role of Gen AI in M&A and the need to monitor its impact.
pages.title: Ensure that the right guardrails are in place

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_109.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses five critical actions CEOs must take during M&A transactions, based on McKinsey research and interviews with global leaders. It highlights the importance of CEO involvement in ensuring successful M&A processes.
pages.title: CEOs in M&A: Five actions only the chief executive can take

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_110.jpg
pages.abstract: The CEO's agenda involves addressing global business concerns and leveraging M&A as a strategic tool. CEOs must focus on strategy, deal size, stakeholder management, capabilities, and culture to ensure M&A success. Defining M&A priorities within the long-term corporate strategy is crucial for identifying opportunities and mounting strategic responses.
pages.title: The CEO's agenda

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_111.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the role of CEOs in M&A, emphasizing the importance of focusing on strategic considerations and delegating detailed tasks. It highlights the need for CEOs to engage with a shortlist of opportunities that align with corporate strategy and to be directly involved in transformative deals, serving as deal champions throughout all phases.
pages.title: Spearhead large, transformational deals—delegate the rest

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_112.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the CEO's role in smaller M&A deals, emphasizing strategic alignment, value creation, and stakeholder management. It highlights the importance of the CEO as a 'chief stakeholder officer,' managing expectations with the target CEO and the board of directors to ensure successful integration and value capture.
pages.title: Be the 'chief stakeholder officer'

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_113.jpg
pages.abstract: The target company CEO plays a crucial role in M&A deals, providing insights into strategies and culture, and aiding the acquiring company's CEO. Effective communication with the board and stakeholders is vital for deal success, fostering trust and transparency throughout the process.
pages.title: CEOs in M&A: What about the target company CEO?

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_114.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of conviction, capacity, and capabilities for successful M&A execution. It highlights the CEO's role in securing organizational conviction and building a management team with the necessary capacity and capabilities. It also emphasizes the significance of a healthy organizational culture for M&A success.
pages.title: Secure the three C’s: Conviction, capacity, and capabilities to execute on M&A

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_115.jpg
pages.abstract: CEOs play a crucial role in M&A by assessing cultures, aligning skills, and ensuring cultural compatibility. They must invest time in due diligence, build relationships, and communicate the vision for the combined company's culture. Establishing guardrails and delegating tasks to a dedicated team is key to successful integration.
pages.title: CEO's Role in M&A Cultural Integration

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_116.jpg
pages.title: Why managing culture is critical for value creation in M&A

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_117.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of organizational culture in M&A transactions, highlighting the risks of cultural misalignment and the benefits of addressing cultural factors. It emphasizes the need for executives to diagnose cultural issues, set priorities, and establish a clear cultural transformation plan to ensure successful integrations.
pages.title: An organization's culture

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_118.jpg
pages.abstract: Leaders should diagnose work processes, set cultural priorities, and support cultural change in M&A discussions. Early involvement of stakeholders and using diagnostics like surveys and interviews can help understand cultural aspects and build common norms.
pages.title: Leaders can take three steps to actively consider aspects of culture in their M&A discussions: diagnosing how work gets done, setting cultural priorities, and hard-wiring and supporting cultural change.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_119.jpg
pages.abstract: Leaders must set cultural priorities using data on existing cultures, addressing common friction points like decision-making and communication styles. They should redefine roles, introduce new cultural artifacts, and serve as role models for behavioral changes. Concrete initiatives and KPIs can support desired cultural shifts.
pages.title: Set cultural priorities

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_120.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of hard-wiring cultural changes into a company's operating model and daily practices. It emphasizes the role of leadership in creating a culture of respect, implementing signature initiatives, empowering change agents, and tracking the implementation of themes and initiatives with the same rigor as financial targets. The page concludes by highlighting the critical role of culture in mergers and acquisitions.
pages.title: Hard-wire and support cultural change

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_121.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses a strategy for managing talent during M&A transactions, emphasizing the importance of retaining and engaging top talent throughout the process to create value. It highlights the critical phases of M&A and offers insights into addressing talent needs effectively.
pages.title: Retain, integrate, thrive: A strategy for managing talent during M&A transactions

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_122.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the paradox in M&A transactions where top talent may leave, causing operational risks and value loss. It highlights the importance of retaining critical talent through strategic steps before, during, and after integrations, emphasizing communication, incentives, and employee value proposition.
pages.title: There is a paradox built into some M&A transactions

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_123.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of identifying and categorizing crucial employee groups in both the target and parent companies before a deal is announced. It emphasizes the need to consider employees at all levels and highlights the significance of nonfinancial incentives in retaining top talent. The page also stresses the role of senior leaders in shaping messaging and conveying empathy to maintain business continuity and future success.
pages.title: Before a deal is announced: Prepare the ground

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_124.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for maintaining stability and focus during the period between a deal announcement and its close in M&A transactions. It emphasizes the importance of effective communication, leadership actions, and the role of frontline managers in retaining top talent and ensuring employee engagement throughout the integration process.
pages.title: Between the deal announcement and close: Maintain stability and focus

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_125.jpg
pages.abstract: Metrics are crucial for performance management, especially in transitions. Leaders should monitor retention metrics, conduct exit interviews, and use tools like dashboards and toolkits to maintain communication and lower attrition. Post-deal, solidifying engagement involves combating change fatigue and creating unity among employees.
pages.title: Metrics are always central to effective performance management, but monitoring and measuring the outcome of retention programs are especially important in times of transition.

pages.page_path: library_pages\M&A Annual Report_ Is the wave finally arriving_McKinsey_2025_02\page_126.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of a redesigned Employee Value Proposition (EVP) post-merger and acquisition (M&A) to align with the new company's direction. It highlights a B2B electronic-materials player's large-scale organizational transformation and the need for a revised EVP. The page emphasizes integrating five core elements of the EVP into daily work and the role of 'cultivation leaders' in retaining talent. It concludes by stressing the critical role of talent in deal theses and the need for a fit-for-purpose retention strategy.
pages.title: Employee Value Proposition in Post-M&A Integration

This report discusses the global M&A market's performance in 2024, highlighting resilience and positive outlook for 2025. It emphasizes McKinsey's role in supporting business and financial executives through various M&A activities, leveraging expertise and global networks. The report also acknowledges contributions from colleagues and clients, expressing gratitude to readers for their interest.
The document discusses the moderate performance of global M&A markets in 2024, influenced by various pressures. It anticipates a strong upward trend in 2025, driven by receding challenges and favorable macroeconomic conditions. However, it notes that benefits will vary among regions, sectors, and dealmakers, with successful strategies requiring clear vision and distinct capabilities.
This page discusses the strong financial positions of corporations in the market for deals, the need for companies to adjust their portfolios for growth, and the successful pursuit of M&A programmatically. It also highlights the impact of political transitions and regulatory changes on various industries, shifts in national politics and international alliances, and the critical role of transactions in adapting to new requirements.
Private equity plays a crucial role in boosting M&A activities in 2025, with substantial dry powder and extended exit hold times. Sponsor-led contributions are lower than in 2021, indicating growth potential. The private-investment industry's growth, especially in the US, encourages more dealmaking. However, geopolitical instability and trade policy changes pose significant risks to M&A activity.
The page discusses the impact of trade policy changes on economic growth, highlighting concerns among business executives. It presents survey data showing that changes in trade policy are seen as the biggest risk in North America and Greater China. The page also touches on regulatory scrutiny as a potential drag on M&A activities.
The global M&A market in 2024 saw a 12% increase in deal value to $3.4 trillion, with an 8% rise in the number of deals. Average deal value grew by 4%, reflecting improved macroeconomic conditions and dealmakers' resilience to geopolitical tensions. New antitrust regulations added complexity and time to deal preparations.
The 2024 M&A landscape saw a decline in megadeals, with midsize deals becoming more popular. Corporate dealmakers dominated transactions, while financial investors reemerged. Energy, materials, tech, media, telecom, and financial services sectors were the busiest, accounting for nearly 60% of company value changes.
The Americas experienced a significant increase in M&A activity in 2024, with deal value growing 12% and deal volume increasing 9%. The average deal size also rose to $648 million. This trend is expected to continue in 2025.
The economic outlook in the Americas is positive due to strong corporate profits, cooling inflation, and a normalizing labor market. Dealmakers closed major deals, and companies attracted global interest. However, policy changes and uncertainty around the new US administration's policies could impact growth. Rising confidence among US CEOs is supported by historical trends in merger volumes during second-term presidencies.
The EMEA region saw a 15% increase in M&A activity in 2024, despite economic challenges and geopolitical risks. Companies focused on resilience, scale, and efficiency. The eurozone's growth is expected to be 1%, and PE firms accounted for 29% of M&A value.
The page discusses M&A activity in EMEA and APAC regions in 2024, highlighting an 8% increase in average deal value in EMEA and a 10% rise in overall deal value in APAC. Despite these improvements, deal values and volumes still lagged behind 20-year averages. The page also notes regional disparities, with Greater China experiencing a 45% decline in activity since 2020, while Australia and New Zealand saw significant inflows due to large mining deals.
The document discusses M&A trends in the APAC region, highlighting India's decline in M&A activity, cautious optimism for 2025, China's government-driven deals, interest in Indian firms from overseas investors, and rising valuations in Japan. It concludes with an overview of the 2024 deal value increase and underlying shifts.
This page discusses effective M&A practices, emphasizing the importance of adapting tactics and investing in M&A capabilities. It highlights strategies like reducing global risks, integrating AI for deal origination, focusing on smaller deals, and creating a diligence advantage to enhance transaction value and mitigate risks.
This page discusses strategies for capturing full synergies, sharpening integration approaches, and using transactions to drive transformations in M&A. It emphasizes the importance of balancing integration priorities, leveraging AI for problem-solving, and tailoring incentives to retain talent. The page also highlights the role of transactions in launching broad transformations and reshaping market structures.
This page discusses how new technologies and supply chain shifts are influencing key portfolio and investment decisions in advanced industries. Trends such as reduced interest rates and the emergence of new technologies, software, and ecosystems are expected to increase M&A activity in this sector.
The page presents data on M&A activities in advanced industries, showing total deal value and volume by region, private equity activity share, subsector activity share in 2024, and average deal size by subsector. It highlights trends and differences across regions and subsectors from 2020 to 2024.
The page provides an overview of M&A trends, including total deal value by size, share of deal volume, and cross-border deal shares. It also lists the top 10 global deals by value, highlighting major acquirers, targets, and deal values. The data is sourced from Dealogic and McKinsey analysis.
The document discusses M&A activity in advanced industries, noting a decrease in total deal value but an increase in the number of smaller deals in 2024. It highlights trends such as reduced interest rates, new technologies, and the role of private equity. The subsector activity in automotive, aerospace and defense, industrials and electronics, and semiconductors is also analyzed, emphasizing opportunities and challenges in each area.
This page discusses M&A trends in the automotive and aerospace sectors, highlighting the shift towards software and electrification in automotive, the expansion of Asia-Pacific companies into Europe, and the concentration of aerospace M&A in North America. It also notes the trend of aerospace companies moving away from traditional structures and the emergence of new space-related technologies.
This page discusses the trends in industrials and electronics manufacturing, focusing on increased interest in acquisitions involving software, AI, sustainability, and decarbonization technologies. It highlights the importance of connected technologies in building technology ecosystems and the need for commercial and industrial companies to focus on software capabilities. The rapid transition toward sustainable technology is expected to accelerate equipment purchase cycles. The semiconductor subsector will likely experience strong demand due to AI and automotive trends, but will face talent shortages and geopolitical challenges. M&A will be a key strategy for diversification and capability enhancement.
The financial services sector is adapting to a changing landscape. In 2024, most deals were domestic. For 2025, various financial sectors anticipate both challenges and opportunities.
The page provides a comprehensive analysis of M&A activities in financial services, highlighting regional deal values and volumes, private equity involvement, and subsector activity shares. It also tracks average deal sizes across various financial subsectors over five years.
This page presents data on M&A deals, including total deal value by size, share of deal volume, and share of cross-border deals. It also lists the top 10 global deals by value, highlighting major acquirers and targets. The data is sourced from Dealogic and McKinsey analysis.
The financial-services industry's M&A activity is recovering, with 2024 seeing a return to pre-2023 levels. Deals are increasingly domestic, driven by scale and capability. The capital-market, wealth-and-asset management, and fintech sectors are growing, while bank acquisitions have declined. Opportunities for 2025 include sector consolidation in banking and cross-border deals in Europe.

This page discusses the potential for market expansion and growth in the consumer goods sector, driven by declining interest rates and strong financial positions of CPG companies, suggesting an active year for CPG deals.

The top 10 deals are listed with their acquirers, targets, and deal values, emphasizing significant transactions like Mars acquiring Kellanova for $36.1 billion.
The CPG industry faces challenges due to inflation, market saturation, and climate change. Companies have shifted from inorganic growth to a balanced approach, focusing on midsize deals and synergies. Recent acquisitions exemplify this strategy, aiming for growth and cost savings in adjacent product categories.
The document discusses the potential for increased CPG deal activity in 2025, driven by low interest rates and strong balance sheets. It highlights three types of transactions: sector-shaping, horizontal, and targeted spin-offs. Strategic buyers have advantages in sector-shaping and horizontal deals, while financial buyers, especially PE funds, are expected to be active. The food-and-beverage sector is expected to lead deal activity, with heightened activity also anticipated in personal care and beauty sectors.
The global energy and materials sector shows stable overall deal value, with certain segments gaining market share. Factors indicate rising M&A activity in 2025 despite sector uncertainties.
The page provides a comprehensive analysis of M&A activities in the global energy and materials sector, highlighting regional deal values and volumes, private equity involvement, subsector activity shares, and average deal sizes across various years. It shows a shift in focus towards electric power and natural gas sectors with increasing deal volumes and values.

The data covers the years 2020 and 2024, showing trends in deal sizes and cross-border activities.
The document discusses the M&A activity in the global energy-and-materials sector in 2024, noting a 12% increase in deals but a 14% lower deal value compared to 2021. It highlights regional trends, the cautious approach of companies, and anticipates increased M&A activity in 2025 due to factors like interest rates and portfolio reshaping. It also analyzes subsector activities and cross-regional deals.
The EPNG sector saw a 40% increase in deal value in 2024, with a focus on asset transfers and consolidation. Challenges persist due to macroeconomic factors, but interest in renewables is growing. Oil and gas companies are consolidating portfolios and exploring new regions, particularly in the U.S. Permian Basin.
This page discusses M&A trends in chemicals, agriculture, and materials sectors, highlighting decreased deal values, regional shifts in activity, and motivations such as portfolio optimization and consolidation. It also covers the impact of market conditions, government programs, and global trends on M&A activity in these sectors.
M&A activity in mining and metals is trending upward, driven by shifts in electrification, energy transition, and strategic investments. Companies are using M&A to optimize footprints, foster partnerships, and innovate. Despite headwinds like trade tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty, positive factors like lower interest rates and investor interest suggest increased deal activity in 2025.
The page provides a comprehensive overview of M&A activities in the life sciences sector, highlighting regional deal values and volumes, private equity involvement, and subsector activity shares. It also illustrates average deal sizes across various subsectors over time.
This page presents data on M&A deals, including total deal value, share of deal volume, and share of cross-border deals by size. It also lists the top 10 global deals by value, highlighting major acquirers and targets. The data is sourced from Dealogic and McKinsey analysis, with a focus on deals valued over $25 million.
The document discusses the anticipated upswing in life science M&A activity in 2025, driven by improved economic conditions, regulatory changes, and companies' need to augment their pipelines. It highlights the challenges faced in 2024 and the opportunities for 2025, emphasizing the importance of advanced tools, comprehensive diligence, and tailored integration strategies for success.
This page discusses the financial positioning and strategic activities of biopharma, medtech, and life-science-service companies. It highlights the increase in cash reserves, median holding periods, and deal premiums, emphasizing the shift towards forward-looking assets and long-term value creation. Medtech companies focus on step out acquisitions, portfolio simplification, and transactions with at-scale companies. Life-science-service companies aim for integrated solutions and consolidation.
Private capital firms are active in various industries, with technology, media, and telecommunications leading. In 2024, investors may shift from cautious to more aggressive strategies, focusing on midsize deals rather than megadeals.
The private capital market has seen fluctuating deal volumes and values, with a peak in 2021 followed by a decline. The TMT sector remains the most active, while regional trends show increased activity in the Americas. The market is poised for revitalization due to pressure for disinvestments and available dry powder.
Private capital firms face pressure to deploy reserves, explore new investment opportunities in private credit, infrastructure, and secondaries. Creative methods for exiting and reimbursement are needed. Geopolitical dynamics prompt redefinition of roles, with calls for investments in innovation and competitiveness. European competitiveness report emphasizes boosting economic competitiveness through digital technology, energy transition, defense, and innovation.
The healthcare industry faces challenges in 2024 with declining M&A deals due to high valuations, margin pressure, and regulatory uncertainty. The article assesses US deal activity, identifies developments since 2023, and highlights insights across sectors.
The page discusses 2024 US healthcare deal trends, highlighting variations in deal volume by acquirer and target subsector. Pre- and post-acute care and physicians focused on like-for-like consolidations, while hospitals and payers sought growth in near adjacencies. A detailed table illustrates deal volumes and percentages for different subsectors.
The page discusses key developments in healthcare M&A, including consolidation among physician groups, horizontal consolidation in pre-acute care, hospital-led portfolio diversification, and financial investors' focus on healthcare services and technology. It highlights trends such as the shift towards larger organizational structures, increased interest in outpatient behavioral health, and the expansion of at-home care models.
Private equity firms targeted tech-driven platforms to scale portfolio companies, focusing on physician practices to enhance operational efficiencies and service capabilities. Consolidation was prominent in pharmacy, healthcare services, and technology sectors, with like-for-like deals dominating. Payers adopted a targeted approach, focusing on same-sector consolidation and pre- and post-acute care businesses to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs.
The document discusses the decline in US healthcare deal activity in 2024 compared to 2023, with significant drops in physician and healthcare services and technology sectors. It highlights shifts in PE-led activity, focusing on healthcare services and technology deals while reducing physician group transactions. The exhibit provides detailed deal volume changes by acquirer and target subsectors, showing percentage differences and total deal volumes.
The document highlights key trends in healthcare M&A activity in 2024 compared to 2023, including a slowdown in provider-led deals, a decline in payer-led consolidation-focused deals, substantial declines in healthcare services and technology, increases in pharmacy consolidations, and pressure on private equity due to elevated asset valuations.
The document discusses operational challenges in the hospital sector and the decline in private equity transactions. It highlights growing interest in healthcare services and technology sectors, driven by the potential for tech-enabled platforms to improve efficiencies. The outlook for 2025 and 2026 is positive for M&A activity, with a focus on innovation, care-at-home models, value-based contracting, and tech-driven platforms. Challenges like labor shortages and margin pressures are seen as opportunities for creative strategies and targeted investments.
The travel, logistics, and infrastructure sectors are adapting to new opportunities in technology, shifting consumer demographics, and evolving global trade. While M&A activity in travel has been subdued, changes in travel dynamics offer growth prospects. Logistics is expected to see significant technology-driven deals by 2025 as solutions advance.
The page presents M&A trends in travel, logistics, and infrastructure sectors, showing regional deal values and volumes, private equity activity shares, subsector activity percentages, and average deal sizes over time. The data highlights significant growth and shifts in these sectors.

Opportunities for growth and transformation exist, with potential for increased business travel spending and advancements in travel technology.
Logistics companies are experiencing increased deal activity, with potential for consolidation and technology-oriented acquisitions in 2025. Trends include small deals, fragmented markets, and opportunities for bolt-on acquisitions in high-margin segments. Private investors are showing interest in specialized logistics services.
The transportation infrastructure deal activity decreased to $24 billion in 2024, with airports accounting for half of the deals. PE investors are increasingly involved in infrastructure deals, with opportunities in strategic ports and terminals for 2025.
