pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: This introduction outlines the evolving concept of risk and resilience in a world of continuous disruptions. It highlights the need for organizations to balance risk management with growth and adaptability, emphasizing resilience as a key theme. The document explores four key themes: sustainable growth, climate risk, managing uncertainty, and the evolution of risk organizations. It also discusses strategic resilience themes, lessons from Ukraine, climate risk management, and financial/nonfinancial risks.
pages.title: Introduction

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_6.jpg
pages.title: Resilience for sustainable inclusive growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: This page introduces the resilience agenda for sustainable, inclusive growth, presented at the 2023 World Economic Forum. It highlights a collaborative effort by experts from McKinsey's Risk & Resilience Practice, emphasizing the importance of comprehensive action for sustainable development.
pages.title: The resilience agenda for sustainable, inclusive growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges faced by public and private sector leaders in navigating disruptions and crises. It introduces the resilience agenda, emphasizing the need for long-term strategic planning, public-private collaboration, and international cooperation to address interconnected global issues such as climate risk, supply chain vulnerabilities, and socioeconomic inequalities.
pages.title: Leaders of public- and private-sector organizations face disruptions and crises

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: The document outlines six resilience themes: geopolitical, climate, energy, food, trade, supply chain, people, education, organization, healthcare, and digital technology. It emphasizes the need for flexible business strategies, energy transition, supply chain resilience, talent development, healthcare capacity, and ethical digital strategies. The text highlights the importance of aligning actions across these themes to address vulnerabilities and achieve sustainable, inclusive growth.
pages.title: The resilience agenda addresses six resilience themes.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the importance of defining supply chain dependencies and reducing vulnerabilities in the green-energy transition. It emphasizes the need for both efficiency improvements and transitional solutions, as well as the interlinkage of food, water, energy, and climate change. It outlines three areas for building resilient supply chains: spotting risks, reconfiguring sourcing footprints, and building capabilities within the supply chain organization.
pages.title: Organizations should define supply chain dependencies and reduce geopolitical, technological, and single-sourcing vulnerabilities.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for enhancing resilience in people, education, organizations, and healthcare systems. It emphasizes the need for flexible leadership, talent cultivation, and digital transformation to address talent shortages and improve healthcare access. The text highlights the importance of preventative care, workforce expansion, and technological advancements in achieving sustainable and inclusive growth.
pages.title: The resilience agenda for sustainable, inclusive growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the underdeveloped potential of public-private collaboration for fostering resilience, emphasizing the role of technology, leadership, finance, and sustainable economic development. It highlights the need for policy guidance, workforce training, and balanced investments to prevent economic disadvantage and enhance productivity. The value at stake in the resilience agenda is significant, with potential GDP impacts ranging from -8% to +15%.
pages.title: We must realize the underdeveloped potential of public-private collaboration to foster resilience.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the estimated impact of resilience themes on global annual GDP, ranging from –8 to +15 percent. It highlights various impact drivers across different sectors, such as climate, trade, education, digital technology, healthcare, and economic development. The page also mentions the authors and contributors to the report, emphasizing the collaboration between McKinsey and the World Economic Forum.
pages.title: Action or inaction within the resilience themes can have an impact on GDP ranging from –8 to +15 percent.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of building new businesses rather than cutting costs in uncertain economic times. It suggests that executives should focus on resilience and growth strategies.
pages.title: Business building: The path to resilience in uncertain times

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of business building in uncertain times, highlighting the need for companies to adapt to global risks and disruptions. It emphasizes the role of new businesses in enhancing resilience and growth, while addressing challenges such as innovation and internal entrepreneurship.
pages.title: Business building: The path to resilience in uncertain times

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the decline in corporate longevity, highlighting the decreasing share of top 500 global companies. It emphasizes the importance of organic growth strategies and new business builds in fostering resilience and growth, especially in the face of economic challenges and disruptions.
pages.title: Corporate longevity is declining: The share of top 500 global companies has fallen and accelerated amid disruption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the primary reasons organizations build new digital businesses, highlighting strategic diversity as a key driver. It also explores countercyclical businesses and approaches to diversify from inflation exposure, emphasizing stable revenue models and updated business strategies.
pages.title: Today, nearly a third of companies building new businesses are doing so to build a source of strategic diversity.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses resource-light businesses and consolidated supply-chain-driven businesses. It highlights how companies like Uber and Airbnb have scaled with minimal capital by acting as marketplace conveners. It also explores how asset owners are expanding their business functions and the resilience of businesses with light exposure to global logistics. The text mentions circular business models and the example of EMMA Safety Footwear, emphasizing the importance of creating a larger ecosystem for profitability and reduced vulnerability to supply chain disruptions.
pages.title: Resource-light businesses and consolidated supply-chain-driven businesses

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how companies can navigate headwinds by focusing on adjacent businesses, exemplified by News Corporation's digital transformation. It highlights the importance of business building in uncertain times, supported by a survey showing executives prioritizing it and allocating digital technology spending accordingly.
pages.title: Adjacent businesses facing less (or at least different) headwinds

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of building new businesses for corporate longevity and revenue growth. It highlights the risks and benefits, emphasizing the advantages of established companies over startups and the importance of a rigorous methodology. The 2020 survey shows that frequent business builders achieve higher returns, and the research suggests starting new ventures during market discontinuities can lead to better performance.
pages.title: Make business building a habit

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_21.jpg
pages.title: Addressing the revolving door in risk

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the increasing importance of risk management in today's volatile world, highlighting the need for risk and compliance professionals. It explores the challenges of talent scarcity and retention in the field, emphasizing the value of developing and retaining risk professionals with deeper expertise. Companies are advised to cast wide nets to fill the growing need for risk-related roles, integrating risk management more deeply into their operations.
pages.title: It's not just a figment of our collective anxiety

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines the evolution of risk management from medieval times to the 21st century, highlighting key historical events, regulatory changes, and modern challenges. It emphasizes the increasing importance of risk management in various sectors, including finance, pharmaceuticals, and cybersecurity, and the need for robust strategies to address emerging risks.
pages.title: A brief history of risk management

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the skill distance and career transitions of risk and compliance professionals, highlighting that 90% started in non-risk roles. It explains the average skill distance of 40% for new risk professionals and the higher frequency of role changes compared to those in the same risk occupation. The data shows that professionals who change industries undertake more role moves, emphasizing the importance of a skills-based approach in hiring.
pages.title: Ninety percent of risk and compliance workers started in nonrisk roles.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: Companies are hiring risk professionals from various white-collar backgrounds, with 70% coming from industries like finance and technology. Some roles require minimal skill transfer, while others involve significant leaps. Hiring managers should consider candidates' mindset and adaptability.
pages.title: Companies are hiring people into risk roles who started their careers in all sorts of other white-collar professions.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: This exhibit illustrates the flow of workers in risk and compliance roles across various sectors, showing a preference for hiring talent with industry experience. The data highlights the percentage of workers who began and are currently employed in sectors such as Financials, Telecom, media, and technology, Industrials, Healthcare, Energy and materials, and Other sectors.
pages.title: Companies in certain sectors prefer to hire risk and compliance talent with industry experience.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the starting occupations that launch workers into risk and compliance roles, highlighting the skill distances and shares of workers entering the field. It emphasizes the importance of transversal skills like information processing and inductive reasoning, which can remove barriers for candidates without college degrees. The data also reveals that few people stay on a risk and compliance career track long-term.
pages.title: Ten starting occupations launch 45 percent of workers who break into risk from other types of white-collar roles.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: Many risk and compliance professionals leave their field at above-average rates, transitioning to different roles or industries. This trend can benefit organizations by spreading risk management skills and best practices across different sectors, but it raises questions about the sustainability of the field.
pages.title: Workers who started in risk and compliance left the field at above-average rates.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: Companies can enhance employee value in risk and compliance by articulating purpose, redesigning roles, providing learning pathways, and involving cross-functional initiatives. This approach helps attract and retain talent, especially in a volatile world where risk management is vital.
pages.title: Companies can create a stronger employee value proposition in risk and compliance

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the evolving nature of risk management careers, emphasizing the need for reassessment of compensation as companies expand their risk teams. It highlights the opportunity for companies to elevate the risk management function, drawing parallels with the transformation of technology professionals from back-office roles to central corporate figures. The authors advocate for risk management to permeate the broader organization, informing operations and strategy, and stress the importance of professional growth in tandem with the field.
pages.title: Risk Management and Talent in a Volatile World

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_31.jpg
pages.title: Survival through purpose: How Ukrainian businesses endured amid extreme uncertainty

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_32.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the resilience of Ukrainian businesses during Russia's invasion, highlighting their ability to survive and thrive in difficult situations. It details the impact of the invasion on businesses, including disruptions to energy infrastructure and fuel supply chains. A case study of Nova Poshta illustrates the company's efforts to maintain operations and adapt to the crisis.
pages.title: Impact of the invasion on Ukrainian businesses

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: The war has significantly impacted Ukrainian businesses, with 63% experiencing significant operational challenges but not suspending operations. Sales have been deeply affected, with 19% of companies losing over 50% of revenue. However, 15% of businesses reported positive momentum, particularly in transportation and banking sectors.
pages.title: The impact of the war has varied across Ukrainian businesses.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges faced by Ukrainian businesses during the war, including decreased demand, physical damage, and disrupted supply chains. It highlights the initial surprise of business leaders and their responses to these challenges.
pages.title: How Ukrainian business responded, and what worked well

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how Ukrainian businesses responded to the invasion by focusing on employee safety and purpose, maintaining operations despite physical damage, and shifting to a wartime operating model. It highlights the importance of values and communication in retaining employees and ensuring business continuity.
pages.title: Survival through purpose: How Ukrainian businesses endured amid extreme uncertainty

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: Businesses in Ukraine found an agile operating model crucial for navigating wartime challenges. Key techniques included agile decision-making, strong corporate culture, professional resilience planning, leadership commitment, and business diversification strategies.
pages.title: Businesses in Ukraine view an agile operating model as the most helpful factor in navigating the war.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: Ukrainian companies leveraged contingency plans and risk mitigation strategies, emphasizing diversification and personal leadership to navigate the war's challenges. They focused on supply chain and revenue source diversification, and leaders prioritized presence and communication to maintain employee morale and operational continuity.
pages.title: Leveraging contingency plans and risk mitigation strategies

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: Businesses in Ukraine prioritize diversification and resilience post-war, focusing on investment in diversification, scenario planning, and building a resilient workforce. They aim to maintain momentum and adapt to prolonged conflict challenges.
pages.title: Going forward, businesses in Ukraine see diversification of supply chain and revenue sources as a key priority.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the resilience of Ukrainian businesses amid extreme uncertainty, emphasizing the importance of revenue diversification and workforce resilience. It highlights the tools and strategies used by Ukrainian businesses and their potential insights for global enterprises. The page also acknowledges the contributions of various authors and consultants.
pages.title: Survival through purpose: How Ukrainian businesses endured amid extreme uncertainty

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_40.jpg
pages.title: Addressing climate risk and sustainability

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_41.jpg
pages.title: Managing financed emissions: How banks can support the net-zero transition

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_42.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses banks' commitments to reduce financed emissions, complexities in setting targets, and a six-step process for effective emissions baselining and target setting, emphasizing the importance of a robust baseline and aligning with net-zero pathways.
pages.title: Plans to reduce financed emissions should follow a six-step process.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the criteria for building a robust emissions baseline for banks, including sector coverage, asset class coverage, value chain components, greenhouse gases, and scope of emissions. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing heavy-emitting sectors, aligning with international standards, and capturing a comprehensive view of the portfolio for climate commitment.
pages.title: Building a robust emissions baseline

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_44.jpg
library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of derisking momentum cases in banks' decarbonization strategies, involving sector expertise, realistic trajectory assessments, technology understanding, and government policy analysis. It emphasizes the need for reliable momentum cases to bridge the gap to net-zero targets and align portfolios with the Paris Agreement.
pages.title: A good momentum case needs to be derisked and account for realistic assessments of how quickly a sector or large counterparties will decarbonize.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of selecting a reference scenario for achieving Paris alignment, considering temperature ambition, core scenarios, and scenario expansion. It emphasizes the need for banks to assess feasibility, understand business implications, and involve business and risk leadership in the process.
pages.title: Step 4: Determining whether and how to achieve the pathway and capture opportunities

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses scenario analysis for evaluating business implications of net-zero targets, presenting transition trajectories and bank responses. It emphasizes identifying execution levers, growth opportunities, and capabilities for decarbonization technologies to support the net-zero transition.
pages.title: Scenario analysis can show the range of potential outcomes when evaluating business implications of a given net-zero target.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses setting financed emissions targets based on reference scenarios, emphasizing the use of carbon credits, metrics for financed emissions, and granularity in target setting. It also outlines alternative approaches to portfolio alignment, including binary target measurement, benchmark divergence, implied temperature rise, and maturity scale alignment metrics.
pages.title: Step 5: Setting a financed emissions target (if desired), based on the reference scenario

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_49.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for banks to integrate net-zero commitments into their operations, emphasizing the importance of embedding targets into credit policies, data, and incentives. It highlights the need for credible reporting, balance sheet optimization, sectoral leadership, board involvement, and acquiring climate expertise to achieve decarbonization goals.
pages.title: Step 6: Embedding execution and opportunity creation into the bank

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_50.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for banks to manage climate data and engage clients in sustainability efforts. It emphasizes the importance of sourcing accurate emissions data, defining data roles, and building targeted data assets. Banks are encouraged to develop client-level account plans and support decarbonization efforts, positioning themselves as leaders in the transition to a lower-carbon economy.
pages.title: Get and manage climate data, Build client engagement

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_51.jpg
library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_52.jpg
library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_53.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges and opportunities in shaping a resilient sustainability strategy, focusing on affordability, governance, and energy independence. It highlights the trade-offs between climate mitigation and adaptation, the impact of global crises on energy and food prices, and the need for companies to navigate short-term shocks while pursuing long-term net-zero goals. The text emphasizes the importance of diversifying energy sources, improving energy efficiency, and fostering national competitiveness in clean energy technologies.
pages.title: Shaping a resilient sustainability strategy

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_54.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses new value from existing systems, sustainable materials transition, new sources of capital, voluntary carbon market development, and reshaped value chains and reindustrialized nations. It highlights the potential for repurposing carbon-intensive production methods, the need for a materials transition in the energy sector, the rise of new capital sources for net-zero investments, the importance of voluntary carbon markets, and the reshaping of value chains through policy support and reindustrialization efforts.
pages.title: New value from existing systems, Sustainable materials transition, New sources of capital, Voluntary carbon market (VCM) development, Reshaped value chains and reindustrialized nations

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_55.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for CEOs to build resilience and create value through sustainability. It highlights the importance of renewable energy, sustainable materials, and capital deployment with a private-equity mindset. It also emphasizes the need for companies to decarbonize their core business and build new sustainable businesses in reshaped value chains.
pages.title: Resilience today and value tomorrow: Five actions for CEOs

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_56.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses eleven high-potential value pools expected to generate over $12 trillion in yearly revenues by 2030, driven by the net-zero transition. It outlines addressable market sizes across various sectors like industrials, hydrogen, agriculture, water, buildings, carbon management, waste, oil and gas, consumer goods, power, and transport. The text emphasizes the importance of resilience, value creation, and going beyond net zero to achieve net nature positive goals.
pages.title: Eleven high-potential value pools could be worth more than $12 trillion of yearly revenues by 2030 as the net-zero transition advances.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_57.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges CEOs face in balancing sustainability goals with resilience, emphasizing the need for innovation, partnerships, and reskilling. It highlights the importance of public-private collaborations, clean-fuel consortiums, and shared tech road maps. The text also stresses the need for companies to rethink their processes and acquire new skills for sustainable business models.
pages.title: A devilish duality: How CEOs can square resilience with net-zero promises

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_58.jpg
pages.title: Managing risk in uncertainty

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_59.jpg
pages.abstract: This page introduces a technology survival guide for resilience, emphasizing the importance of understanding business process criticality, technology capability, business impact of technology failure, and organizational risk tolerance.
pages.title: A technology survival guide for resilience

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_60.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of resilient technology in maintaining uninterrupted services for customers and organizations during peak times. It highlights the challenges of technology constraints and the need for resilient infrastructure with heightened visibility and transparency. The page also covers the criticality of understanding resilience, evaluating technology, and recognizing business impact. It includes survey data on technology resilience and emphasizes the need for resilient architecture and design, as well as deployment and operations.
pages.title: Understanding criticality

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_61.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines five principles for maintaining resilient technology, emphasizing flexibility, visibility, agility, resilience by design, and interoperability. It also discusses four levels of technology resilience maturity, from basic capabilities to inherent resilience by design, highlighting the importance of monitoring, validation, response, and recovery.
pages.title: McKinsey technology resilience principles

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_62.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the evolution of technology resilience from ad hoc and passive approaches to active and inherent resilience. It outlines four levels of resilience capabilities, from foundational to advanced, emphasizing the importance of centralized backup solutions, redundancy, and proactive monitoring. The text highlights the transition from manual backups and user-based monitoring to automated failover tests and inherent system design for critical applications.
pages.title: A technology resilience journey is one of evolving complexity and maturity.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_63.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the keys to establishing a resilient technology environment, including a blame-free culture, metric-driven approach, and rehearsing outages. It also highlights the importance of prioritizing critical services and understanding the underlying technology landscape for building technology resilience.
pages.title: How to become resilient

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_64.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how a European bank, an Asian fintech, and an oil and gas company are working toward technology resilience. The European bank is leveraging the cloud for out-of-region recovery and flexible scaling, while the Asian fintech is enhancing its cloud infrastructure for continuous service delivery. The oil and gas company is implementing a holistic cybersecurity transformation to protect critical assets. The page also highlights the importance of assessing current resilience levels and reviewing past crises to improve technology resilience.
pages.title: A European bank works toward technology resilience

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_65.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for enhancing technology resilience, including assessing past incidents, identifying common factors, and implementing cross-functional approaches. It emphasizes the importance of clear ownership, governance, and regular testing to ensure system resilience.
pages.title: Remediate gaps through cross-functional approach

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_66.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of failover testing for business-critical applications and outlines a three-step journey to technology resilience, including technology resilience diagnostic and conducting an incident retrospective. It also presents survey results on failover scenarios tested by organizations.
pages.title: The journey to technology resilience in three steps

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_67.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses survey results on unplanned failover testing, showing that most respondents do not perform random testing. It emphasizes the importance of developing a resilient technology architecture and ongoing processes for achieving and maintaining resilience.
pages.title: More than half of survey respondents say they do not perform random failover testing, while only one in five tests all applications.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_68.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the increasing direct losses from operational-risk failures and highlights the significant impact on share prices in today's volatile economic environment. It introduces the topic of response and resilience in operational-risk events, authored by Hugh Dang, Merlina Manocaran, Scott Murff, and Olivia White.
pages.title: Response and resilience in operational-risk events

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_69.jpg
pages.abstract: Operational-risk events cause significant financial and reputational damage, with long-term effects on shareholder returns. Share prices initially decline, and total shareholder returns continue to fall over time, resulting in substantial losses beyond the immediate financial impact.
pages.title: The impact of operational-risk events on shareholder returns deepens in the ensuing weeks.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_70.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how operational-risk events impact shareholder returns differently based on event type. Improper practices lead to gradual market reactions, while suitability, fiduciary, and disclosure violations cause faster declines. European markets react more strongly and faster than North American markets, with shareholder losses exceeding reported losses over time.
pages.title: The impact of operational-risk events on shareholder returns varies over time according to the type of event.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_71.jpg
pages.abstract: Operational-risk events significantly impact shareholder returns, with European companies experiencing greater negative effects compared to North American companies. Financial institutions face harsher market reactions, with a 4% decline in TSR for financial firms versus a 1% decline for nonfinancial firms. Volatile markets exacerbate these effects, leading to larger drops in share prices for affected companies.
pages.title: The impact of operational-risk events on shareholder returns is greater for European versus North American companies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_72.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the methodology used to analyze the impact of operational-risk events on share prices between 2006 and 2020. It details the criteria for selecting events, the geographical and sectoral distribution, and the calculation of abnormal returns. It also explores alternative methodologies for measuring impact and highlights the importance of considering market forces and industry dynamics in crisis planning.
pages.title: Methodology

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_73.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the impact of operational-risk events on shareholder returns, showing that financial institutions in North America and Europe experience greater negative effects compared to nonfinancial companies. Graphs illustrate shareholder returns relative to peers before and after risk events, highlighting significant declines. The text advises firms to be aware of the magnified effect of operational-risk losses on shareholder value during market uncertainty.
pages.title: The effect of operational-risk events on shareholder returns is greater for financial institutions than other types of firms in North America and Europe.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_74.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses how operational-risk events impact shareholder returns, influenced by market volatility. It highlights the need for organizations to develop robust monitoring and response capabilities, manage stakeholders proactively, and communicate effectively to mitigate negative effects on market value.
pages.title: The outcome of operational-risk events on shareholder returns can be affected by market volatility.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_75.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges banks face with Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) due to rate resets. It highlights the importance of focusing on six key areas to manage rising interest rates and credit spread risk effectively, meet regulatory requirements, and gain a competitive edge.
pages.title: Rate reset presents banks with IRRBB challenge

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_76.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges banks face due to rising interest rates, including increased uncertainty in customer behavior and regulatory risks. It highlights the European Banking Authority's new guidelines for interest rate risk in the banking book and the key drivers of interest rate risk, such as balance sheet exposure, yield curve scenarios, and behavioral adjustments.
pages.title: Rising interest rates and their impact on banks

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_77.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the evolving methods for measuring IRRBB risk, focusing on the new supervisory outlier test that assesses the impact of shocks on NII. It highlights the challenges banks face with the new methodology and the importance of balancing delta EVE and delta NII. The text also outlines best practices for deposit modeling and hedging, emphasizing customer segmentation and core balance modeling.
pages.title: IRRBB's new definition of risk to net interest income

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_78.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses best practices for managing deposit and mortgage risks, including deposit volume modeling, deposit beta, hedging strategies, and advanced analytics. It also covers prepayment behavior, interest rate scenarios, hedging ratios, pricing, and credit spread risk in the banking book.
pages.title: Best Practices for Managing Deposit and Mortgage Risks

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_79.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the complexities of credit spread volatility and its correlation with credit ratings, emphasizing that higher-rated companies can be more volatile. It highlights the importance of considering both market credit and liquidity spreads in risk management. The text also addresses the challenges banks face in implementing CSRBB and IRRBB rules, suggesting strategic changes and a focus on governance, organization, and processes.
pages.title: It is not always the case that credit spread volatility is directly correlated to credit rating, and higher-rated companies are often more volatile.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_80.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the increasing focus on credit spread risk in the banking book, outlining the scope of CSRBB and its application to various financial instruments. It emphasizes the importance of integrating credit spreads into the steering process, using advanced analytics, and refining behavioral models to manage changes in NII effectively.
pages.title: Credit spread risk in the banking book is increasingly in focus.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_81.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines six key areas for banks to manage interest rate risk, including supervisory outlier tests, business and hedging strategies, credit spread risk, and reporting frameworks. Effective management in these areas helps banks gauge the impact of rising interest rates, meet regulatory expectations, and gain competitive advantage.
pages.title: Rate reset presents banks with IRRBB challenge

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_82.jpg
pages.title: Navigating economic uncertainty: New guidance for credit risk management

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_83.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges banks face in navigating economic uncertainty and the need for new approaches in credit risk management. It highlights five imperatives for banks to sharpen their credit risk management capabilities, including creating scenarios, revisiting risk limits, developing new metrics, prebaking action menus, and enabling flexible execution. It also emphasizes the importance of cultivating the ability to simulate impacts on portfolios and obligors across multiple scenarios.
pages.title: Navigating economic uncertainty: New guidance for credit risk management

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_84.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how banks use forward-looking credit assessment to identify microsegments of borrowers that respond differently to stress. It explains the process of reconstructing financial profiles, applying macroeconomic drivers, and creating microsegments. The content highlights the importance of automated platforms for scenario analysis and the need to refine risk limits and triggers in response to current economic conditions.
pages.title: Forward-looking assessment of borrowers can identify microsegments with differing responses to stress.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_85.jpg
pages.abstract: Banks must reassess through-the-cycle portfolio behavior in higher rate environments, reevaluate risk limits, and develop forward-looking metrics to better predict risks and opportunities in a volatile world.
pages.title: The reasonable assumption is that through-the-cycle portfolio behavior may significantly change, so banks need to revisit these views of client performance in a higher rate environment.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_86.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses structured, forward-looking credit assessment methods for industry risk rankings. It highlights the importance of periodic trend reviews, scenario modeling for large obligors, and the use of continuous monitoring tools. The page also introduces the concept of 'prebaked' management levers to enhance preparedness in uncertain times.
pages.title: Structured, forward-looking and fundamentals-driven credit assessment can inform industry risk rankings.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_87.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the development of early-warning signals at industry and obligor levels by combining multiple data sources. It introduces a continuous-monitoring dashboard structure and emphasizes the importance of agile decision-making through cross-functional collaboration and flatter hierarchies for effective credit risk management.
pages.title: Early-warning signals can be developed at industry and obligor level, combining multiple data sources.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_88.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the transformation route for banks in managing credit risk amidst economic complexity. It emphasizes the need for real-time interaction, structured evaluation of capabilities, and the use of digital tools like machine learning. The text highlights the importance of revisiting current approaches and enhancing data and forecasting capabilities to navigate uncertainties effectively.
pages.title: The route to transformation

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_89.jpg
pages.title: The evolution of risk organizations

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_90.jpg
pages.abstract: This article discusses the strategic and resilience-building role of risk management in financial institutions, as highlighted by chief risk officers. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and addressing risks amid ongoing crises and disruptions.
pages.title: Risk and resilience priorities, as told by chief risk officers

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_91.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the evolving context and priorities of risk management in banks, highlighting the perspectives of chief risk officers. It covers the impact of various crises on the banking environment, the importance of climate change and cybercrime, and the role of digital transformation and nontraditional competitors in shaping the future of financial services.
pages.title: Risk and resilience priorities, as told by chief risk officers

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_92.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses major risks faced by banks, highlighting direct financial impact, customer harm, and reputational damage as top concerns. Cyber, data, and technology risks, along with climate risk, are seen as rising in importance. Poor data quality is a significant concern, and regulatory agendas consume most of the CROs' time. Organizations are moving towards resilience to handle disruptions effectively.
pages.title: More on the major risks banks face

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_93.jpg
pages.abstract: Risk management is evolving with a focus on resilience, foresight tools, and digital transformation. CROs are addressing over-the-horizon risks through scenario-based planning and sophisticated risk identification. The three-lines-of-defense model is adapting, with the first line becoming more proficient in risk management and the second line focusing on new risk types. Digitization, including AI, is enhancing risk monitoring and decision-making.
pages.title: Where is risk management going?

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_94.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses regulatory expectations and market shifts in risk management, highlighting the impact of poor data quality, the need for digital improvements, and the emergence of new regulatory areas like AMLA and ESG. It also addresses cost pressures and shifting risk priorities in the financial industry.
pages.title: Regulatory expectations and market shifts in risk management

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_95.jpg
pages.abstract: This section discusses the evolving role of risk functions in banks, emphasizing value creation, digital transformation, and strategic resilience. It highlights the need for strong analytics, data control, and upskilling, while embracing fintech partnerships. CROs are prioritizing long-term efforts in digital innovation, talent acquisition, and regulatory expertise to navigate economic crises and foster growth.
pages.title: Creating and demonstrating value as a risk function

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_96.jpg
pages.abstract: The article discusses the evolving role of risk functions in the financial services industry amid increasing global risks and economic uncertainty. It emphasizes the need to develop talent to ensure organizational resilience. The collaborative effort represents views from McKinsey's Risk & Resilience Practice.
pages.title: The next frontier in risk efficiency

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_97.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges faced by Chief Risk Officers (CROs) in the financial services industry regarding resource allocation for risk management. It highlights the need for CROs to balance efficiency and regulatory pressures, and presents findings from a McKinsey survey on risk function resourcing levels. The survey reveals variations in risk FTE intensity among banks and suggests that rightsizing the risk function requires granular comparisons and consideration of various factors.
pages.title: Chief risk officers (CROs) in the financial-services industry are taking a hard look at their resourcing levels.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_98.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the allocation of resources for individual risks within banks, focusing on credit risk management, market risk, operational risk, and model risk management. It highlights the decrease in credit risk FTEs due to automation and the rise in model risk management resources due to regulatory requirements. The exhibit illustrates the FTE intensity by risk area, showing credit risk consumes the most resources.
pages.title: Allotting resources for individual risks

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_99.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the allocation of risk resources in banks, highlighting the varying percentages dedicated to transversal risk teams and shared service centers. It emphasizes the need for competence in new risk types and the reshaping of risk functions through organizational levers like refocusing LOD2 responsibilities and balancing resources.
pages.title: Some banks devote less than 10 percent of their risk resources to transversal risk teams and shared service centers, while others allocate more than 50 percent.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_100.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the alignment of credit risk full-time employees with business units or geographies, even in banks with global functions. It highlights the management of various risk areas, such as market risk, regulatory relations, and liquidity risk, and the limited use of near- and offshoring by banks. The median allocation for banks with significant offshoring is 33 percent, with strategies focusing on offshoring manual work processes.
pages.title: Credit risk full-time employees are almost fully aligned on business units or geographies, even for banks that rely on global functions in other areas.

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_101.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for building an efficient and effective risk function in banks, emphasizing strong risk culture, best-in-class credit underwriting, digital monitoring, automated risk reporting, improved financial crime processes, aligned risk architecture, agile governance, performance management, and model development strategies.
pages.title: Building an efficient and effective risk function

pages.page_path: library_pages\McKinsey on Risk_ Resilience for sustainable, inclusive growth_2023_06_14\page_102.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the shift of CROs towards improving efficiency in risk management, highlighting the potential for cost reduction and increased effectiveness through structured risk transformation programs and advanced tools.
pages.title: Improving Efficiency in Risk Management
