pages.abstract: The McKinsey Global Institute (MGI) conducts independent research on global economic trends, combining economics and management insights. It covers over 20 countries and 30 industries, focusing on themes like growth, labor markets, and technology. Led by senior partners and advised by leading economists, MGI aims to inform business and policy leaders about economic transformations.
pages.title: McKinsey Global Institute

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_3.jpg
pages.title: Securing Europe's competitiveness

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_4.jpg
pages.abstract: The preface highlights the importance of technology in Europe's competitiveness, growth, and strategic autonomy amidst global challenges. It discusses Europe's technological and corporate competitiveness crisis and proposes actions for improvement. The report analyzes European corporations' performance, identifies underperformance compared to US counterparts, and suggests leveraging Europe's scale for better response to disruptions.
pages.title: Preface

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_5.jpg
pages.title: Acknowledgments and Contributors

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_6.jpg
pages.title: Modern Office Interior

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_7.jpg
pages.title: Contents

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe faces a corporate and technological gap, lagging behind in profitability, growth, and innovation compared to its international peers. It is falling behind in eight of ten transversal technologies, particularly in digitization and AI. To address this, Europe needs to be proactive in favor of speed and scale, level the playing field, and consider initiatives like joint procurement and fast-track regulatory approval. Despite challenges, Europe has strengths in sustainability, inclusion, and high-quality education.
pages.title: Addressing Europe’s corporate and technology gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe's corporations underperformed US counterparts in 2014-19 due to tech gaps. Europe holds strong positions in automotive, pharma, and defense but is technologically outpaced. The value at stake is €2-4 trillion annually to 2040. Europe needs to play at full scale, increase speed, and level the playing field.
pages.title: Europe’s corporate and technology gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_10.jpg
pages.title: Autumn Gathering by the Canal

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe leads in sustainable growth, with faster carbon emission reductions and renewable energy adoption compared to the US and China, contributing to global climate action and economic inclusivity.
pages.title: When Europe works, it works well

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe leads in sustainability and inclusion metrics but faces challenges in macroeconomic growth. It excels in low CO2 emissions, income equality, and social progress but lags in GDP growth and debt levels compared to OECD countries.
pages.title: Europe has been a leader on sustainability and inclusion, but the trajectory of macroeconomic growth is a concern.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: The page shows that European CO2 emissions per $ million of GDP and per capita are lower than in other major regions and declining faster. The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of CO2 emissions in Europe is significantly lower compared to other regions. This collective scale has worked in Europe’s favor in terms of reducing emissions.
pages.title: European CO2 emissions are lower than in other major regions and declining faster.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe leads in inclusion and social progress, with Northern and Continental Europe excelling. Europe has lower income inequality, higher gender equality, and the highest life expectancy globally. European countries rank high in well-being, health, and life satisfaction. Social mobility is also stronger in several European economies compared to the United States.
pages.title: Inclusion and social progress: Northern and Continental Europe lead on most dimensions

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: This page illustrates Europe's global leadership in social progress, highlighting dimensions like personal safety, health, and environmental quality. It compares Europe's top 5 countries and its 5 largest countries with the United States and China, showcasing Europe's significant advantages in various social indicators.
pages.title: Europe is a global leader on social progress, reflecting personal safety, health, and quality of the environment.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents data from the World Happiness Report, highlighting that life satisfaction is highest in Northern and Continental Europe, with countries like Finland, Denmark, and Switzerland leading. The United States ranks 18th, and China ranks 94th. The European average life satisfaction is 6.4, while Eastern and Southern Europe have lower scores.
pages.title: Life satisfaction is the highest in Northern and Continental Europe.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents data on income mobility across generations in various countries, highlighting that Northern European countries have the highest income mobility. It shows the number of generations required for low-income families to reach mean income levels, with Denmark having the lowest number (2 generations) and Colombia the highest (11 generations).
pages.title: Differences within regions persist, but Northern European countries have the highest income mobility across generations.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe's GDP growth was more dynamic than the US on a per capita basis between 1970 and 2010, driven by convergence of Central and Eastern European economies and the Single Market. However, European GDP growth slowed between 2010 and 2020, falling behind the US due to policy differences and the euro crisis. Europe's per capita GDP remains lower than the US.
pages.title: Europe has tracked major advanced economies on growth and prosperity

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses Europe's GDP growth decline post-euro crisis, comparing per capita and total GDP trends with the US and China. It highlights societal and lifestyle choices as key factors in Europe's persistent GDP gap with the US.
pages.title: The pace of Europe’s GDP growth dropped after the euro crisis in per capita and total terms.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: This page compares per capita GDP between US states and European countries, showing that most US states have higher GDP than European countries. It discusses factors like societal choices and regional divides contributing to the GDP gap.
pages.title: Most US states have higher per capita GDP than most European countries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the per capita GDP gap between Europe 30 and the United States, highlighting that 40% of this gap is due to labor market choices. It also emphasizes Europe's collaboration across countries, which has supported its strong performance in sustainability, inclusion, and growth. Key initiatives include the European Green Deal, Fit for 55 package, and Horizon Europe program. Additionally, it mentions the impact of European direct investment and labor mobility on less prosperous regions and the creation of world-competitive companies.
pages.title: 40 percent of the per capita GDP gap with the United States reflects labor market choices.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe excels in education, trade openness, and lower national debt. Eleven European countries rank in the top 20 on PISA scores, and Europe hosts 43% of the world's top 100 universities for life sciences. Europe's trade openness is higher than the United States, with exports accounting for 10.9% of GDP. Europe has sophisticated industrial supply chains and lower public and private debt as a share of GDP. However, Europe's future growth is uncertain due to underperforming companies compared to the United States.
pages.title: European countries in the top 20 on PISA scores

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_23.jpg
pages.title: Europe Map with Circuit Design

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_24.jpg
pages.title: 科学家观察样本

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe's tech-driven corporate gap is widening due to underinvestment in R&D and ICT, making it vulnerable in competitiveness. The potential loss of €2-4 trillion in corporate value by 2040 highlights the need for Europe to address its technology gap to maintain economic growth, sustainability, and strategic autonomy.
pages.title: 2. Europe’s tech-driven corporate gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: This page analyzes corporate data from McKinsey's CPAanalytics database, focusing on companies in Europe and the US. It excludes certain companies based on reporting criteria and includes subsidiaries and state-owned firms with commercial remits. The analysis compares R&D intensity and investment in intangible assets between the US and Europe, highlighting differences in technology sectors and enterprise value. The page also discusses the impact of geopolitical events on market valuations.
pages.title: Corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: The document compares Europe and the US in profitability, growth, investment, and R&D, showing Europe lagging behind. Recent data indicates Europe's tech industry growth, with increased unicorns and venture capital funding, but capital investment remains lower. Europe's rising share of small-scale funding rounds suggests future potential, and US venture capital funds are increasingly participating in Europe.
pages.title: Corporate Europe lags behind US counterparts in aggregate on profitability, growth, investment, and R&D.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: The page compares the performance of European and US companies in terms of ROIC, growth, investment, and R&D. European companies lag behind their US counterparts, with tech-creating industries accounting for a significant portion of the gap. European companies have lower ROIC, slower growth, lower investment, and less R&D spending compared to US companies.
pages.title: Corporate Europe’s performance is not on a par with that of US counterparts, largely because of tech-creating industries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: The document compares the growth of US and European corporate values, highlighting that US values have risen strongly while European values have fallen behind. It details the performance of various sectors and notes differences in metrics like ROIC, revenue growth, and R&D investment between European and US companies.
pages.title: US corporate values are rising strongly, while European company valuations are falling behind.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: This page provides a sector deep dive comparing Europe 30 and the United States across various industries. It includes metrics such as ROIC, growth, investment, and R&D spending, highlighting differences in performance and trends between 2014 and 2019.
pages.title: Sector deep dive (1/2).

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_31.jpg
pages.abstract: This page provides a detailed comparison of various sectors' performance metrics between Europe and the United States from 2014 to 2019. It includes ROIC, growth, investment, and R&D spending, highlighting significant differences and trends across sectors such as consumer goods, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, materials, energy, utilities, and transportation.
pages.title: Sector deep dive (2/2).

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_32.jpg
pages.abstract: The text discusses the impact of technology on various sectors, emphasizing the shift towards horizontal competitive dynamics and the increasing importance of digital transformation. It highlights the widening gap between leading and lagging companies in terms of economic profit, with superstar firms capturing a disproportionate share. Europe's position relative to global leaders in key technologies is analyzed, revealing that it leads in only two out of ten critical areas.
pages.title: As technology permeates sectors and scale advantages and winner-takes-most dynamics rise, Europe’s approach may not be sustainable

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines over 60 future areas of competition across various sectors and technologies, including next-level process automation, future of connectivity, distributed infrastructure, next-generation computing, applied AI, future of programming, trust architecture, bio revolution, next-generation materials, and future of cleantech. Each sector is detailed with specific innovations and applications.
pages.title: There are over 60 future areas of competition at the intersection of transversal technologies and sectors.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: The document compares the share of world-class patents in frontier technologies between Europe and the United States in 2019. It highlights that the US generates more patents in various technologies, including next-level automation, future of connectivity, and bio revolution. The lack of scale in transversal technologies is identified as a risk for Europe's position across sectors, including automotive and luxury goods. Europe is lagging in areas such as electric vehicles, autonomous vehicles, wearable devices, and online retail platforms.
pages.title: The United States generates more world-class patents than Europe in transversal technologies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: This page compares Europe's position in ten transversal technologies against leading or second-best regions. Europe leads in next-generation materials and future of cleantech, while trailing in others like distributed infrastructure and future of programming. The metrics include innovation, production, and adoption, with Europe showing an average ratio of 0.6, 0.6, and 0.7 respectively.
pages.title: Out of ten transversal technologies, such as AI, quantum computing, and cloud, Europe leads on two.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe lags behind other major regions in various transversal technologies, affecting its performance in traditional sectors. European companies face challenges in scale and strategic control compared to their US counterparts, with lower market-to-book ratios and book equity levels.
pages.title: A snapshot of Europe’s position relative to other major regions in ten transversal technologies largely reveals lags.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: This page illustrates the change in market capitalization of top European and US firms across various sectors from 2000 to 2019, showing which sectors have strengthened, weakened, or remained unchanged in Europe's position compared to the US.
pages.title: Markets have already embedded the gap across sectors.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: The page compares market-to-book ratios and book equity between US and European companies across various industries in 2019, highlighting a significant difference in favor of US companies. It also notes a shift in the dominance of European brands in the US premium car market to electric vehicles.
pages.title: US companies' market-to-book ratios are almost double and equity is nearly 30 percent higher than those of European counterparts.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the significant value at stake for Europe in terms of growth, sustainability, and inclusion. It highlights the potential economic impact of failing to improve transversal technologies, estimating a missed opportunity of €2 to €4 trillion annually by 2040. The value at stake is equivalent to 30-70% of Europe's forecast GDP growth between 2019 and 2040, six times the annual cost of the net-zero transition, and close to annual social expenditure. The document emphasizes the importance of growth for creating new income streams and a healthy investment climate, while also addressing the need for sustainability and inclusion.
pages.title: The value at stake is high, not only for growth but also for sustainability, inclusion, and Europe's strategic autonomy

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_40.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses methodologies to estimate the value at stake for Europe, ranging from €2 trillion to €7 trillion in corporate value added by 2040. It analyzes market valuations, forecast market sizes of transversal technologies, and the economic impact of technology adoption, considering Europe's 23% share of global GDP.
pages.title: Value at stake—methodology

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_41.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the need for Europe to achieve strategic autonomy in critical technologies amidst a polarized geopolitical environment. It highlights the current low production and market share of European companies in semiconductors and infrastructure as a service (IaaS). The text also points out the vulnerability of Europe due to lagging tech-creating industries and the importance of addressing the technology gap for sustainable and inclusive growth.
pages.title: A shifting geopolitical environment that is increasingly polarized accentuates the need for strategic autonomy on critical technologies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_42.jpg
pages.title: Wind Turbines in Agricultural Fields

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: This chapter discusses the sustainable and inclusive growth standings of nine diverse European countries, summarizing their corporate positions. Highlighted countries include France, Germany, Italy, The Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
pages.title: 3. A country-level view

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_44.jpg
pages.abstract: The France scorecard compares France's performance across various sustainability, inclusion, and economic prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. France ranks moderately in CO2 emissions and fossil fuel consumption but performs well in life expectancy and social progress. Economic growth and investment flows are also highlighted.
pages.title: France scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: France leads in sustainability with low CO2 emissions due to nuclear energy but lags in economic growth and corporate performance compared to the US and Europe 30 average. French companies underperform in return on invested capital and R&D intensity despite higher revenue growth.
pages.title: France's sustainability and corporate performance

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: The Germany scorecard compares Germany's performance across various sustainability, inclusion and well-being, and growth and prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. Germany ranks relatively well in life expectancy, social progress, and per capita GDP but faces challenges in income inequality and fossil fuel consumption.
pages.title: Germany scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: Germany excels in inclusion and growth but lags in sustainability. Its per capita CO2 emissions are high, and its emissions reduction targets are at risk due to reliance on coal. Germany's life satisfaction is high, but its per capita GDP growth is lower than the Europe 30 average. Corporate R&D spending is high but does not translate into higher returns on invested capital or revenue growth compared to US counterparts.
pages.title: Germany corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: The Italy scorecard compares Italy's performance across various sustainability, inclusion, and economic metrics with other OECD countries. Key findings include Italy's relatively low CO2 emissions per capita, moderate fossil fuel consumption, and high life expectancy. However, it faces challenges in income inequality, poverty rates, and per capita GDP growth compared to other countries.
pages.title: Italy scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_49.jpg
pages.abstract: Italy performs well on sustainability but lags in inclusion, growth, and prosperity. Corporate Italy is near the Europe 30 average but lags in return on invested capital, revenue growth, and R&D intensity. Italy's R&D spending relative to revenue is significantly lower than the US and Europe 30 average.
pages.title: Italy's performance on sustainability and corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_50.jpg
pages.abstract: The Netherlands scorecard compares the country's performance across various sustainability, inclusion, and economic prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. It highlights the Netherlands' position in decile rankings for CO2 emissions, fossil fuel consumption, income inequality, poverty rate, social mobility, life expectancy, social progress, life satisfaction, GDP, GDP growth, foreign investment, current account balance, public debt, and private debt.
pages.title: Netherlands scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_51.jpg
pages.abstract: The Netherlands has higher per capita GDP and lower CO2 emissions compared to Europe 30 but lower than the US. It performs well on social inclusion and prosperity but lags in corporate performance metrics like ROIC and revenue growth compared to Europe 30 and the US.
pages.title: Netherlands corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_52.jpg
pages.abstract: The Poland scorecard compares various sustainability, inclusion and well-being, and growth and prosperity metrics of Poland with other OECD countries. It highlights Poland's performance in CO2 emissions, fossil fuel consumption, income inequality, poverty rate, social mobility, life expectancy, social progress, life satisfaction, per capita GDP, GDP growth, foreign direct investment, current account balance, public debt, and private debt.
pages.title: Poland scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_53.jpg
pages.abstract: Poland's sustainability position is mixed, with lower per capita carbon emissions than Europe 30 but higher fossil fuel consumption. Income inequality is lower, but poverty rates are higher than the US. Poland's economy lags in per capita GDP but shows rapid growth. Corporate Poland underperforms in return on invested capital but excels in revenue growth and capital expenditure.
pages.title: Poland's position on sustainability is mixed

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_54.jpg
pages.abstract: The Spain scorecard compares Spain's performance across various sustainability, inclusion, and economic prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. It highlights Spain's position in CO2 emissions, fossil fuel consumption, income inequality, life expectancy, GDP growth, and foreign investment flows, among others, providing a comprehensive overview of its socio-economic status.
pages.title: Spain scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_55.jpg
pages.abstract: Spain's corporate performance lags behind Europe 30 and US averages in ROIC and R&D intensity, but shows strong revenue growth, possibly due to recovery from the 2008 economic crisis. Sustainability and solar power usage are strong, but income inequality and poverty rates are high.
pages.title: Spain corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_56.jpg
pages.abstract: The Sweden scorecard compares Sweden's performance across various sustainability, inclusion and well-being, and growth and prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. Sweden ranks well in life expectancy, social mobility, and per capita GDP but faces challenges in CO2 emissions and fossil fuel consumption. The scorecard highlights Sweden's strengths and areas for improvement in economic and social indicators.
pages.title: Sweden scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_57.jpg
pages.abstract: Sweden excels in sustainable growth, inclusion, and corporate performance. Despite challenges in poverty and social exclusion for non-EU citizens, Sweden shows strong economic indicators, including GDP, income inequality, and corporate metrics like ROIC, revenue growth, and R&D intensity, often surpassing EU and US averages.
pages.title: Sweden's Sustainable Growth and Corporate Performance

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_58.jpg
pages.abstract: The Switzerland scorecard compares its performance across sustainability, inclusion and well-being, and growth and prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. Switzerland ranks well in life expectancy, social mobility, and GDP per capita but faces challenges in income inequality and fossil fuel consumption.
pages.title: Switzerland scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_59.jpg
pages.abstract: Switzerland's corporations outperform Europe 30 and US companies in return on invested capital and R&D intensity. Revenue growth is higher, but capital expenditure is lower. Despite high per capita CO2 emissions, Switzerland's domestic production is low, with emissions largely from imported products.
pages.title: Switzerland corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_60.jpg
pages.abstract: The United Kingdom scorecard compares its performance across various sustainability, inclusion, and economic prosperity metrics with other OECD countries. It highlights the UK's position in CO2 emissions, fossil fuel consumption, income inequality, poverty rates, social mobility, life expectancy, GDP growth, and debt levels, providing insights into its relative strengths and weaknesses.
pages.title: United Kingdom scorecard

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_61.jpg
pages.abstract: The United Kingdom's corporate performance is mixed compared to Europe 30, with higher returns on invested capital but weaker revenue growth and R&D intensity. Sustainability metrics are stronger, but income inequality and poverty rates are higher. Growth in per capita GDP lagged behind Europe 30 from 2000 to 2019.
pages.title: United Kingdom corporate analysis

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_62.jpg
pages.title: Technician Operating Industrial Robot

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_63.jpg
pages.abstract: This chapter discusses Europe's lagging position in transversal technologies, analyzing its competitiveness compared to China and the United States. Europe trails in innovation, production, and adoption across eight of ten key technologies, with average factors of 0.6, 0.6, and 0.7 against leading regions. Addressing these gaps is crucial for Europe's future competitiveness and resilience.
pages.title: 4. Europe is falling behind on transversal technologies

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_64.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines ten key transversal technologies crucial for Europe's future competitiveness and prosperity, including next-level automation, future of programming, future of connectivity, trust architecture, distributed infrastructure, bio revolution, next-generation computing, next-gen materials, applied AI, and future of cleantech. It also explains how Europe's factor scores for innovation, production, and adoption are analyzed against the US and China using various metrics.
pages.title: Europe’s future competitiveness and prosperity depend on ten transversal technologies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_65.jpg
pages.abstract: Next-level automation, including robotics and virtualization, is forecast to add €130 billion to the economy by 2040. Europe lags behind in innovation but is strong in production and adoption. Automation can boost productivity and efficiency. Robotics hardware has three segments: industrial robots, professional service robots, and domestic service robots. Cobots are growing fast, and professional service robots are expected to dominate the market by 2025.
pages.title: Next-level automation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_66.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the advancements in robotics and automation, focusing on AMRs, additive manufacturing, and virtualization processes. It highlights Europe's leadership in robotics but notes challenges from the United States in innovation and China in adoption. The page also compares venture capital funding and patent filings in robotics and automation across Europe, the United States, and China.
pages.title: Robotics and automation trends in Europe, the United States, and China

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_67.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe leads in robot production volume and professional service robots but lags in innovation patents and private equity funding. It has a strong market share in service robots and cobots, with European companies like ABB and Kuka playing significant roles. However, it faces competition from the United States and China in venture capital and robot installations.
pages.title: Europe lags behind on some metrics of innovation but leads on several metrics of production and adoption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_68.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the adoption of robots in Europe, the United States, and China, highlighting Europe's leading position in robot density despite heavy use by a small number of companies. It also covers the rapid growth of robot installation in China and the impact of COVID-19 on Europe and the United States. The future of connectivity is explored, focusing on 5G and IoT technologies, their potential to generate economic value, and Europe's lag in innovation and production compared to other regions.
pages.title: 271 robots per 10,000 employees in Europe vs 255 in the United States and 246 in China

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_69.jpg
pages.abstract: China leads in 5G adoption and production market share but lags in knowledge creation. Europe excels in scientific publications, while the US holds more world-class patents. The future of 5G connectivity shows China's dominance in adoption and production, with Europe and the US contributing significantly in different segments.
pages.title: Future of connectivity (5G): China leads on all dimensions except knowledge creation and shares lead with Europe on production market share.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_70.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the global landscape of 5G and IoT technologies, highlighting Europe's lead in scientific publications, the United States' dominance in world-class patents, and China's strength in technical innovations and 5G adoption. It also covers the production dynamics between Europe and China, the shift towards Open RAN standards, and the forecasted 5G penetration rates. Additionally, it compares IoT-related patent filings and revenue generation among regions.
pages.title: Innovation, Production, Adoption, and IoT in 5G and related technologies

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_71.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the future of IoT, highlighting China's leadership in innovation and adoption metrics, the United States' dominance in investment and market share, and Europe's relatively smaller contributions. It provides detailed statistics on patents, capital investment, revenue share, and projected industrial IoT usage, emphasizing the competitive landscape and regional strengths.
pages.title: Future of connectivity (IoT)

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_72.jpg
pages.abstract: Distributed infrastructure, including cloud and edge computing, is crucial for business innovation and optimization. It democratizes computing power, accelerates time to market, and reduces costs. Europe lags behind in adoption, while the US leads globally. Spending on cloud and edge services is expected to grow significantly by 2025.
pages.title: 3. Distributed infrastructure

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_73.jpg
pages.abstract: The United States leads in innovation, production, and adoption of distributed infrastructure. It holds the majority of world-class patents, venture capital funding, and market share in cloud services. The US also dominates private equity and M&A funding, with significant contributions from major tech companies.
pages.title: The United States leads on metrics of innovation, production, and adoption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_74.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the dominance of US companies in cloud services, the lagging adoption of cloud services by European companies, and the potential of next-generation computing, including quantum computing and neuromorphic hardware, to solve complex problems and generate significant economic value.
pages.title: Next-generation computing

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_75.jpg
pages.abstract: Next-generation computing accelerates development cycles and lowers entry barriers across industries. The US and China lead in quantum computing, with China excelling in patents and public investment, the US in private funding, and Europe in publications. Europe is catching up with substantial innovation and investment expected in the coming years.
pages.title: Why does this transversal technology matter?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_76.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the global landscape of quantum computing investment and research, highlighting Europe's lead in publications, China's dominance in patents, and the significant investments by the US and China. It covers the involvement of major tech companies in both countries, the rise of venture capital and startup funding, and the public funding commitments by China, Europe, and the US.
pages.title: Innovation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_77.jpg
pages.abstract: Applied AI, leveraging algorithms for real-world data processing, is poised to generate €1-2 trillion in gross value by 2040. It enhances automation, R&D, and customer service while Europe lags behind in adoption. The global AI market is expected to reach $360 billion by 2028, with the US leading in AI investment and China as a strong competitor. AI's potential economic impact could add $13 trillion to global GDP by 2030.
pages.title: 5. Applied AI

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_78.jpg
pages.abstract: The United States leads in AI innovation and venture capital funding, with a 47% share of world-class patents and $8 billion in funding in 2020. China leads in AI adoption, with a 61% adoption rate in 2021. The US also leads in private investments and public funding, while China has the largest share of peer-reviewed AI publications.
pages.title: The United States leads on some metrics of innovation and production; China leads on adoption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_79.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the significant investment in AI by the United States compared to Europe and China, highlighting the dominance of US tech giants and startups. It also compares AI adoption rates and practical applications across regions, noting China's lead in speech technology and mobile payments. The future of programming is described as 'Software 2.0,' with a growing market for low- and no-code solutions.
pages.title: Production

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_80.jpg
pages.abstract: Software 2.0, through machine-written programs, shifts the focus from coding to designing frameworks for machine learning, exemplified by low/no-code platforms. It enables rapid scaling of AI applications, reduces workforce needs, and accelerates software development. The US leads in innovation and production, with significant venture capital funding and production of low/no-code platforms, while Europe lags behind and China has a minimal presence.
pages.title: Why does this transversal technology matter?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_81.jpg
pages.abstract: The United States leads in innovation investment and production, particularly in venture capital funding for software and low-/no-code platforms. Trust architecture, including blockchain and zero-trust security, enables verifiable data flow and mitigates cyber risk. Europe lags behind in trust architecture adoption. Trust architecture is crucial for verifying information and reducing intermediaries in business transactions.
pages.title: The United States leads on innovation investment and production.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_82.jpg
pages.abstract: The United States leads Europe in innovation, production, and adoption of blockchain and cybersecurity. It has a higher share of world-class patents, venture capital funding, corporate funding, and adoption rate in top companies compared to Europe and China. The U.S. also has a greater need for solutions to improve payment speed and security due to its lack of a standard national ID and large unbanked population.
pages.title: The United States leads on metrics of innovation, production, and adoption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_83.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the United States' leadership in innovation, production, and adoption of blockchain technology, as well as the emerging Bio Revolution. It highlights the U.S.'s dominance in private corporate funding, government funding, and top players in blockchain and cybersecurity. The Bio Revolution, characterized by advancements in biological sciences and computing, is projected to have a significant economic impact across various industries.
pages.title: Innovation, Production, and Adoption in Blockchain and the Bio Revolution

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_84.jpg
pages.abstract: This page compares Europe, the United States, and China in biotech innovation, production, and adoption. Europe leads in scientific publications but lags in patents and funding. The United States excels in patents, funding, and FDA/EMA approvals. China is rapidly catching up in all dimensions. The data highlights the global biotech landscape and regional strengths.
pages.title: Bio Revolution: Europe leads on scientific publications, but the United States leads on production and adoption.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_85.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses Europe's competitiveness in biotech innovation, highlighting its lead in scientific publications and patents, but also noting the widening gap in early-stage funding compared to the United States. It also covers the production and adoption of biotech therapies, emphasizing the United States' dominance in new biotech companies and therapies, while Europe and China are catching up in certain areas.
pages.title: Innovation in Biotech: Europe's Competitiveness

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_86.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses next-generation materials, their innovations, and their impact on various industries. It highlights three subsegments: nanomaterials, composites, and future construction materials. Europe leads in production and adoption, while the US excels in innovation. The page also explains the significance of these materials in reducing carbon footprints and improving efficiency across sectors.
pages.title: 9. Next-generation materials

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_87.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the global nanomaterials market, highlighting that Europe and the United States lead in patents and venture capital spending. Europe excels in corporate investment and adoption, being the largest end market in 2020. The United States has a slight lead in innovation metrics, while Europe leads in production and adoption metrics. The page includes an exhibit summarizing these metrics for Europe, the United States, China, and Asia.
pages.title: Nanomaterials: The United States leads on most indicators, but Europe is strong on funding and patents

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_88.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the production, adoption, and innovation in nanomaterials and composites across Europe, the United States, and China. It highlights Europe's leadership in carbon nanotubes and graphene, the United States' dominance in venture capital investment for carbon fiber startups, and China's strong position in fiber-reinforced polymers. The page also covers the applications of composites in various markets and the competitive landscape among global suppliers.
pages.title: Production, Adoption, and Innovation in Nanomaterials and Composites

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_89.jpg
pages.abstract: The document compares the United States, Europe, and China in next-generation materials, particularly composites. Europe matches the US in innovation and leads in green cement and CLT production. Adoption varies by market, with Europe gaining in green cement due to supportive policies. Europe has a strong presence in CLT production and holds a significant share of the global market.
pages.title: Next-generation materials (composites)

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_90.jpg
pages.abstract: The page compares Europe, the United States, and China in innovation, production, and adoption of next-generation construction materials. Europe leads in production metrics, with the highest number of green cement players and cross-laminated timber production market share. The United States matches Europe in innovation and adoption, with a higher green cement end-market share. Data on China is limited.
pages.title: Next-generation materials (future construction materials)

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_91.jpg
pages.abstract: Cleantech, encompassing established and emerging technologies, is poised to generate significant economic value by 2040. Europe leads in innovation but lags in production, while China dominates production and the US excels in innovation. The EU needs substantial investment in clean technologies to achieve net-zero emissions, with potential cost savings in the long term. The global cleantech market is expected to grow substantially, with renewables projected to dominate energy production by 2050.
pages.title: 10. The future of cleantech

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_92.jpg
pages.abstract: The page compares Europe, the United States, and China in cleantech metrics. Europe leads in innovation and per capita capacity but lags in future cleantech. The data includes patents, production percentages, and adoption rates for solar, wind, and batteries. The US/Europe comparison highlights funding, projects, patents, and innovation in various cleantech sectors.
pages.title: Europe leads on metrics of innovation and per capita capacity but lags on future cleantech.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_93.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses Europe's lead in cleantech innovation, particularly in patents and venture capital investment. It compares the United States and China in various technologies like nuclear fusion, CCUS, smart grids, and batteries. Europe is noted for its strong venture capital investment and public R&D in cleantech, while the United States leads in several breakthrough technologies.
pages.title: Innovation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_94.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the global leadership of Europe and China in various cleantech categories, including wind power, solar manufacturing, hydrogen production, and energy storage. It highlights Europe's growing presence in startups and compares the market shares of top manufacturers in these sectors between Europe, China, and the United States. The page also touches on the fragmented hydrogen market and the inclusion of nuclear fission in the EU taxonomy.
pages.title: European wind power manufacturers in 2020 top ten vs 6 in China and 1 in the United States

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_95.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses China's dominance in battery manufacturing and cleantech supply chain, including raw materials and energy storage. It highlights Europe's and the US's reliance on imports for key materials and their efforts to increase renewable energy share. The text also compares the installed capacity of renewables, public and private investments in low-carbon technology, and the individual types of cleantech between China, Europe, and the US.
pages.title: Securing Europe's competitiveness: Addressing its technology gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_96.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the growth of the electric vehicle and hydrogen markets, highlighting Europe's and China's investments and market shares. It emphasizes Europe's lagging position in key technologies and the need for European decision-makers to consider strategies to enhance competitiveness. It also notes Europe's recent catch-up in the EV market.
pages.title: Until recently, China had the largest EV market

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_97.jpg
pages.title: Global Map with Circuit Design Overlay

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_98.jpg
pages.title: Bridge over a town

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_99.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe faces various impediments to competitiveness, including fragmentation, lack of technology ecosystems, insufficient risk-capital funding, and an unsupportive regulatory environment. These challenges hinder the growth of new companies and attract tech talent, reinforcing each other and creating a less favorable environment for innovation.
pages.title: 5. A range of impediments stand in the way of progress

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_100.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights Europe's critical challenges in tech ecosystems due to fragmentation and lack of scale. It identifies various handicaps across different transversal technologies, emphasizing the need for improvements in areas like funding, talent attraction, and regulatory environments.
pages.title: As economies of scale and scope become more important, Europe’s fragmentation and lack of tech ecosystems become critical.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_101.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses Europe's structural disadvantage due to fragmentation, impacting startups' growth. European companies face smaller domestic markets compared to the US and China, leading to early internationalization. The exhibit highlights GDP disparities and the fragmented nature of the European market.
pages.title: Fragmentation and lack of scale

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_102.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges faced by EU member states in AI due to fragmented digital markets, contrasting it with the concentrated data collection in the US and the scale of China's tech ecosystem. It highlights cybersecurity governance differences in the EU, the fragmented European market for the Bio Revolution, and the lack of established technology ecosystems compared to the US. Europe's impressive ecosystems are noted but fall short of matching the US.
pages.title: Lack of established technology ecosystems

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_103.jpg
pages.abstract: The document compares R&D spending between top US and European tech companies, highlighting a significant disparity. It discusses Europe's lack of first-wave tech companies and clusters, its vulnerability in 5G and cloud markets, and the challenges in AI and next-generation computing due to path dependency and weak ecosystems. The EU is launching new investments to support AI, but these may not be sufficient.
pages.title: Top ten US tech companies spend four times more than Europe’s top ten.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_104.jpg
pages.abstract: This page compares the distribution of startups in Europe and the US based on their headquarters' location in super tech hubs. European startups are less concentrated in top tech hubs compared to US startups. It also highlights the less developed risk-capital funding in Europe due to a conservative capital market structure and lack of angel investor money.
pages.title: Startups in Europe are less concentrated around top tech hubs than those in the United States.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_105.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses reasons for Europe's late entry into venture capital, including less government support, a less active stock market compared to the US, and regulatory challenges. It highlights the need for Europe to scale up public support and address regulatory barriers to foster venture capital activity and innovation.
pages.title: Reasons for Europe's Late Entry into Venture Capital

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_106.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the global regulatory landscape for emerging technologies such as autonomous vehicles, blockchain, biotech, distributed infrastructure, and applied AI. It highlights regional differences in regulation, the impact on innovation and adoption, and the balance between policy objectives like financial stability and consumer protection.
pages.title: Emerging Technologies and Global Regulation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_107.jpg
pages.abstract: The EU's labor market regulation is less business-friendly compared to the US and China, impacting adaptability to digital business models. Europe excels in product-market regulation but falls short in labor policy, tax, and property rights. Flexicurity principles are recommended for better labor reallocation during technological disruption.
pages.title: Labor market flexibility

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_108.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges Europe faces in translating university research into commercial applications compared to China and the United States. It highlights the lower levels of entrepreneurship, less industry experience among EU startup founders, and fragmented R&D investment. The page also addresses the brain drain of European researchers to other countries due to better financial rewards and migration policies.
pages.title: Translation of university research into commercial applications

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_109.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses factors limiting Europe's ability to attract tech talent, such as fewer scale-up companies, lack of stock options, and immigration policies. It also compares STEM graduate rates among regions, highlighting China's high rate and Europe's second place in absolute numbers.
pages.title: The environment for attracting tech and entrepreneurial talent

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_110.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe attracts fewer immigrant inventors and exhibits a more risk-averse business mindset compared to the United States. This affects its position in transversal technologies and entrepreneurial activities, with fewer European adults being entrepreneurs and less positive media portrayal. Risk aversion impacts investment in deep tech, such as quantum computing, and European startups may face more restrictions from public funding compared to traditional venture capital.
pages.title: Risk-averse mindset

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_111.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe lags behind the US and China in digital infrastructure, with lower broadband access and investment. Challenges include limited 5G base stations, cloud market dominance by US companies, and reliance on satellites. Addressing these issues is crucial for Europe's innovation and competitiveness.
pages.title: Digital infrastructure

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_112.jpg
pages.title: Train at Station

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_113.jpg
pages.abstract: Europe must enhance competitiveness and growth by leveraging strengths in education, industrial fabric, and supply chains, while addressing challenges like market fragmentation, lack of scale, and regulatory barriers to achieve greater scale, speed, and a level playing field for its firms.
pages.title: 6. Achieving scale, speed, and a level playing field

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_114.jpg
pages.abstract: The page highlights four key challenges in Europe's tech sector and proposes policy solutions in three areas: scale, level playing field, and speed. These address market fragmentation, lack of tech ecosystems, underdeveloped risk capital, and regulatory barriers, aiming to enhance competitiveness and innovation.
pages.title: Four standout challenges can be addressed through policies in three areas.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_115.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses Europe's efforts to address its corporate performance gap through various initiatives like Horizon Europe and IPCEI. It highlights the need for Europe to reevaluate trade-offs on 11 policy and regulatory initiatives to enable firms to compete at scale and speed. The text emphasizes the importance of increasing resources and supporting cross-border scale-up and consolidation in key tech areas.
pages.title: To help European firms to compete, Europe could reevaluate trade-offs on 11 policy and regulatory initiatives

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_116.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses European initiatives like the Chips Act, Scale-up Europe, Fund of funds, and JEDI to boost tech growth. It highlights the need for regulatory harmonization and a 28th regime for high-growth firms to address cross-border complexities and foster a unified European market.
pages.title: European Initiatives for Tech Growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_117.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the need for cross-border consolidation in Europe, including completing the Single Market, revisiting antitrust rules, and removing political obstacles. It highlights the importance of integrating energy systems, establishing common digital standards, and addressing issues in finance and electronic identity. The page also emphasizes the need for increased European basic research funding, venture capital structures, and changes to pension institutions to support innovation and global competition.
pages.title: Facilitate and encourage cross-border consolidation, including completing the Single Market

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_118.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses pooling public procurement and R&D support in Europe, emphasizing defense and healthcare. It highlights Europe's strengths in research, the need for better integration, and the importance of joint procurement to support innovation and regional focus. The page also addresses the need for increased development and crisis support for less developed European regions.
pages.title: Pool more public procurement and R&D support among a coalition of the willing, including in defense and healthcare

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_119.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the need for Europe to balance precautionary principles with accelerated decision-making and failure tolerance, emphasizing the importance of speed and simplicity in regulatory approaches. It highlights the European Medicines Agency's rapid authorization of COVID-19 vaccines and suggests applying similar speed to innovation areas. The text also proposes rebalancing regulatory approaches to encourage experimentation and innovation while maintaining data privacy and consumer protection. Finally, it advocates for fast-track regulatory approval and decision-making processes to enhance Europe's competitiveness in tech-enabled sectors.
pages.title: Speed and simplicity

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_120.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses embracing faster labor reallocation and reskilling, ensuring a level playing field for smaller firms around natural digital monopolies, and initiating a debate to protect nascent technology-savvy firms. It highlights the need for flexible labor markets, fair behavior of digital gatekeepers, and support for European innovators to compete globally.
pages.title: Embrace faster labor reallocation and reskilling

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_121.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses Europe's need to enhance talent attraction and development to remain competitive in technology-driven markets. It highlights the disparity in attracting immigrant inventors compared to the United States and suggests strategies for European firms to step up, including setting long-term targets, leveraging M&A, and forming cross-sector alliances.
pages.title: Double down on talent as Europe's prime success factor in future markets

pages.page_path: library_pages\Securing Europe’s competitiveness_ Addressing its technology gap_McKinsey_2022_09_01\page_122.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the need for companies to invest in innovation and technology governance, focusing on agile and customer-centric approaches. It highlights Siemens' initiative to upskill and reskill employees in digital capabilities. The text also addresses European countries' leadership in sustainability and inclusion, while raising concerns about corporate and technology gaps, supply chain security, and strategic autonomy. It suggests that the momentum from the war in Ukraine could drive action on technology and competitiveness trade-offs, emphasizing the need for detailed work to address Europe's corporate performance and innovation gaps.
pages.title: Invest in innovation and technology governance and capabilities at scale and pace.

pages.title: Related MGI and McKinsey research
