pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI has the potential to significantly boost global productivity and economic value across various sectors, automate a substantial portion of work activities, and accelerate workforce transformation. However, it requires strategic investments in worker support and skill development to fully realize its benefits.
pages.title: Key insights

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the rise of generative AI, driven by significant investments in machine learning and deep learning. It highlights tools like ChatGPT and AlphaGo, emphasizing their broad utility and the subtle yet pervasive impact of AI on daily life. The latest applications enable tasks like text writing and digital art creation, prompting stakeholders to consider their implications on business and society.
pages.title: Generative AI as a technology catalyst

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the evolution of generative AI, driven by foundation models and deep learning. It highlights the capabilities and challenges of generative AI, including processing large datasets, performing multiple tasks, and the increasing investment in the field. The page also mentions notable advancements like ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Claude, and the geographic concentration of investments in North America.
pages.title: How did we get here? Gradually, then all of a sudden

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_8.jpg
pages.title: Glossary

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: This page explains key concepts in machine learning and AI, including modality, productivity, prompt engineering, self-attention, structured and unstructured data, transformers, technical automation potential, and use cases. It highlights how these concepts contribute to AI's capabilities and applications.
pages.title: Key Concepts in Machine Learning and AI

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI marks a significant evolution in AI. Companies are adapting it quickly, and understanding its value to the economy and society is crucial. Two lenses are used to identify where generative AI can deliver the most significant value and estimate its potential impact.
pages.title: Generative AI use cases across functions and industries

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: The document evaluates the potential impact of generative AI through two lenses: total economic potential of 60-plus organizational use cases and labor productivity potential across 2,100 detailed work activities. It identifies 63 use cases spanning 16 business functions, delivering economic benefits of $2.6 to $4.4 trillion annually. The second lens analyzes AI's impact on 850 occupations and 2,100 work activities, estimating its effect on global workforce productivity.
pages.title: The potential impact of generative AI can be evaluated through two lenses.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the economic benefits of generative AI, estimating a potential annual impact of $6.1 to $7.9 trillion when applied to knowledge workers' activities. It highlights the additional value generative AI can create beyond traditional AI and analytics, with a focus on productivity improvements. A bar chart illustrates the potential economic impact, showing incremental contributions from advanced analytics, new generative AI use cases, and total AI economic potential.
pages.title: Generative AI could create additional value potential above what could be unlocked by other AI and analytics.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: This chapter discusses the value potential of generative AI, emphasizing its expanding capabilities beyond traditional AI applications. It details the methodology used to estimate the value of generative AI use cases, focusing on significant improvements in key outputs and excluding cases where the sole benefit is natural language use. The potential annual value across the economy is estimated, particularly in sales and marketing, based on the 2022 global economy structure.
pages.title: How we estimated the value potential of generative AI use cases

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the value potential of generative AI across various business functions, highlighting that customer operations, marketing and sales, software engineering, and research and development account for about 75% of the total annual value. A scatter plot illustrates the impact of generative AI, showing significant potential in functions like sales, marketing, and software engineering. The page also notes that the potential value for manufacturing and supply chain functions is now lower due to the nature of generative AI use cases.
pages.title: Value potential by function

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can revolutionize internal knowledge management systems, enhancing efficiency and decision-making. It can act as a virtual expert, retrieving information and engaging in dialogue, potentially saving knowledge workers significant time and improving productivity.
pages.title: Generative AI as a virtual expert

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how customer operations can be transformed through customer self-service interactions with chatbots, customer-agent interactions with AI assistance, and agent self-improvement using AI-generated insights.
pages.title: How customer operations could be transformed

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can revolutionize customer operations by enhancing self-service, improving initial contact resolution, reducing response time, and increasing sales. It boosts productivity and quality, especially for less-experienced agents, and can automate up to 50% of human-serviced contacts.
pages.title: Customer operations

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how marketing and sales can be transformed through strategization, awareness, and consideration. Professionals gather data from various sources to create effective communications, while customers receive personalized campaigns and access to dynamic recommendations.
pages.title: How marketing and sales could be transformed

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how generative AI enhances conversion and retention in marketing and sales. Virtual sales representatives build trust through humanlike qualities, while AI-powered chatbots improve customer retention. Generative AI personalizes messages and creates content, but requires careful consideration to avoid risks like plagiarism and biased data.
pages.title: Conversion and Retention in Marketing and Sales

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI offers marketing significant benefits including efficient content creation, enhanced data use, SEO optimization, and personalized product discovery, potentially increasing marketing productivity by 5-15% of total spending.
pages.title: Potential operational benefits from using generative AI for marketing

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can enhance sales productivity by 3-5% through improved lead prioritization, customer engagement, and automation, while also acting as a virtual collaborator to augment worker productivity.
pages.title: Generative AI in Sales

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how software engineering can be transformed through the use of generative AI in inception and planning, system design, coding, and testing, highlighting the benefits of AI in accelerating processes and improving quality.
pages.title: How software engineering could be transformed

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the role of AI in software engineering, highlighting its potential to enhance productivity by 20-45% through tasks like code generation and refactoring. It emphasizes the growing importance of software in various industries and the benefits of generative AI tools like GitHub Copilot, which can significantly speed up development processes and improve work satisfaction.
pages.title: Maintenance

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how generative AI can transform product R&D through early research analysis, virtual design, virtual simulations, and physical test planning, potentially delivering 10-15% productivity in R&D costs. Examples include its use in life sciences and chemical industries for generating candidate molecules and designing small-molecule therapeutics.
pages.title: How product R&D could be transformed

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI enhances design efficiency and product quality, reducing costs and accelerating testing phases. Deep learning surrogates, paired with generative AI, can significantly speed up simulations, enabling faster decision-making and innovation in product design.
pages.title: The economic potential of generative AI: The next productivity frontier

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the value potential of generative AI across various modalities and industries. It highlights the current focus on text-based applications and the emerging capabilities in image, audio, and video generation. The page also explores the potential of generative AI in R&D and its economic impact, estimating a value generation of $2.6 to $4.4 trillion across 63 use cases.
pages.title: Value potential by modality

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents a detailed analysis of the impact of generative AI on various business functions across different industries. It highlights the varying degrees of impact, ranging from low to high, and provides specific percentages of industry revenue affected. The data is presented in a heatmap format, showing the total revenue and the impact on different business functions such as marketing, customer operations, and product R&D. The analysis covers a wide range of industries including administrative services, advanced electronics, agriculture, banking, and more, providing a comprehensive view of the economic potential of generative AI.
pages.title: Generative AI use cases will have different impacts on business functions across industries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the potential value of generative AI across various industries, including banking, retail, and pharmaceuticals. It highlights specific use cases and their value potential, emphasizing improvements in efficiency, customer interactions, and product development. The page also mentions detailed industry spotlights for further analysis.
pages.title: Generative AI could deliver significant value when deployed in some use cases across a selection of top industries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can significantly enhance retail and CPG industries by automating key functions, personalizing customer experiences, and accelerating value creation. It offers opportunities for improved customer interaction, creative innovation, and efficient data management, while also presenting challenges related to quality control and security.
pages.title: Generative AI could change the game for retail and consumer packaged goods companies

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can significantly impact the banking industry by enhancing productivity, customer satisfaction, decision-making, and risk management. Banks are integrating generative AI in front-line operations and software activities, leveraging it for virtual expert assistance, customer-facing chatbots, and software development. This technology can reduce costs, improve customer experience, and optimize code development.
pages.title: Banks could realize substantial value from generative AI

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_31.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the benefits of generative AI in content creation for banks, including personalized marketing and regulatory compliance. It outlines key factors banks should consider when integrating AI, such as regulation levels, user types, automation, and data constraints. It concludes by highlighting the potential of AI bots for providing continuous technical support.
pages.title: Factors for banks to consider

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_32.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI can significantly impact pharmaceutical and medical-product industries by improving R&D efficiency. It accelerates drug discovery processes, such as lead identification and indication finding, through advanced automation and data processing. However, integrating generative AI requires addressing factors like human oversight, explainability, and privacy concerns to fully capture its benefits.
pages.title: Generative AI deployment could unlock potential value equal to 2.6 to 4.5 percent of annual revenues across the pharmaceutical and medical-product industries

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: This chapter discusses the potential organizational value of generative AI across industries and business functions. It highlights the broader impact of AI embedded in tools used by knowledge workers and emphasizes the need for companies to maximize AI value while managing its effects on workforces and society.
pages.title: The economic potential of generative AI: The next productivity frontier

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how generative AI will impact work activities, economic growth, and productivity. It highlights historical examples of technology augmenting human capabilities and suggests that generative AI will follow a similar pattern but affect different types of activities and occupations. The analysis builds on previous work by the McKinsey Global Institute on technological automation.
pages.title: The generative AI future of work: Impacts on work activities, economic growth, and productivity

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the potential impact of technology adoption on work activities, emphasizing the need for labor productivity acceleration to achieve economic growth and enhance prosperity. It highlights the challenges of integrating technological advancements into practical solutions and adapting to large-scale shifts in occupations and demographics.
pages.title: Labor productivity will have to accelerate to achieve economic growth and enhance prosperity.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the methodology for assessing automation potential across 2,100 work activities and 18 capabilities, including expert surveys and historical analysis. It models adoption timelines and costs, considering factors like regulation and investment. The analysis covers various occupations and activities, detailing capability requirements and potential impacts.
pages.title: About the research

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses advancements in generative AI, highlighting how technology is expected to surpass human performance in various capabilities sooner than anticipated. It includes an exhibit showing expert assessments of when technology will achieve human-level performance in different technical areas, with a focus on natural-language understanding being achieved by 2023 instead of the previously estimated 2027.
pages.title: Accelerating the technical potential to transform knowledge work

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how generative AI has increased the potential for automation from 50% to 60-70% of work hours, compressing the range between early and late adoption scenarios. It presents a graph showing automation potential by scenario and explains that adoption lags behind technical potential due to integration time, costs, and diffusion rates.
pages.title: The advent of generative AI has pulled forward the potential for technical automation.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses how generative AI could accelerate automation adoption in work activities, particularly in postsecondary English teaching. It presents updated scenarios showing a decade's acceleration in reaching 50% automation by 2045, compared to previous estimates. The core focus is on the potential shift in teacher roles and the impact on work activities.
pages.title: The midpoint scenario at which automation adoption could reach 50 percent of time spent on current work activities has accelerated by a decade.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_40.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the varying pace of automation adoption across different countries, influenced by wage levels. Developed countries with higher wages are likely to adopt automation faster due to economic feasibility. The analysis includes scenarios for early and late adoption, illustrated with graphs for select countries. The content also highlights the reliance on assumptions and sensitivities in analyzing generative AI's impact.
pages.title: Different countries, different pace of adoption

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_41.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the limitations and assumptions of the analysis on automation potential, noting that it only considers current work activities and first-order effects. It highlights the variability in technology adoption rates and the potential impact of generative AI on job activities, while acknowledging the possibility of employment reduction in some job categories.
pages.title: Limitations of our analyses, key assumptions, and sensitivities

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_42.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI significantly boosts automation potential in knowledge work, especially in decision making, collaboration, and expertise application. It has less impact on physical tasks. Automation potential for expertise application increased by 34 percentage points, while management and talent development rose from 16% to 49% between 2017 and 2023. This is due to AI's natural language capabilities.
pages.title: Generative AI's potential impact on knowledge work

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the impact of generative AI on automation potential across various occupations, highlighting significant increases in automation for educators, professionals, and creatives. It provides a detailed comparison of automation potential with and without generative AI, showing substantial differences in sectors like office support, production work, and food services.
pages.title: Advances in technical capabilities could have the most impact on activities performed by educators, professionals, and creatives.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_44.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI significantly increases technical automation potential for higher-educated workers, challenging traditional skill indicators and promoting a skills-based workforce development approach. It impacts occupations requiring higher educational attainment more than lower-skilled jobs, potentially reshaping workforce training and matching systems.
pages.title: Generative AI increases the potential for technical automation most in occupations requiring higher levels of educational attainment.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how generative AI is expected to have a significant impact on high-wage jobs, transforming the work of higher-wage knowledge workers. It contrasts this with previous models suggesting automation's biggest impact was on lower-middle-income quintiles. The page includes a detailed chart showing automation adoption per wage quintile in various countries, highlighting the shift in automation impact due to generative AI.
pages.title: Generative AI could have the biggest impact on activities in high-wage jobs; previously, automation’s impact was highest in lower-middle-income quintiles.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses how global economic growth has slowed due to factors like the COVID-19 pandemic and long-term structural challenges such as declining birth rates and aging populations. It highlights the decline in employment growth and productivity growth over the past decade, emphasizing the need for generative AI to propel higher productivity growth.
pages.title: Generative AI could propel higher productivity growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: The deployment of generative AI and other technologies could accelerate productivity growth, providing a 0.5 to 3.4 percent boost to the global economy from 2023 to 2040, with generative AI contributing 0.1 to 0.6 percentage points. This requires effective redeployment of labor hours to match or exceed current productivity levels, with varying impacts across developed and emerging economies.
pages.title: Generative AI could contribute to productivity growth if labor hours can be redeployed effectively.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: Generative AI expands work activities for automation, increasing productivity and offsetting aging impacts. However, workers need support in transitioning to new activities or roles.
pages.title: The economic potential of generative AI: The next productivity frontier

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_49.jpg
pages.title: The economic potential of generative AI: The next productivity frontier

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_50.jpg
pages.abstract: This section discusses the potential of new technologies, particularly generative AI, to reshape societies and businesses. It highlights the current applications of AI and the rapid development of generative AI, which is expected to generate significant economic value. However, it also addresses the challenges and risks associated with generative AI, including concerns about intellectual property, accuracy, explainability, and bias.
pages.title: Considerations for businesses and society

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_51.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the responsible use of generative AI, highlighting various risks such as fairness, intellectual property, privacy, security, explainability, reliability, organizational impact, and social and environmental impact. It also poses critical questions for companies and business leaders on managing these risks and leveraging the potential benefits of generative AI.
pages.title: Using generative AI responsibly

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic potential of generative AI_ McKinsey_2023_06_01\page_52.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the implications of generative AI on future work, workforce planning, and policy-making. It explores how to support workers, develop retraining programs, and ensure human-centric AI development. It also addresses individuals' concerns about AI's impact on their lives and livelihoods, emphasizing the need for balanced perspectives and citizen involvement in AI deployment. The text highlights the rapid adoption of generative AI, its potential economic value, and the challenges it poses, urging collaborative efforts to maximize its benefits while mitigating risks.

94.file_desc:
Generative AI has the potential to significantly boost global productivity and economic value across various sectors, automate a substantial portion of work activities, and accelerate workforce transformation. However, it requires strategic investments in worker support and skill development to fully realize its benefits.
This page discusses the rise of generative AI, driven by significant investments in machine learning and deep learning. It highlights tools like ChatGPT and AlphaGo, emphasizing their broad utility and the subtle yet pervasive impact of AI on daily life. The latest applications enable tasks like text writing and digital art creation, prompting stakeholders to consider their implications on business and society.
This page discusses the evolution of generative AI, driven by foundation models and deep learning. It highlights the capabilities and challenges of generative AI, including processing large datasets, performing multiple tasks, and the increasing investment in the field. The page also mentions notable advancements like ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Claude, and the geographic concentration of investments in North America.
This page explains key concepts in machine learning and AI, including modality, productivity, prompt engineering, self-attention, structured and unstructured data, transformers, technical automation potential, and use cases. It highlights how these concepts contribute to AI's capabilities and applications.
Generative AI marks a significant evolution in AI. Companies are adapting it quickly, and understanding its value to the economy and society is crucial. Two lenses are used to identify where generative AI can deliver the most significant value and estimate its potential impact.
The document evaluates the potential impact of generative AI through two lenses: total economic potential of 60-plus organizational use cases and labor productivity potential across 2,100 detailed work activities. It identifies 63 use cases spanning 16 business functions, delivering economic benefits of $2.6 to $4.4 trillion annually. The second lens analyzes AI's impact on 850 occupations and 2,100 work activities, estimating its effect on global workforce productivity.
The page discusses the economic benefits of generative AI, estimating a potential annual impact of $6.1 to $7.9 trillion when applied to knowledge workers' activities. It highlights the additional value generative AI can create beyond traditional AI and analytics, with a focus on productivity improvements. A bar chart illustrates the potential economic impact, showing incremental contributions from advanced analytics, new generative AI use cases, and total AI economic potential.
This chapter discusses the value potential of generative AI, emphasizing its expanding capabilities beyond traditional AI applications. It details the methodology used to estimate the value of generative AI use cases, focusing on significant improvements in key outputs and excluding cases where the sole benefit is natural language use. The potential annual value across the economy is estimated, particularly in sales and marketing, based on the 2022 global economy structure.
This page discusses the value potential of generative AI across various business functions, highlighting that customer operations, marketing and sales, software engineering, and research and development account for about 75% of the total annual value. A scatter plot illustrates the impact of generative AI, showing significant potential in functions like sales, marketing, and software engineering. The page also notes that the potential value for manufacturing and supply chain functions is now lower due to the nature of generative AI use cases.
Generative AI can revolutionize internal knowledge management systems, enhancing efficiency and decision-making. It can act as a virtual expert, retrieving information and engaging in dialogue, potentially saving knowledge workers significant time and improving productivity.
This page discusses how customer operations can be transformed through customer self-service interactions with chatbots, customer-agent interactions with AI assistance, and agent self-improvement using AI-generated insights.
Generative AI can revolutionize customer operations by enhancing self-service, improving initial contact resolution, reducing response time, and increasing sales. It boosts productivity and quality, especially for less-experienced agents, and can automate up to 50% of human-serviced contacts.
This page discusses how marketing and sales can be transformed through strategization, awareness, and consideration. Professionals gather data from various sources to create effective communications, while customers receive personalized campaigns and access to dynamic recommendations.
This page discusses how generative AI enhances conversion and retention in marketing and sales. Virtual sales representatives build trust through humanlike qualities, while AI-powered chatbots improve customer retention. Generative AI personalizes messages and creates content, but requires careful consideration to avoid risks like plagiarism and biased data.
Generative AI offers marketing significant benefits including efficient content creation, enhanced data use, SEO optimization, and personalized product discovery, potentially increasing marketing productivity by 5-15% of total spending.
Generative AI can enhance sales productivity by 3-5% through improved lead prioritization, customer engagement, and automation, while also acting as a virtual collaborator to augment worker productivity.
This page discusses how software engineering can be transformed through the use of generative AI in inception and planning, system design, coding, and testing, highlighting the benefits of AI in accelerating processes and improving quality.
This page discusses the role of AI in software engineering, highlighting its potential to enhance productivity by 20-45% through tasks like code generation and refactoring. It emphasizes the growing importance of software in various industries and the benefits of generative AI tools like GitHub Copilot, which can significantly speed up development processes and improve work satisfaction.
This page discusses how generative AI can transform product R&D through early research analysis, virtual design, virtual simulations, and physical test planning, potentially delivering 10-15% productivity in R&D costs. Examples include its use in life sciences and chemical industries for generating candidate molecules and designing small-molecule therapeutics.
Generative AI enhances design efficiency and product quality, reducing costs and accelerating testing phases. Deep learning surrogates, paired with generative AI, can significantly speed up simulations, enabling faster decision-making and innovation in product design.
This page discusses the value potential of generative AI across various modalities and industries. It highlights the current focus on text-based applications and the emerging capabilities in image, audio, and video generation. The page also explores the potential of generative AI in R&D and its economic impact, estimating a value generation of $2.6 to $4.4 trillion across 63 use cases.
This page presents a detailed analysis of the impact of generative AI on various business functions across different industries. It highlights the varying degrees of impact, ranging from low to high, and provides specific percentages of industry revenue affected. The data is presented in a heatmap format, showing the total revenue and the impact on different business functions such as marketing, customer operations, and product R&D. The analysis covers a wide range of industries including administrative services, advanced electronics, agriculture, banking, and more, providing a comprehensive view of the economic potential of generative AI.
This page discusses the potential value of generative AI across various industries, including banking, retail, and pharmaceuticals. It highlights specific use cases and their value potential, emphasizing improvements in efficiency, customer interactions, and product development. The page also mentions detailed industry spotlights for further analysis.
Generative AI can significantly enhance retail and CPG industries by automating key functions, personalizing customer experiences, and accelerating value creation. It offers opportunities for improved customer interaction, creative innovation, and efficient data management, while also presenting challenges related to quality control and security.
Generative AI can significantly impact the banking industry by enhancing productivity, customer satisfaction, decision-making, and risk management. Banks are integrating generative AI in front-line operations and software activities, leveraging it for virtual expert assistance, customer-facing chatbots, and software development. This technology can reduce costs, improve customer experience, and optimize code development.
This page discusses the benefits of generative AI in content creation for banks, including personalized marketing and regulatory compliance. It outlines key factors banks should consider when integrating AI, such as regulation levels, user types, automation, and data constraints. It concludes by highlighting the potential of AI bots for providing continuous technical support.
Generative AI can significantly impact pharmaceutical and medical-product industries by improving R&D efficiency. It accelerates drug discovery processes, such as lead identification and indication finding, through advanced automation and data processing. However, integrating generative AI requires addressing factors like human oversight, explainability, and privacy concerns to fully capture its benefits.
This chapter discusses the potential organizational value of generative AI across industries and business functions. It highlights the broader impact of AI embedded in tools used by knowledge workers and emphasizes the need for companies to maximize AI value while managing its effects on workforces and society.
This page discusses how generative AI will impact work activities, economic growth, and productivity. It highlights historical examples of technology augmenting human capabilities and suggests that generative AI will follow a similar pattern but affect different types of activities and occupations. The analysis builds on previous work by the McKinsey Global Institute on technological automation.
This page discusses the potential impact of technology adoption on work activities, emphasizing the need for labor productivity acceleration to achieve economic growth and enhance prosperity. It highlights the challenges of integrating technological advancements into practical solutions and adapting to large-scale shifts in occupations and demographics.
This page discusses the methodology for assessing automation potential across 2,100 work activities and 18 capabilities, including expert surveys and historical analysis. It models adoption timelines and costs, considering factors like regulation and investment. The analysis covers various occupations and activities, detailing capability requirements and potential impacts.
This page discusses advancements in generative AI, highlighting how technology is expected to surpass human performance in various capabilities sooner than anticipated. It includes an exhibit showing expert assessments of when technology will achieve human-level performance in different technical areas, with a focus on natural-language understanding being achieved by 2023 instead of the previously estimated 2027.
This page discusses how generative AI has increased the potential for automation from 50% to 60-70% of work hours, compressing the range between early and late adoption scenarios. It presents a graph showing automation potential by scenario and explains that adoption lags behind technical potential due to integration time, costs, and diffusion rates.
The document discusses how generative AI could accelerate automation adoption in work activities, particularly in postsecondary English teaching. It presents updated scenarios showing a decade's acceleration in reaching 50% automation by 2045, compared to previous estimates. The core focus is on the potential shift in teacher roles and the impact on work activities.
This page discusses the varying pace of automation adoption across different countries, influenced by wage levels. Developed countries with higher wages are likely to adopt automation faster due to economic feasibility. The analysis includes scenarios for early and late adoption, illustrated with graphs for select countries. The content also highlights the reliance on assumptions and sensitivities in analyzing generative AI's impact.
This page discusses the limitations and assumptions of the analysis on automation potential, noting that it only considers current work activities and first-order effects. It highlights the variability in technology adoption rates and the potential impact of generative AI on job activities, while acknowledging the possibility of employment reduction in some job categories.
Generative AI significantly boosts automation potential in knowledge work, especially in decision making, collaboration, and expertise application. It has less impact on physical tasks. Automation potential for expertise application increased by 34 percentage points, while management and talent development rose from 16% to 49% between 2017 and 2023. This is due to AI's natural language capabilities.
The document discusses the impact of generative AI on automation potential across various occupations, highlighting significant increases in automation for educators, professionals, and creatives. It provides a detailed comparison of automation potential with and without generative AI, showing substantial differences in sectors like office support, production work, and food services.
Generative AI significantly increases technical automation potential for higher-educated workers, challenging traditional skill indicators and promoting a skills-based workforce development approach. It impacts occupations requiring higher educational attainment more than lower-skilled jobs, potentially reshaping workforce training and matching systems.
This page discusses how generative AI is expected to have a significant impact on high-wage jobs, transforming the work of higher-wage knowledge workers. It contrasts this with previous models suggesting automation's biggest impact was on lower-middle-income quintiles. The page includes a detailed chart showing automation adoption per wage quintile in various countries, highlighting the shift in automation impact due to generative AI.
The document discusses how global economic growth has slowed due to factors like the COVID-19 pandemic and long-term structural challenges such as declining birth rates and aging populations. It highlights the decline in employment growth and productivity growth over the past decade, emphasizing the need for generative AI to propel higher productivity growth.
The deployment of generative AI and other technologies could accelerate productivity growth, providing a 0.5 to 3.4 percent boost to the global economy from 2023 to 2040, with generative AI contributing 0.1 to 0.6 percentage points. This requires effective redeployment of labor hours to match or exceed current productivity levels, with varying impacts across developed and emerging economies.
Generative AI expands work activities for automation, increasing productivity and offsetting aging impacts. However, workers need support in transitioning to new activities or roles.
This section discusses the potential of new technologies, particularly generative AI, to reshape societies and businesses. It highlights the current applications of AI and the rapid development of generative AI, which is expected to generate significant economic value. However, it also addresses the challenges and risks associated with generative AI, including concerns about intellectual property, accuracy, explainability, and bias.
This page discusses the responsible use of generative AI, highlighting various risks such as fairness, intellectual property, privacy, security, explainability, reliability, organizational impact, and social and environmental impact. It also poses critical questions for companies and business leaders on managing these risks and leveraging the potential benefits of generative AI.
This page discusses the implications of generative AI on future work, workforce planning, and policy-making. It explores how to support workers, develop retraining programs, and ensure human-centric AI development. It also addresses individuals' concerns about AI's impact on their lives and livelihoods, emphasizing the need for balanced perspectives and citizen involvement in AI deployment. The text highlights the rapid adoption of generative AI, its potential economic value, and the challenges it poses, urging collaborative efforts to maximize its benefits while mitigating risks.
The image illustrates a man using a smartphone in a technologically advanced urban setting, highlighting the integration of technology in daily life and its potential impact on productivity.

This page details the economic potential of generative AI by analyzing its impact on various business functions like marketing, IT, talent management, and finance. The analysis includes expert inputs, internal experiments, and published research to quantify the potential benefits.

It details methodologies, data sources, and findings, such as the potential for AI to automate work tasks, substitute jobs, and boost productivity. The studies cover various regions and emphasize the significant role of AI in transforming labor markets and productivity.
This page discusses the occupational exposure to generative AI, focusing on language modeling and image generation. It analyzes the impact on various occupations, demographics, and productivity. The findings highlight the correlation between AI exposure and factors like education, salary, and demographic representation. Additionally, it explores the economic potential of generative AI, estimating its impact on automation, productivity, and workforce dynamics across 47 countries.
This page discusses the assessment of automation potential across global occupations, using a machine learning algorithm to score work activities based on 18 capabilities. It outlines the process of defining automation levels, manual adjustments, and the modeling of automation adoption timelines, focusing on technical feasibility and generative AI's impact on various capabilities.

The wage evolution for countries is also modeled in two stages, considering growth rates and reclassification into cohorts.

pages.abstract: The executive summary highlights the significant economic impact of US Latinos, their growing consumer market, and the unmet needs that could reach $660 billion. Companies can capitalize on this market by addressing these issues and tailoring their strategies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the potential economic benefits of closing the Latino wealth gap, emphasizing the need for better job opportunities and financial inclusion. It highlights the challenges Latinos face in wealth accumulation and access to capital, and suggests that addressing these issues could significantly boost the economy and create millions of jobs.
pages.title: Closing the Latino wealth gap would strengthen the existing consumer opportunity by more than 500 percent

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights the economic disparities and resilience of Latinos in the US, detailing gaps in income, wealth, and consumption compared to non-Latino White Americans. It also showcases the potential economic impact of increasing Latino business ownership and the recovery of Latino-owned firms post-COVID-19.
pages.title: The economic state of Latinos in the US: Determined to thrive

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: Latinos face economic challenges but show resilience. Despite vulnerabilities in low-wage jobs and COVID-19 impacts, 80% of Latino businesses stabilized sales by mid-2021. Latinos are advancing in professional roles, entrepreneurship, and consumer spending. Strategic interventions can further enhance their economic participation and prosperity.
pages.title: Latinos' proven resilience through the pandemic indicates strong fundamentals for economic mobility

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights the economic challenges and growth of the Latino population in the US, emphasizing their underrepresentation in high-paying jobs, limited access to capital for entrepreneurship, and slower wealth accumulation compared to non-Latino Whites. It also outlines the data sources used for the research, including various surveys and official statistics.

pages.abstract: This introduction highlights the growing economic significance of Latinos in the US, their vulnerabilities to economic challenges, and the need for equitable interventions to support their advancement. It emphasizes the potential benefits for society as a whole if these interventions are implemented.
pages.title: 1. Introduction

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_14.jpg
pages.title: The economic state of Latinos in the US: Determined to thrive

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: Latino consumers have grown their household consumption to $1 trillion, showing a 6% annual growth rate. They are conscious of their impact and choose brands that value the environment and employees. However, they are dissatisfied with product offerings, especially compared to non-Latino Whites. Addressing price and quality could unlock $109 billion in spending. Latinos are younger, increasingly educated, but with lower incomes. Companies can support them by optimizing value propositions and tailoring marketing strategies.
pages.title: 2. Latino consumers: Driving growth with conscious choices

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: Latinos are planning to cut spending 4x more than the general population due to inflation. They spend more on essentials and non-essentials compared to the general population, despite lower income levels. Latinos account for 19% of the US population but only 13% of total household income, with a $554 billion gap in consumption.
pages.title: Affordability will become more important, as Latinos are planning to cut spend 4x more than the general population.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the growth in Latino consumption, noting that despite an increase, it still lags behind their share of the US population. It highlights the higher spending on essentials by Latino households and compares their consumption patterns with non-Latino White households. The page also presents data on the total annual household consumption and the gap in Latino consumption relative to their population share, emphasizing a $554 billion difference.
pages.title: While Latino consumption has grown, it still falls short of Latinos' share of the US population.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the dissatisfaction of Latino consumers with current product offerings, highlighting that 28% of Latinos are unhappy compared to 21% of non-Latino Whites. It identifies missed opportunities for companies due to unmet needs and low product penetration in specific categories. The text also explores variations in dissatisfaction among Latino subgroups based on education, income, background, and gender, and notes a significant increase in dissatisfaction between 2021 and 2022.
pages.title: Latino consumer needs are not being met

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: Latinos are dissatisfied with product offerings due to price, quality, and value. Addressing these issues could increase their consumption by 25%, with a potential $33 billion more spent annually. Companies addressing dissatisfaction may benefit from additional market support, though much of this would be due to shifts in spending.
pages.title: Opportunities to address dissatisfaction: A win-win situation

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: This page details the potential additional spending by dissatisfied Latino consumers across various categories, highlighting significant unmet demand in housing, hospitality, and vehicle purchases. The data reveals that addressing dissatisfaction could unlock $33 billion in additional spending, with housing showing the largest unmet demand at $10.8 billion.
pages.title: Latino consumers would be willing to spend $33 billion more if reasons for dissatisfaction were addressed

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses Latino consumption patterns, highlighting their strategic spending, price-conscious behavior, and high attention to sustainability. Latinos spend more on essentials, actively seek savings, and are influenced by social media. They are engaged consumers who use omnichannel and e-commerce platforms more than the general population.
pages.title: Latino consumption patterns: Strategic spenders, socially aware, and social media savvy

pages.page_path: library_pages\The economic state of Latinos in the US_ Determined to thrive_McKinsey_2022_11_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: Latino consumers are significantly impacted by inflation, leading to changes in spending habits. They are more likely to cut back on non-essential spending and switch to private brands. The fall in Latino spending could result in an aggregate loss of $80 billion, with a greater reduction in non-essential categories compared to the general population.

pages.title: Contents

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_4.jpg
pages.abstract: This page summarizes the potential economic scenarios resulting from asset price inflation and financial system shifts, highlighting the need for productivity acceleration to align economic growth with balance sheet health. It outlines the risks of volatility, high inflation, and asset price contractions, emphasizing the importance of strategic decision-making and investment in technology and human capital.
pages.title: At a glance

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: The document outlines four potential economic scenarios to 2030, including a return to past era, higher for longer, balance sheet reset, and productivity acceleration. Each scenario describes what would happen, what it means, growth, inflation, real rate, and growth in asset values for the US. The scenarios range from sluggish growth with balance sheet risk to growth in real wealth with declining balance sheet risk.
pages.title: Four broad economic and balance sheet scenarios to 2030 are possible.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: The introduction discusses recent banking turbulence against a backdrop of higher interest rates and high leverage, marking a shift from previous conditions of loose money and wealth growth. It highlights the rapid expansion of the global balance sheet over two decades, leading to debt and asset price growth but lagging productivity and economic output, resulting in increased inequality. By late 2022, economic instability was evident, with households losing significant wealth. The text poses questions about the future of wealth, economic growth, and the potential rebalancing of the financial system.
pages.title: Introduction

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses potential long-term economic paths, focusing on four scenarios modeled by MGI. It highlights the importance of productivity growth and balance sheet health in shaping economic outcomes. The stakes are high, with significant impacts on GDP growth and household wealth depending on the scenario. Decision makers must consider balance sheet impacts when formulating economic policy.
pages.title: The economic, banking, and investment landscape of the next ten years may look very different from that of the past 20 years.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents a scenario analysis of GDP growth and household wealth in the United States by 2030, showing variations under different economic conditions. Real GDP growth and household wealth are projected to change significantly, with productivity acceleration leading to the highest positive impact. The primary channels of wealth adjustment include asset price inflation, inflation dampening, asset correction, and productive new capital formation.
pages.title: GDP growth varies by 1.7 percentage points and household wealth by $48 trillion across scenarios in the United States.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: The global balance sheet encompasses all real and financial assets and liabilities across various sectors, valued at market prices. It includes three interlocking components: the financial sector, the financial system, and the real economy. This sheet provides insights into the global economic structure and asset distribution.
pages.title: What is the global balance sheet?

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: The global balance sheet is divided into three interlocking balance sheets, each valued around $500 to $600 trillion. The financial sector creates and intermediates assets, the financial system separates wealth from investment, and the real economy drives growth and wealth. The data includes financial assets and liabilities held by various sectors, with a focus on debt, equity, currency, and other financial assets.
pages.title: The global balance sheet consists of three interlocking balance sheets of, coincidentally, ~$500 trillion to $600 trillion each.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: The past two decades have seen rapid growth in global net worth and debt, outpacing GDP growth. However, productivity growth among G-7 countries has slowed significantly, highlighting a disconnect between wealth accumulation and economic growth.
pages.title: Two decades of growing ‘paper wealth’ but slow economic growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: The global balance sheet has outpaced GDP growth since 2000, with asset valuations increasing faster than real economic output. Between 2000 and 2021, $160 trillion in 'paper wealth' was created, and net investment generated significant new debt. The balance sheet quadrupled to $1.6 quadrillion, with real and financial assets growing rapidly. Pandemic support measures further accelerated this trend.
pages.title: The global balance sheet began rapidly outgrowing GDP in about 2000.

pages.page_path: library_pages\The future of wealth and growth hangs in the balance_McKinsey_2023_05_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the growth of major asset types relative to GDP as real interest rates declined. It highlights the rise in real estate, equity, debt, and currency/deposits since 2000, with variations across economies. The US is used as an example, showing significant outgrowth of these assets compared to GDP since the mid-1990s.
