pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces economic and climate challenges in 2024, with uncertain consumer confidence and fluctuating demand. Companies must adapt with new pricing strategies and increased transparency to navigate these headwinds.
pages.title: Riding Out the Storm

pages.abstract: Fashion leaders anticipate challenges in 2024 due to increased scrutiny on supply chains, new sustainability regulations, and competition from fast-fashion brands. They are focusing on generative AI for design and product development, brand marketing for emotional connections, and adapting to consumer demands for authenticity. Travel and outdoor activities are expected to rise, influencing fashion trends and marketing strategies.
pages.title: Looking to 2024, fashion leaders are anticipating further headwinds and are uncertain about prospects for the year ahead.

pages.abstract: Fashion executives face uncertainty in 2024 due to geopolitical events, economic weakness, and high interest rates. While 26% expect improvement, 38% anticipate worsening conditions. Geopolitical instability is the top risk, with 62% citing it as a major concern.
pages.title: Destination Unknown

pages.abstract: The document discusses anticipated retail sales growth across regions in 2024, highlighting slower but normalized growth. It compares non-luxury and luxury segments in Europe, the US, and China, noting inflation concerns and regional variations. Non-luxury retail sales are forecast to remain steady, with growth between 2% and 4% globally, while luxury segments show more volatility. The text also mentions the impact of inflation and central bank policies on consumer behavior.
pages.title: Slower but normalised growth is anticipated across regions in 2024

pages.abstract: The document discusses the uncertain outlook for the fashion industry in 2024, with no clear consensus among executives. It compares expectations for 2024, 2023, and 2022, highlighting variations in better, same, and worse conditions. It also analyzes growth forecasts for non-luxury and luxury sectors in the US, China, and Europe, considering factors like inflation, consumer sentiment, and e-commerce trends.
pages.title: Uncertainty reigns as executives reveal no clear consensus on the outlook for 2024

pages.abstract: The page discusses expected retail price changes in 2024, with 69% of executives planning increases. It highlights growth predictions for luxury markets in the US, China, and Europe, noting factors like tourism and currency impacts. The Middle East, India, and Asia Pacific are seen as promising regions for growth.
pages.title: Companies are planning price increases to combat continued inflation, with 25 percent of executives expecting increases of over 5 percent
Galerie royale Saint-Hubert

pages.abstract: Fashion executives are focusing on increasing sales, pricing strategies, and sustainability in 2024. They aim to balance cost control with investments in innovation like AI, while consumers prioritize reliable brands and luxury goods. Bold decision-making is crucial amid macroeconomic challenges.
pages.title: Strategic Priorities

pages.abstract: The document outlines key trends in the global economy and consumer behavior for 2024, including economic uncertainty, climate-related challenges, increased travel, evolving influencer marketing, and the rise of technical outdoor wear. It highlights the need for brands to adapt to these shifts by building resilience, refreshing strategies, and embracing new forms of partnership and lifestyle integration.
pages.title: The State of

pages.abstract: The page discusses key trends in the fashion industry for 2024, including the impact of generative AI, fast fashion competition, brand marketing, sustainability regulations, and supply chain challenges. It highlights the need for brands to adapt to evolving consumer preferences and regulatory changes.
pages.title: Fashion 2024
Global Economy

pages.abstract: The global economic outlook for 2024 is expected to remain unsettled due to financial, geopolitical, and other challenges. Fashion markets in the US, Europe, and China face varying headwinds, necessitating robust contingency planning. Key insights include a slowdown in global GDP growth, tempered consumer spending, and potential growth in Emerging Asia, particularly India.
pages.title: Fragmented Future

pages.abstract: The document discusses global consumer spending trends, focusing on apparel spending intentions in Europe, the US, and China. It highlights economic challenges such as inflation, interest rate hikes, and geopolitical conflicts. Europe and the US are expected to reduce apparel spending, while China's spending is projected to rise. The economic outlook for Europe is gloomy due to the war in Ukraine and stagnating growth in Germany. Inflation remains high globally, and central banks expect interest rates to stay elevated.
pages.title: Consumers in Europe and the US plan to reduce apparel spend, while China’s is expected to rise

pages.abstract: The document discusses economic challenges in Europe, the US, and China, including inflation, consumer confidence, and property market crises. It highlights the impact of Federal Reserve policies in the US, the fragility of consumer confidence, and the high savings rate in China. The text also mentions the decline in savings in the US and Europe post-Covid-19.
pages.title: Global Economy

pages.abstract: The document discusses the economic challenges and opportunities in the fashion industry for 2024, highlighting consumer spending pressures, economic growth forecasts, and regional variations. It emphasizes the need for resilience and strategic planning in the face of slowing growth and geopolitical conflicts.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024
The Tumultuous Path to an Exit

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces investment challenges due to inconsistent performance and polarisation. Fashion businesses need solid fundamentals for funding. Private equity firms face difficulties exiting fashion assets in 2024 due to market volatility. The financial performance of luxury and non-luxury fashion diverged after 2018. PE investors are cautious about non-luxury fashion, with deal volume stagnating. Investors prioritize brands with timeless designs and strong brand stories to minimize 'fashion risk.'
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: The page discusses how companies with strong revenue and profit growth have higher market values. It highlights the PE industry's focus on luxury and other fashion-related sectors, the growing backlog of deals needing realization, and the cautious approach towards certain segments due to macroeconomic headwinds and trend-related risks.
pages.title: Market values are higher for companies with strong revenue and profit growth

pages.abstract: The page discusses the distribution of assets acquired by private equity investors in EMEA, highlighting that around half of the assets are brands, which pose trend-related risks. It also explores the challenges and opportunities in the public market for fashion and luxury brands, noting the performance of newly listed AF&L stocks and factors contributing to the success of brands like Zegna and On.
pages.title: Around half of fashion assets that private equity investors may want to offload soon are brands, which can pose trend-related risks

pages.abstract: The page discusses the revival of the fashion industry, focusing on IPOs and the factors that contribute to successful flotations. It highlights the importance of revenue growth, margin accretion, and investor expectations. The text also mentions the impact of public market revivals on private equity deals and the challenges faced by brands like Birkenstock. The key requirements for successful flotations include a compelling equity story, sustained revenue and margin growth, scalability, and resilience.
pages.title: Signs of Revival

pages.abstract: The page discusses the increasing visibility of the climate crisis in 2023, highlighting the fashion industry's vulnerability. It emphasizes the need for resilience in supply chains and emission reduction. Key insights include the fashion industry's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions, potential economic impacts by 2030, and competing challenges like economic uncertainty.
pages.title: 02. Climate Urgency

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces significant climate-related risks due to its global supply chains. Immediate action is needed to address these risks, as extreme weather events are increasing in frequency and intensity. Brands must revisit supplier standards and invest in climate resilience.
pages.title: Climate Risks in Fashion Industry

pages.abstract: The document discusses the economic impact of climate-related disasters on the fashion industry, highlighting significant losses in various countries and the increasing cost of such disasters over the past 50 years. It emphasizes the need for short and long-term strategies to address climate challenges, including de-risking the value chain and enhancing sustainability. The fashion industry's reliance on regions most affected by climate upheavals poses an outsized risk, with potential economic annihilation by 2100 if global warming reaches 5°C. By 2030, extreme weather events could jeopardize $65 billion in apparel exports and eliminate nearly one million jobs.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces significant climate-related risks, impacting raw material production, manufacturing, and logistics. Companies must adopt strategies to boost resilience, prioritize worker health, and invest in innovation to reduce environmental impact. Collaboration and industry-wide initiatives are crucial for effective adaptation.
pages.title: Weather-Proofing Strategies in 2024 and Beyond
Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: This page discusses the upcoming surge in travel post-pandemic, highlighting shifts in consumer values and expectations. It advises brands and retailers to adapt their strategies to cater to travelers' needs. Key insights include global travel surpassing pre-pandemic levels in 2024, high shopping intentions among travelers, and a preference for new destinations.
pages.title: 03. Vacation Mode

pages.abstract: The page discusses how consumers prioritize experiences over shopping while travelling post-Covid-19. It highlights the rise in global travel flows, lifestyle changes like remote work, and the trend of 'workation' trips. It also mentions the growth in sales for luxury brands due to tourists and the expectation of increased shopping while travelling.
pages.title: Consumers will prioritise experiences whilst travelling

pages.abstract: The document discusses the revival of tourism in capital cities like Paris and London, highlighting the surge in visitor numbers. It also explores the trend of travelers seeking new destinations, driven by a post-pandemic desire for freedom and escapism. Brands are adapting by expanding into second-tier cities and leveraging pop-up experiences in categories like food, nature, and wellness. Examples include Prada's pop-up café, Fendi's resort-based rollout, and Dior's Dioriviera. The fusion of fashion and hospitality is also noted, with collaborations offering travelers unique experiences.
pages.title: Pushing the Boundaries

pages.abstract: The new travel era boosts resort fashion, with brands launching collections and creative marketing strategies. Luxury and mass-market brands collaborate to meet consumer demand for vacation wear, emphasizing unique experiences and partnerships with travel-related industries.
pages.title: Get Packing
How China's Tourists Will Return in 2024

pages.abstract: Chinese tourists are expected to return overseas in 2024, with evolving preferences and behaviors. Domestic travel has thrived during the pandemic, with robust consumer willingness to travel. McKinsey research shows travel as a top spending category. Hainan has become a tax-free shopping hotspot, with fashion sales soaring.
pages.title: Chinese tourists' return and evolving travel preferences

pages.abstract: Chinese consumers are planning both international and domestic travel, with a higher net intent for business travel domestically and personal travel internationally. The luxury retail market in Hainan is expected to grow significantly, attracting over 80 million visitors annually. Luxury brands are investing in domestic markets, and duty-free allowances are incentivizing domestic spending. Experts forecast a permanent repatriation of luxury spend, with domestic shopping accounting for a larger share of the market.
pages.title: Chinese consumers are planning both international and domestic travel

pages.abstract: This page discusses the recovery of outbound travel from mainland China, highlighting a surge in travel bookings and visa processing services. It details the shift in consumer priorities towards experiences like dining and sightseeing, with shopping remaining a significant activity. The page also notes the recovery of shopping spending among Chinese tourists in Asia Pacific, reaching 109 percent of 2019 levels, driven by increased average spend per shopper. It concludes with new shopping priorities, emphasizing in-store experiences and omnichannel engagement.
pages.title: Outbound Travel Recovery and Shopping Trends Among Chinese Consumers

pages.abstract: Brands and retailers should adapt to evolving Chinese consumer preferences by enhancing in-store experiences, integrating digital ecosystems, revamping product assortments, and catering to diverse global shoppers. This includes focusing on luxury goods, personalized services, and strategic partnerships with influencers.
pages.title: How Should Brands and Retailers Respond?

pages.abstract: Brand marketers need to adapt their influencer strategies in 2024, focusing on new creative personalities who gain trust and fandom. Consumers are bothered by sponsored content and demand authenticity. Marketers should emphasize video and relinquish some creative control.
pages.title: The New Face of Influence

pages.abstract: Engagement rates on Instagram have declined, and consumers are showing fatigue towards traditional influencer marketing. Young consumers, especially Gen-Z, are adept at tuning out noise, losing attention to ads quickly. However, influencers remain a powerful channel for brands, with the industry forecast to grow. Consumers now prefer authentic and relatable influencers over other attributes.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: Consumers prefer fashion influencers who are relatable and authentic. Attributes like relatability and authentic content are highly valued. TikTok has become a leading platform for influencers due to its emphasis on authenticity and user engagement. New influencers with quirky, humorous, and vulnerable styles are gaining popularity, especially among Gen-Z audiences.
pages.title: Consumers prefer fashion influencers who are relatable and authentic over other traits

pages.abstract: This page discusses the shift in consumer behavior towards more authentic and off-beat content creators, highlighting successful collaborations between fashion brands and influencers. It emphasizes the need for brands to be creative, move beyond traditional polished promotions, and embrace innovative campaigns that resonate with audiences. The text also stresses the importance of deeper partnerships with influencers, empowering them with creative control, and integrating brand messages seamlessly into their content style.
pages.title: Consumers are showing signs of fatigue towards traditional influencer marketing after years of being bombarded with product promotions and brand announcements.

pages.abstract: The Gstaad Guy uses social media wit to parody the ultra-wealthy, turning it into a full-time business by partnering with luxury brands for high-net-worth shoppers, showcasing the impact of niche influencer marketing on brand-customer connections.
pages.title: Gstaad Guy: Catering to the 1% with Social Media Wit

pages.abstract: Gstaad Guy, a satirical social media persona, parodies the ultra-rich through fictional characters like Constance and Colton. His content resonates with the wealthy elite, leading to collaborations with luxury brands like Loro Piana. His videos, starting from a personal joke, gained traction in exclusive communities and influenced consumer behavior.
pages.title: Gstaad Guy: Satirical Social Commentary on Ultra-Rich

pages.abstract: The page discusses the unique position of the Gstaad Guy account in the influencer landscape, focusing on creating authentic characters and engaging high-net-worth individuals through niche humor and storytelling. It highlights the business opportunities arising from this approach, emphasizing the importance of authentic connections in luxury social-media marketing.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: The text discusses the nuances of luxury social-media marketing, emphasizing the importance of authenticity and genuine connections over mere ad space sales. It highlights the value of small, dedicated communities and the need for sustainable growth rather than rapid scaling. The author reflects on personal experiences and the role of characters in storytelling, aiming for timeless appeal rather than fleeting trends.
pages.title: In the world of luxury social-media marketing, selling ad space and having a very authentic partnership are two very different things.

pages.abstract: Technical outdoor wear is gaining momentum due to healthier lifestyles and gorpcore trends. Brands are merging functionality with style, launching lifestyle collections and incorporating technical elements. Increased competition is expected in 2024, with some brands targeting high-end markets and others focusing on footwear. The cooling of gorpcore may lead to a quieter outdoor fashion style.
pages.title: 05. Outdoors Reinvented

pages.abstract: The page discusses the growing consumer interest in outdoor activities and healthier lifestyles post-Covid-19, highlighting the success of outdoor brands like Salomon and Asics. It explores the gorpcore trend, investment in outdoor wear, and collaborations between luxury and outdoor brands, emphasizing the mainstream adoption of outdoor-inspired fashion.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: Brands are aligning outdoor products with everyday lifestyles, integrating fashion and functionality. Luxury brands are moving from one-off outdoor collections to permanent lines, while outdoor brands are adopting luxury elements. The trend towards 'quiet outdoor' styles is expected to grow, focusing on minimal logos and technical fabrics. Outdoor-style footwear is gaining traction among sneaker enthusiasts. Brands are developing products that bridge utility and fashion, suitable for both urban and outdoor settings. Competition in the outdoor category is expected to increase across price points.
pages.title: The challenge for all brands will be to establish relevancy among diverse customer segments, from technical outdoor-goers to StockX customers, while staying true to the brand's core.

pages.abstract: The page discusses consumer shifts in the apparel and footwear markets, highlighting the challenges brands face in maintaining their identity while appealing to diverse customer segments. It emphasizes the importance of innovation and material testing for outdoor and fashion brands entering each other's markets.
pages.title: Consumer Shifts

pages.abstract: David Allemann, co-founder and executive co-chairman of a Swiss performance sportswear brand, discusses leveraging innovation, technology, and athlete collaborations to build credibility with outdoor consumers.
pages.title: On: Capitalising on the Perennial Sportswear Boom

pages.abstract: On's expansion from high-tech running footwear to fashion-forward sportswear is an evolution driven by credibility and innovation. The brand's partnership with Roger Federer and focus on performance and sustainability have contributed to its growth. The sportswear market's shift towards everyday wear and outdoor lifestyles presents opportunities for brands like On.
pages.title: On's Evolution in Sportswear

pages.abstract: This page discusses the influence of sports technology on fashion, the challenges of entering the performance footwear market, and the importance of athlete collaboration in product development. It highlights the unique technology and engineering behind On's footwear and the personal approach to partnerships with athletes like Roger Federer and Iga Świątek.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: On's approach to launching its apparel category involves leveraging its unique background in sports and fashion, using technical fabrics, and building a community through grassroots efforts and physical presence in key markets, especially in China.
pages.title: On's Approach to Launching Its Apparel Category
Fashion System

pages.abstract: This page discusses the emerging role of generative AI in creative industries, particularly fashion. It highlights the need for fashion players to explore AI's potential beyond automation to enhance human creativity. Key insights include the significant value AI can bring to design and product development, the prioritization of AI by fashion executives, and the substantial equity funding for AI-focused startups.
pages.title: 06. Gen AI's Creative Crossroad

pages.abstract: This page discusses the impact of generative artificial intelligence (gen AI) on the fashion industry, highlighting its potential to transform the industry by enhancing and replacing skills. It mentions the rapid growth of gen AI tools like ChatGPT and their applications in design and product development. The page also notes the cautious approach of fashion companies towards adopting gen AI due to concerns about job and workflow impacts.
pages.title: Disruptive technologies in the workplace

pages.abstract: The page discusses the adoption of generative AI in the fashion industry, highlighting its practical applications and investments. It mentions the increasing use of AI in marketing, design, and customer experience, with examples of brands like Zalando, Kering, and Ganni incorporating AI technologies. The page also notes the significant funding for AI-focused startups and the potential for AI to disrupt the industry.
pages.title: Though still an emerging technology, more than half of fashion executives say their companies are using gen AI

pages.abstract: This page discusses the integration of generative AI in the fashion industry, highlighting its potential to enhance creativity and efficiency. It covers various applications, from accelerating design processes in fast fashion to enabling experimentation in luxury brands. The text emphasizes the importance of human skill and creativity in brand differentiation and the role of AI as a tool for curation rather than replacement. It also mentions specific examples of brands using AI and the benefits of AI tools like AiDA and Cala.
pages.title: In fashion, human skill and creativity often hold the key to brand differentiation.
Driving Growth Through Generative AI: An Executive Playbook

pages.abstract: Generative AI can enhance fashion business capabilities across the value chain, from product development to customer service, by automating tasks, personalizing experiences, and improving efficiency. It offers opportunities for innovation and cost savings but requires careful implementation to manage risks.
pages.title: Generative AI can add value across the fashion value chain

pages.abstract: This page discusses the opportunities and challenges of implementing generative AI in the fashion industry, emphasizing the need for strategic planning, collaboration, and upskilling. It highlights the importance of setting priorities for impact, shaping effective teams, and establishing a central control tower for successful AI integration.
pages.title: Setting Priorities for Impact

pages.abstract: This page discusses the structure of a generative AI team, emphasizing the need for specialized squad members and executive sponsors. It outlines a sample squad structure with roles like UI/UX Designer, Product Manager, and Data Scientist. The page also explores tech and partnership choices for AI adoption, highlighting the benefits of fine-tuning third-party models and deploying specialized applications.
pages.title: A generative AI team should contain specialised squad members and executive sponsors

pages.abstract: The page discusses the importance of tech partners and vendors in providing hard-to-find talent while emphasizing the need for leaders to build in-house skills and knowledge through these relationships. A model is featured wearing a blue quilted coat with a belt, showcasing a fashion-forward look.
pages.title: Hard-to-find talent may be provided through tech partners and vendors

pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges and opportunities of integrating gen AI in the fashion industry, emphasizing the need for careful risk management, including bias, creativity, intellectual property, and data protection. It highlights the importance of human-centered governance, employee training, and secure IT infrastructure to responsibly scale gen AI applications.
pages.title: Navigating Risks and Scaling Up in Gen AI for Fashion

pages.abstract: Fast-fashion competition intensifies as Shein and Temu lead with innovative tactics. Success depends on adapting to consumer preferences and navigating regulations. Third-generation fast-fashion companies attract significant consumer attention, driven by agile supply chains and data-driven design. Challenges in 2024 include evolving standards on sustainability and trade practices.
pages.title: Fast Fashion's Power Plays

pages.abstract: The page discusses the evolution of fast fashion, highlighting the rise of third-generation companies like Shein and Temu. These companies offer ultra-low prices and rapid trend turnovers, capturing consumer attention. The text explains their innovative operating models, including agile supply chains and data-driven product design, while noting challenges like delivery times and quality control.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: Third-generation fast-fashion retailers like Shein and Temu have built loyal customer bases through influencer marketing and gamification, achieving high conversion and retention rates. However, they face increasing public and regulatory scrutiny over environmental impact and unethical practices. Policy changes in key markets may challenge their business model.
pages.title: Loyal and growing customer bases and high app adoption rates and engagement tactics

pages.abstract: The document outlines the evolution of fast-fashion companies across three generations, highlighting their strategies and challenges. It emphasizes the need for adaptation in the face of industry disruptions and Shein's efforts to maintain its leading position through diversification and global expansion.
pages.title: Three generations of fast-fashion companies are underpinned by an evolution in speed and innovation

pages.abstract: Shein's transition to an omnichannel model and marketplace strategy could challenge its competitive edge. The retailer is piloting an 'everything store' model in the US and Brazil, potentially expanding in 2024, and entering luxury fashion. Third-generation fast-fashion companies may disrupt the market by expanding across categories and using gamification tactics to engage customers.
pages.title: Shein's Retail Strategy and Market Disruption

pages.abstract: Third-generation fast-fashion players, particularly Shein and Temu, have attracted significant interest among consumers across various age groups in the US and UK. The data shows their strong presence compared to incumbents, with notable shopping percentages in the last 12 months.
pages.title: Fast Fashion's Power Plays

pages.abstract: The page discusses the growing popularity of third-generation fast-fashion retailers like Shein and Temu among consumers in the UK and US. It highlights their increasing share of wallet and net purchase intent compared to traditional retailers like H&M. The page also emphasizes the perception of these companies as offering low prices, a broad range of products, a fun shopping experience, and social buzz.
pages.title: in Numbers

pages.abstract: Mun-il Han, CEO of Musinsa, has developed a unique business model benefiting emerging brands, Gen-Z customers, and the company. Leveraging K-culture's global rise, Musinsa is expanding internationally.
pages.title: Musinsa: Taking the K-Fashion Ecosystem Global

pages.abstract: Musinsa, a Korean fashion marketplace, has expanded globally, leveraging K-pop and K-content's popularity. It connects 8,000 brands with Gen-Z fans, focusing on sellers and innovative marketing. With a presence in 13 countries, Musinsa aims to disrupt the fashion industry by creating a new ecosystem.
pages.title: Musinsa's Global Expansion and K-Fashion's Rise

pages.abstract: Musinsa Standard store in Seoul highlights its community-driven approach to fashion and lifestyle, catering to young people's interests. It differentiates itself in the e-retailing market by focusing on community engagement, curation, and personalized recommendations rather than gamification.
pages.title: Musinsa Standard Store and Ecosystem

pages.abstract: Musinsa focuses on supporting sellers and up-and-coming designers, investing in brands, and expanding its customer base to include older demographics. The company secured $190 million in funding and is expanding offline presence in Korea. Its global strategy involves introducing westernized brands and expanding to other markets like Tokyo, Bangkok, or Singapore.
pages.title: Musinsa's Fashion Ecosystem and Global Expansion

pages.abstract: Brand marketing is expected to regain prominence as the fashion industry shifts focus from performance marketing to long-term brand-building strategies. Key insights highlight the need for marketers to engage shoppers differently due to rising costs and data privacy regulations, with 71% of executives planning increased spending on brand marketing in 2024.
pages.title: 08. All Eyes On Brand

pages.abstract: The page discusses the shift in marketing spend from performance marketing to brand marketing in the fashion industry. It highlights the increasing focus on brand storytelling and the benefits of brand marketing in capturing new customer bases. The page also provides examples of successful brand marketing strategies, such as Hugo Boss's image reboot.
pages.title: More executives expect to increase spending on brand marketing than performance marketing

pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of customer perception and cross-funnel strategy for chief marketing officers. It highlights Zegna's brand refresh and collaboration with Fear of God, as well as New Balance's use of collaborations and targeted marketing. The Brand Marketing Toolkit section emphasizes the role of brand storytelling and emotional affinity, leveraging personalities behind brands and other community-building strategies.
pages.title: Chief marketing officers and their teams will need a laser-sharp focus on customer perception and cross-funnel strategy
Jacquemus Pop-Up

pages.abstract: The document discusses the revitalization of brands through craftsmanship, memorable shopping moments, and cross-industry collaborations. It emphasizes the importance of emotional connections, immersive experiences, and strategic storytelling for long-term brand success. The focus shifts from performance marketing to brand marketing, requiring a cohesive team of specialists and a long-term strategy.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: Olivier Bialobos, Dior's Deputy Managing Director, discusses the challenges and strategies in balancing tradition, innovation, and scale to drive the luxury brand's growth and desirability.
pages.title: Dior: Balancing Tradition, Innovation and Scale

pages.abstract: This page discusses Olivier Bialobos' role in shaping Christian Dior's communications strategy over 18 years, highlighting the brand's growth, revenue projections, and marketing challenges in the digital age. It emphasizes the importance of desirability, values, and sustainability in luxury branding, while also exploring Dior's cultural initiatives like museum exhibitions.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: The text discusses the evolution of Dior's brand codes and values under different designers, emphasizing the importance of unifying fashion and beauty messages. It highlights the role of visual language, ambassadors, and the creative processes of designers in maintaining Dior's iconic status while adapting to changing times.
pages.title: How can the codes and values of a brand like Dior change over time?

pages.abstract: The fashion industry is transitioning from self-regulation to new sustainability rules, impacting consumers and businesses globally. Up to 16 EU legislations are in discussion, affecting the entire value chain. Regulatory compliance must be integrated across all functions.
pages.title: 09. Sustainability Rules

pages.abstract: The fashion industry faces stricter sustainability regulations, particularly from the EU, targeting areas like product design, waste management, and reporting. These rules aim to reduce environmental impact, combat greenwashing, and promote transparency, with significant implications for brands and consumers globally.
pages.title: The Heat is On

pages.abstract: This page outlines sustainability regulations impacting the fashion and textile industries in the EU and US. It details adopted, proposed, and draft regulations, covering extended producer responsibility, reporting, due diligence, eco-design, waste management, green claims, microplastics, labelling, and worker protection. The EU focuses on circularity and transparency, while the US emphasizes emissions reporting and supply chain accountability.
pages.title: Sustainability regulations impacting fashion and textiles are on the horizon

pages.abstract: The page discusses the global regulatory landscape for fashion sustainability, highlighting initiatives in the US, UK, and China. It emphasizes the need for holistic approaches and traceability in supply chains to achieve regulatory compliance and meaningful progress.
pages.title: Fashion System

pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for decarbonising the fashion industry, focusing on sourcing and production, design, and end-of-life waste. It highlights the importance of energy efficiency, sustainable materials, and innovative business models like resale and recycling. The text also emphasizes the need for regulatory competence and strategic partnerships to navigate upcoming regulations and create a greener horizon.
pages.title: Sourcing and production, Design, End-of-life waste

pages.abstract: This page discusses Rachel Arthur's insights on how the UN aims to guide brands in promoting sustainability. It highlights the increasing importance of sustainability regulations in 2024 and emphasizes the role of marketers in improving the fashion industry's operations by adjusting communication strategies to combat overproduction and overconsumption.
pages.title: Rachel Arthur: How the UN Wants Brands to Sell Sustainability

pages.abstract: The document discusses the UN's call for fashion brands to stop promoting overconsumption, highlighting the role of marketing in driving unsustainable practices. It introduces the Sustainable Fashion Communication Playbook, which aims to align communication with sustainability goals. Key recommendations include avoiding greenwashing, shifting consumer culture, and promoting circular solutions like resale and repair. The playbook emphasizes the need for tailored approaches in different markets.
pages.title: The State of Fashion 2024

pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges of shifting towards sustainable fashion practices, emphasizing the need for marketers to promote sustainable lifestyles despite conflicting KPIs. It highlights the importance of advocacy, education, and policy changes to address overconsumption and waste, while also considering the role of businesses and workers in achieving sustainability.
pages.title: Fashion System: Sustainability and Advocacy

pages.abstract: Consumer demand changes have led to the bullwhip effect, pressuring fashion suppliers. To meet renewed demand, brands should focus on transparency and strategic partnerships. Key insights include significant upstream supplier impact, expected challenges for supplier relationships, and potential capacity improvements in textile factories by Q3 2024.
pages.title: Bullwhip Snaps Back

pages.abstract: The bullwhip effect has caused significant disruptions in the fashion industry's supply chain, leading to a sharp decline in factory utilization, layoffs, and delayed investments. Changes in consumer demand are magnified at each step from retailers to raw material suppliers, resulting in overcompensation and decreased order volumes. The pullback has disproportionately impacted upstream suppliers, with fabric exports dropping nearly 20 percent in the last quarter of 2022.
pages.title: The “bullwhip effect” disproportionately impacts upstream suppliers who have seen up to a 50 percent drop in order volumes

pages.abstract: The page discusses the significant decline in textile production and exports, highlighting the impact on factories and workers in various countries. It mentions the closure of factories, reduced capacity, and labor issues such as strikes and job losses. The text also notes the humanitarian crisis and supply-chain volatility affecting the textile industry.
pages.title: The Bullwhip Snaps

pages.abstract: The document discusses challenges in the textile industry, including worker displacement, skills loss, and supply chain disruptions. It highlights the need for brands to make their supply chains more resilient through transparency, strategic partnerships, and worker rights initiatives. The text also addresses sustainability regulations and the importance of investing in infrastructure for speed and sustainability.
pages.title: Navigating Disruption

pages.abstract: David Savman, Chief Supply Chain Officer at PVH Corp, discusses strategies for transforming supply chains through trust and transparency amidst geopolitical, macroeconomic, and consumer shifts expected to intensify in 2024.
pages.title: PVH Corp: Transforming Supply Chains Through Trust and Transparency

pages.abstract: The document discusses the importance of strong relationships in supply chain management, particularly in the fashion industry. It emphasizes the need for transparency, strategic partnerships, and agility in inventory and supply planning to navigate market fluctuations and build resilient business models.
pages.title: Supply Chain Relationships in Fashion

pages.abstract: The document discusses the importance of trust and better data in global supply chains, emphasizing the need for diverse sourcing strategies, transparency, and human rights in supply chains. It highlights the role of technology and traceability in sustainability and the critical human aspect often overlooked. The solution involves building strong relationships, ensuring accuracy, and maintaining trust to handle demand fluctuations and grow businesses sustainably.
pages.title: The solution is based on better data, but it’s also based on something as simple as trust.
McKinsey Global Fashion Index

pages.abstract: The fashion industry showed resilience in 2022, driven by the luxury segment's growth through price increases. Despite macroeconomic challenges, strong revenues and cost discipline protected margins. The mid-market faced pressure, but luxury's top players dominated. Polarisation increased, with 'Super Winners' gaining more economic profit. LVMH led the Super Winners, and sportswear brands like Nike performed well. Economic uncertainty persists, but the luxury segment supports profitability.
pages.title: Resilience Buoyed by Luxury

pages.abstract: The fashion industry showed strong financial performance in 2022, with economic profit (EP) near 2021 levels. The McKinsey Global Fashion Index (MGFI) tracks financial development and value creation. Despite challenges like geopolitical uncertainty and inflation, the industry maintained revenue gains and cost control, achieving average adjusted EBITA margins of almost 12%. The EP index hit 203 in 2022, just 12 points lower than the record set in 2021.
pages.title: After a strong recovery in 2021, industry economic profit was maintained in 2022

pages.abstract: The luxury segment drove economic profit growth, with pricing-led strategies and resilient consumer spending. Mid-market and value/discount segments suffered, with mid-market EP dropping significantly. Pricing adjustments were key for profitability, with luxury brands excelling. Margin improvements were crucial for sustaining elevated EP levels.
pages.title: Luxury was the main segment driving economic profit while others, particularly the mid-market, suffered

pages.abstract: Luxury segment saw significant margin improvements, outperforming other segments. High-income shoppers maintained spending, while lower-income consumers cut back. Affordable luxury improved year-on-year but remained below long-term averages. Premium/bridge, mid-market, and value/discount segments suffered, with mid-market experiencing the largest decline. Luxury now accounts for nearly half of the industry's total EP, with an EP index of 90. LVMH posted a record performance with €79.2 billion in revenue.
pages.title: Luxury also saw the greatest margin improvements

pages.abstract: The fashion industry is experiencing increased polarisation, with luxury brands driving significant economic profit growth. The top 20% of companies account for 125% of industry EP, while the bottom 20% account for most losses. Luxury margins and revenues have improved, but mid-market and value/discount margins have contracted. The industry is returning to pre-pandemic polarisation patterns.
pages.title: The industry is once again showing signs of increased polarisation

pages.abstract: The fashion industry experienced a shift in 2021 with value creators outnumbering destroyers for the first time since 2014. Luxury brands like LVMH and Hermès performed well, while mid-market players faced challenges. The top 20 companies saw an increase in EP levels, with the top 10 generating 81% of the EP. New entrants in the Super Winners list reflect post-pandemic consumer behavior, with luxury and sportswear brands showing strong performance. Department stores experienced a rebound in 2021 but face challenges in the business model.
pages.title: Super Winners

pages.abstract: The exhibit highlights the top 20 players in economic profit for 2022, showing luxury brands like LVMH and Hermès leading, while sports brands reshuffle. It also indicates changes in market cap and rank compared to 2019-2021, with some brands showing significant growth and others declining.
pages.title: Luxury leads the Super Winners, while sports players reshuffle

pages.abstract: The document discusses the correlation between company size and EP production, highlighting the significant performance of Super Winners. It addresses inventory challenges during the pandemic, noting the divide between luxury and non-luxury segments. The sportswear segment is analyzed, showing rapid growth and the emergence of new players like Lululemon and On, alongside established brands like Nike and Anta.
pages.title: Inventory Headaches and Sportswear Segment Deep Dive

pages.abstract: The online pure play segment faced challenges in 2022, with a shift towards improving bottom lines. Luxury and sportswear sectors showed resilience, while mass-market businesses struggled. The industry is expected to maintain steady margins, with luxury driving performance. Uncertainty in the economic environment may lead to further deterioration in performance.
pages.title: Segment Deep Dive: Online Pure Players

pages.abstract: The top 20 companies significantly increased their economic profit (EP) in 2022, while others experienced a decline. The EP is highly concentrated among the top 10 companies. Inventory challenges escalated above pre-pandemic historical averages in 2022, with inventory value as a percentage of revenues reaching higher levels compared to previous years.
pages.title: In 2022, the top 20 companies increased their EP while others shrank
