It emphasizes the expertise and perspectives offered in the report, aimed at M&A leaders across various industries.
pages.title: Top M&A trends in 2024: Blueprint for success in the next wave of deals.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_4.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the potential for a new era in M&A in 2024, highlighting the volatility of the global M&A market from 2020 to 2023. Despite challenges, dealmakers are optimistic. The durability of M&A is supported by factors like AI, sustainability, and tech-enabled consumer demands. Analysis shows that companies making small to midsized deals annually outperform others in shareholder returns.
pages.title: Will 2024 launch a bright new era for M&A?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_5.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the trends in M&A activities, highlighting the success of programmatic acquirers in managing portfolios and divesting nonstrategic assets. It also mentions the impact of cash as a source of ballast and the challenges faced by private equity investors. The text further explores the favorable macroeconomic environment, including inflation rates, job growth, and consumer spending, while noting the rising concern about geopolitical instability.
pages.title: Top M&A trends in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: The 2023 M&A market experienced a significant decline, with global deal value falling 16% to $3.1 trillion. Despite an increase in average deal size, the number of companies changing hands decreased by 27%. The performance of various sectors and regions may indicate recovery areas. Analysts remain optimistic about corporate prospects for 2024, predicting 5% revenue growth and gains in EBITDA and net earnings.
pages.title: What we can learn from 2023 M&A market performance

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: The Americas remained the most active M&A market in 2023, with deal value slightly trailing 2020 despite a 7% decline. EMEA faced challenges, with M&A value and volume dropping. APAC saw a 19% decline in M&A value but remains attractive for acquirers, especially in fast-growing economies. Expect robust dealmaking in APAC as multinationals seek opportunities.
pages.title: M&A Trends in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the significant role of the energy and materials sector in M&A activities in 2023, highlighting a shift towards corporate dealmaking. It also notes the dominance of domestic deals and a slight increase in cross-regional activity.
pages.title: Global energy and materials accounted for the largest share of M&A activity in 2023.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: Global M&A activity surged in 2023, with a 41% increase in the fourth quarter compared to the third. The value reached $1 trillion, up 37% from the previous year. The number of companies changing hands and average deal size also increased, reflecting a growing sense of optimism in the market.
pages.title: Deals between regions increased in 2023.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: The fourth quarter of 2023 saw a significant surge in global M&A deal value, with all regions contributing. The Americas saw a 39% increase in company value changes and a 47% growth in average deal size. EMEA experienced a 60% rise in deal activity value and a 63% increase in average deal size. APAC showed a 29% rise in M&A activity value from the third quarter and a 15% increase from the previous year, being the only region with a rise in transaction numbers.
pages.title: Global deal value jumped in the fourth quarter of 2023.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines key steps for companies to prepare for potential M&A transactions in 2024, emphasizing strategy updates, risk mitigation, value creation, partnerships, and alternative deal structures to navigate the evolving M&A landscape.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: The chemicals industry faces cyclical challenges, and M&A is a key strategy for value creation. With signs of an upturn in M&A activity, companies should take bold actions like aspirational transformations and aggressive capital allocation. Preparing for successful M&A execution is crucial, considering the industry's specific nuances.
pages.title: Chemicals: Success through timely, tailored action

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how chemicals companies are exploring M&A as a strategic tool to adapt and thrive in the current industry paradigm. The accompanying image highlights agricultural activities, symbolizing the industry's connection to resource management.
pages.title: Chemicals companies and M&A strategic shifts

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: The chemicals sector has underperformed the global stock market index for more than two years. Historical drivers of outperformance are less prevalent, and companies are seeking new strategic shifts. M&A activity in the chemicals industry has been significantly impacted by global challenges.
pages.title: Industry underperformance requires bold action

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: The chemicals sector has seen a decline in M&A activity, with global M&A deal value decreasing by 14% and chemicals M&A by 30% over the past few years. This underperformance is attributed to market corrections. M&A trends in the chemicals industry are shifting towards sub-sector themes and megadeals, with consolidation in specific segments like agriculture chemicals and personal care.
pages.title: Global M&A and deals in the chemicals sector have slowed in the past few years.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the significant role of megadeals in the chemicals M&A market over the past decade, supported by data on total M&A activity and chemicals' share of deal value. It explains the industry's success in creating value through large deals and compares different M&A approaches.
pages.title: Megadeals have played a big role in the chemicals M&A market over the past decade.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: The chemicals industry has succeeded with large M&A deals more than other industries. Successful dealmakers pursue focused platforms for geographic or product depth, complemented by a programmatic approach with smaller deals and divestitures.
pages.title: In chemicals, both programmatic and large-deal M&A can deliver excess TSR.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses recent drivers of programmatic chemicals M&A, focusing on consumer markets, sustainability, and geographic optimization. It highlights the importance of aligning M&A strategies with consumer trends, sustainability goals, and local market needs. The text also emphasizes the need for tailored integration plans to maximize value creation and avoid common pitfalls in the chemicals industry.
pages.title: Recent drivers of programmatic chemicals M&A

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses two common failure modes in transformational expectations: focusing solely on cost synergies and setting unrealistic revenue targets. It emphasizes the importance of understanding deal rationales, protecting target company culture, and ensuring operational readiness on day one for successful integration.
pages.title: Successfully delivering on transformational expectations requires avoiding two typical failure modes.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: The integration team should define day one critical escalation processes for potential risks and rehearse plans with stakeholders. Companies must protect and nurture technical talent, especially researchers and scientists, by offering creative incentives and strategic location planning.
pages.title: The integration team should define day one critical escalation processes for both companies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges of retaining technical and R&D talent, emphasizing the need for more than just financial incentives. It highlights the importance of thoughtful organizational strategies, such as rotations and hybrid work models, to support innovation. Additionally, it underscores the significance of M&A activities in the chemicals industry and the need for a deep understanding of both M&A basics and industry-specific nuances.
pages.title: Retaining technical and R&D talent requires more than traditional financial retention measures.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_30.jpg

It highlights the total deal value by target region in billions of dollars for fiscal year 2023, showing a significant increase in APAC and Americas compared to EMEA. The number of deals also varies across the regions, with APAC leading in 2021 but declining in subsequent years.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_32.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of thoughtful M&A strategies for growth in the technology, media, and telecom sectors. It highlights the interconnectedness of TMT companies, their reliance on M&A for growth, and the challenges faced in 2023, including a decline in transactions and value. Despite these challenges, M&A remains a key growth driver, with examples from technology, media, and telecom sectors illustrating strategic acquisitions and consolidations.
pages.title: Thoughtful M&A strategies are key to growth in tech, media, and telecom

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: The page highlights TMT's substantial contribution to global M&A activity in 2023, maintaining a 17% share, a slight decrease from the previous year. The visual of a telecommunications tower emphasizes the industry's role.
pages.title: TMT's Contribution to Global M&A Activity

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: Programmatic M&A offers superior shareholder returns compared to other M&A strategies, particularly in the TMT sector. It generates excess total shareholder returns of 2.3 percent, outperforming large deals and selective M&A. The data highlights the enduring value of programmatic M&A in creating better outcomes for companies.
pages.title: The enduring value of programmatic M&A

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the dominance of small deals in the TMT sector, the prevalence of megadeals, and the central role of software in M&A activity. It highlights trends such as consolidation in telecom, expansion into new areas by media and tech players, and the expected continued activity in software M&A in 2024, driven by factors like declining valuations, rising confidence, and strategic acquisitions.
pages.title: Technology: Software remains the center of activity

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for successful companies to strengthen integration and organic scaling capabilities through cross-selling, portfolio reconfiguration, and programmatic M&A approaches in the media sector. It highlights the importance of technological capabilities, management knowledge, and careful consideration of market dynamics and regulatory concerns.
pages.title: Winners will significantly strengthen their integration and organic scaling capabilities.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses various strategies employed by media and telecom companies in M&A activities, including media vertical heroes, beyond-media conglomerates, and digital disruptors. It highlights the importance of adapting M&A approaches due to cautious competition authorities and showcases the success of programmatic M&A in the telecom sector.
pages.title: Players need to be cautious as government competition authorities have struck down several horizontal mergers.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the top telecom M&A trends in 2023, focusing on EMEA's dominance and themes like consolidation, de-layering, and diversification. It highlights the need for operators to adapt to changing market dynamics and regulatory pressures.
pages.title: An erosion in value from traditional telecom products will force players to look elsewhere for returns.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges and opportunities in diversification within the TMT sector, emphasizing the demand for new services beyond connectivity. It highlights the growing regulatory scrutiny affecting technology, media, and telecom sectors, detailing specific regulatory concerns and their impacts. The outlook for 2024 and beyond focuses on the dynamic nature of these sectors, the importance of programmatic M&A, and the need for strategic portfolio re-evaluation.
pages.title: Caution: Regulatory obstacles need attention

pages.abstract: The fact sheet provides a summary of deal values in the life sciences sector from 2020 to 2023, categorized by APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions. The Americas consistently held the highest deal value, with a peak of 517 billion dollars in 2021. The number of deals fluctuated, with the highest count in 2021 at 1224.
pages.title: Life sciences Fact sheet

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_41.jpg
pages.abstract: The page details the share of activity by subsector for FY 2023, showing Biotech as the dominant sector in both deal value and volumes. It also presents the average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023, highlighting significant fluctuations in the Pharma and Biotech sectors.
pages.title: Share of activity by subsector, FY 2023

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_42.jpg
pages.abstract: The life sciences M&A sector experienced a revival in 2023 after a dip during the pandemic, with pharmaceutical companies focusing on growth and medtech companies on profitability. Deal value peaked at $517 billion in 2021, and the number of deals increased significantly between 2019 and 2021. The sector promises continued activity in 2024.
pages.title: Life sciences M&A shows new signs of life

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: The document highlights a significant 23% increase in transaction values in 2023 compared to the previous year, surpassing pre-pandemic levels of 2020, indicating a robust recovery and growth in the market.
pages.title: Transaction Value Growth in 2023

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_44.jpg
pages.abstract: The life sciences sector experienced increased deal activity in 2023, contrasting with the global M&A market's decline. Biotechs sought financial support from big pharma and PE players, while medtechs optimized portfolios. Large transactions like Pfizer's Seagen acquisition impacted transaction value, but most deals were smaller biotech-related ones. Biotech and pharma deals dominated volume and value, while smaller medtech deals contributed less to value.
pages.title: Unlike the global M&A market, the life sciences sector saw deal activity increase in 2023.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the programmatic approach to M&A in the life sciences sector, focusing on smaller biotech-related transactions. It highlights the benefits of this approach, such as higher TSR and strategic acquisitions. The pharmaceutical industry is particularly suited for this method, with small deals enabling focused acquisitions and global market access. The document also explores how pharma companies target precommercial biotech assets to accelerate R&D and reduce timelines, emphasizing the importance of thoughtful integration and alignment between acquiring and target companies.
pages.title: Most of the deals in the sector remained smaller biotech-related transactions aimed at generating growth.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of accelerating product launches and scaling commercial presence in pharmaceutical deals. It highlights the role of clean teams in developing plans and the significance of culture and talent retention in successful acquisitions. The text emphasizes the challenges of integrating small companies with large pharmaceutical firms and the need for thoughtful cultural integration.
pages.title: Culture looms especially large in pharmaceutical deals because so many deals involve large companies acquiring small companies.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: Medtech companies are adapting to financial pressures by reshaping their portfolios, focusing on digital offerings, and exploring creative transaction structures to enhance value creation and secure higher valuations in the capital markets.
pages.title: In search of profitability: Medtech deals manage the portfolio proactively

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: Medtech companies are exploring non-traditional transaction structures like joint ventures and strategic partnerships to fuel growth. The M&A outlook for 2024 is promising due to strong balance sheets and a focus on new technologies. Companies are shedding noncore assets and considering spinning off parts of their portfolio to pursue higher aggregate growth.
pages.title: Medtech companies look at growth across the portfolio and spin off lower-growth businesses in pursuit of higher aggregate growth.

pages.title: Top M&A trends in 2024

pages.abstract: The fact sheet presents the total deal value by target region in the financial services sector from January 2020 to December 2023. It shows the deal values for APAC, EMEA, and Americas, along with the number of deals each year. The Americas region had the highest deal value in 2021, while APAC had the highest in 2022. The number of deals peaked in 2021 and declined in subsequent years.
pages.title: Financial services Fact sheet

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_51.jpg
pages.abstract: The page details subsector activity in FY 2023, highlighting deal values and volumes across various banking sectors. It also tracks the average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023, with Financing solutions showing the most growth.
pages.title: Subsector activity, FY 2023

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_52.jpg
pages.abstract: The financial services M&A outlook is promising, with a focus on growth and capabilities. Despite fewer deals, average sizes have increased. Notable 2023 deals include UBS acquiring Credit Suisse and JPMorgan Chase's First Republic deal. Most large deals aimed to rebalance portfolios or acquire failing banks' assets, with some focused on scale and technology.
pages.title: Rebound of financial services M&A: Focus on growth and capabilities

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_53.jpg
pages.title: The industry needs M&A to grow, innovate, and become more resilient.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_54.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the expected trends in M&A activities in the financial services sector for 2024, emphasizing the importance of capability-building and scale efforts. It highlights that while many institutions have M&A strategies, best practices are not yet standardized. The text also explores how scale and capability deals will dominate as banks seek growth avenues, with a focus on building scale, acquiring capabilities, and selective carve-outs. The banking sector's performance and regional differences are also analyzed.
pages.title: Some best practices in M&A have yet to become the norm.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_55.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how recent advances in banking business models enhance cross-border M&A transactions, focusing on technology adoption, customer service improvements, and strategic acquisitions. pages.title: Creating value with M&A in Asia’s diverse marketplace

pages.abstract: The page highlights that 65% of deal value in 2023 was concentrated in four key sectors: energy and materials, advanced industries, tech, media, and telecom (TMT), and financial services, indicating a significant focus on these industries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_128.jpg
pages.abstract: The Asia-Pacific region continues to account for about a quarter of global deal activity by value. Domestic in-country activity within the region still accounts for more than 70 percent of M&A value, but the share of activity originating from other regions rose in 2023. Many acquirers in slower-growth regions found promising targets in APAC in the fastest-growing countries and in those with less geopolitical risk. In contrast, GDP growth in the European Union and the United States was low in 2023, and foreign direct investment in China declined partly due to geopolitical tensions and tougher regulatory scrutiny.
pages.title: Asia-Pacific continues to account for about a quarter of global deal activity by value.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_129.jpg
pages.abstract: The value of inbound acquisitions from the Americas and EMEA increased significantly in 2023, with net-positive deal inflow in Australia and India. Cross-border in-region deal value rose to 12%, driven by large deals in Singapore and Greater China. Investors in the Middle East showed increased interest. About 65% of deal value occurred in energy and materials, advanced industries, tech, media, and telecom sectors.
pages.title: The value of inbound acquisitions from the Americas and EMEA rose sharply in 2023.

It highlights the challenges of due diligence in the region and identifies four main trends driving inbound deal activity, with a focus on the energy transition and sustainability-related dealmaking.
pages.title: Powerful trends are now driving inbound dealmaking

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_131.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses trends in corporate strategies, focusing on partnerships with Chinese technology firms, the attractiveness of consumer-facing sectors in APAC, and the importance of carve-outs and divestitures for aligning portfolios with overall strategies. It highlights examples such as Stellantis's investment in Leapmotor and Dai-ichi Life Holdings' investment in RenewBuy.
pages.title: Carve-outs and divestitures should continue as companies align their portfolios with overall strategies and shed low-growth, low-margin businesses.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_132.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the increasing trend of companies in the APAC region responding to activist demands, consolidating, and restructuring to boost efficiencies and growth. It highlights the acquisition of Toshiba and United Malt Group as examples. The text also outlines four key capabilities that will distinguish successful acquirers in APAC in 2024, emphasizing the importance of understanding local markets and building relationships.
pages.title: Four capabilities will distinguish the most successful acquirers in APAC in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_133.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses key M&A trends in 2024, focusing on maintaining constant tabs on acquisition targets, empowering local M&A teams, exploring diverse deal structures, and adapting to cultural nuances during integration. It highlights the importance of trust-building, local expertise, and cultural fit in successful M&A deals.
pages.title: Top M&A trends in 2024

pages.page_path: library_pages\Top M&A trends in 2024_ Blueprint for success in trends_McKinsey\page_134.jpg
pages.abstract: This page emphasizes the importance of cultural differences in mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the APAC region. It highlights the need for acquirers to understand working norms, governance practices, and decision-making processes at every integration stage. A case study of a US-based manufacturer acquiring a Japanese conglomerate illustrates the value of cultural alignment. The conclusion stresses the unique opportunities and risks in APAC, urging acquirers to invest in deep insights and culturally astute integration for long-term success.
pages.title: We urge acquirers to pay close attention to cultural differences—working norms, governance practices, and how decisions are made—at every stage of integration.

This page introduces the inaugural annual report on global M&A trends in 2024, highlighting the increase in M&A activity in Q4 2023 and McKinsey's role in supporting clients through M&A transactions. It emphasizes the expertise and perspectives offered in the report, aimed at M&A leaders across various industries.
The document discusses the potential for a new era in M&A in 2024, highlighting the volatility of the global M&A market from 2020 to 2023. Despite challenges, dealmakers are optimistic. The durability of M&A is supported by factors like AI, sustainability, and tech-enabled consumer demands. Analysis shows that companies making small to midsized deals annually outperform others in shareholder returns.
The document discusses the trends in M&A activities, highlighting the success of programmatic acquirers in managing portfolios and divesting nonstrategic assets. It also mentions the impact of cash as a source of ballast and the challenges faced by private equity investors. The text further explores the favorable macroeconomic environment, including inflation rates, job growth, and consumer spending, while noting the rising concern about geopolitical instability.
The 2023 M&A market experienced a significant decline, with global deal value falling 16% to $3.1 trillion. Despite an increase in average deal size, the number of companies changing hands decreased by 27%. The performance of various sectors and regions may indicate recovery areas. Analysts remain optimistic about corporate prospects for 2024, predicting 5% revenue growth and gains in EBITDA and net earnings.
The Americas remained the most active M&A market in 2023, with deal value slightly trailing 2020 despite a 7% decline. EMEA faced challenges, with M&A value and volume dropping. APAC saw a 19% decline in M&A value but remains attractive for acquirers, especially in fast-growing economies. Expect robust dealmaking in APAC as multinationals seek opportunities.
The page discusses the significant role of the energy and materials sector in M&A activities in 2023, highlighting a shift towards corporate dealmaking. It also notes the dominance of domestic deals and a slight increase in cross-regional activity.
Global M&A activity surged in 2023, with a 41% increase in the fourth quarter compared to the third. The value reached $1 trillion, up 37% from the previous year. The number of companies changing hands and average deal size also increased, reflecting a growing sense of optimism in the market.
The fourth quarter of 2023 saw a significant surge in global M&A deal value, with all regions contributing. The Americas saw a 39% increase in company value changes and a 47% growth in average deal size. EMEA experienced a 60% rise in deal activity value and a 63% increase in average deal size. APAC showed a 29% rise in M&A activity value from the third quarter and a 15% increase from the previous year, being the only region with a rise in transaction numbers.
This page outlines key steps for companies to prepare for potential M&A transactions in 2024, emphasizing strategy updates, risk mitigation, value creation, partnerships, and alternative deal structures to navigate the evolving M&A landscape.
This page discusses the M&A trends in Asia's diverse marketplaces, highlighting the varying activities in different regions and the importance of understanding local cultures and business practices. It also provides contact information for comments and additional resources for further insights.
This page introduces the topic of industry sector updates and emerging trends, setting the stage for detailed information on M&A trends in 2024.
The fact sheet provides a summary of deal values in the chemicals and agriculture sector from 2020 to 2023, categorized by target regions (APAC, EMEA, Americas). The total deal value and number of deals are presented for each year, showing fluctuations in investment across regions over the four-year period.
The page presents data on the share of activity by subsector for FY 2023, showing deal values and volumes dominated by other chemicals. It also illustrates the average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023, with other chemicals maintaining the highest average deal size.
The chemicals industry faces cyclical challenges, and M&A is a key strategy for value creation. With signs of an upturn in M&A activity, companies should take bold actions like aspirational transformations and aggressive capital allocation. Preparing for successful M&A execution is crucial, considering the industry's specific nuances.
This page discusses how chemicals companies are exploring M&A as a strategic tool to adapt and thrive in the current industry paradigm. The accompanying image highlights agricultural activities, symbolizing the industry's connection to resource management.
The chemicals sector has underperformed the global stock market index for more than two years. Historical drivers of outperformance are less prevalent, and companies are seeking new strategic shifts. M&A activity in the chemicals industry has been significantly impacted by global challenges.
The chemicals sector has seen a decline in M&A activity, with global M&A deal value decreasing by 14% and chemicals M&A by 30% over the past few years. This underperformance is attributed to market corrections. M&A trends in the chemicals industry are shifting towards sub-sector themes and megadeals, with consolidation in specific segments like agriculture chemicals and personal care.
The page discusses the significant role of megadeals in the chemicals M&A market over the past decade, supported by data on total M&A activity and chemicals' share of deal value. It explains the industry's success in creating value through large deals and compares different M&A approaches.
The chemicals industry has succeeded with large M&A deals more than other industries. Successful dealmakers pursue focused platforms for geographic or product depth, complemented by a programmatic approach with smaller deals and divestitures.
This page discusses recent drivers of programmatic chemicals M&A, focusing on consumer markets, sustainability, and geographic optimization. It highlights the importance of aligning M&A strategies with consumer trends, sustainability goals, and local market needs. The text also emphasizes the need for tailored integration plans to maximize value creation and avoid common pitfalls in the chemicals industry.
This page discusses two common failure modes in transformational expectations: focusing solely on cost synergies and setting unrealistic revenue targets. It emphasizes the importance of understanding deal rationales, protecting target company culture, and ensuring operational readiness on day one for successful integration.
The integration team should define day one critical escalation processes for potential risks and rehearse plans with stakeholders. Companies must protect and nurture technical talent, especially researchers and scientists, by offering creative incentives and strategic location planning.
This page discusses the challenges of retaining technical and R&D talent, emphasizing the need for more than just financial incentives. It highlights the importance of thoughtful organizational strategies, such as rotations and hybrid work models, to support innovation. Additionally, it underscores the significance of M&A activities in the chemicals industry and the need for a deep understanding of both M&A basics and industry-specific nuances.
The fact sheet provides an overview of deal values in the technology, media, and telecommunications sectors across APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions. It highlights the total deal value by target region in billions of dollars for fiscal year 2023, showing a significant increase in APAC and Americas compared to EMEA. The number of deals also varies across the regions, with APAC leading in 2021 but declining in subsequent years.
The page presents data on deal activity by subsector in FY 2023, showing Tech as the dominant sector in both deal value and volume. The average deal size trends indicate Telecom had a significant peak in 2021, while Tech remained stable.
This page discusses the importance of thoughtful M&A strategies for growth in the technology, media, and telecom sectors. It highlights the interconnectedness of TMT companies, their reliance on M&A for growth, and the challenges faced in 2023, including a decline in transactions and value. Despite these challenges, M&A remains a key growth driver, with examples from technology, media, and telecom sectors illustrating strategic acquisitions and consolidations.
The page highlights TMT's substantial contribution to global M&A activity in 2023, maintaining a 17% share, a slight decrease from the previous year. The visual of a telecommunications tower emphasizes the industry's role.
Programmatic M&A offers superior shareholder returns compared to other M&A strategies, particularly in the TMT sector. It generates excess total shareholder returns of 2.3 percent, outperforming large deals and selective M&A. The data highlights the enduring value of programmatic M&A in creating better outcomes for companies.
This page discusses the dominance of small deals in the TMT sector, the prevalence of megadeals, and the central role of software in M&A activity. It highlights trends such as consolidation in telecom, expansion into new areas by media and tech players, and the expected continued activity in software M&A in 2024, driven by factors like declining valuations, rising confidence, and strategic acquisitions.
This page discusses strategies for successful companies to strengthen integration and organic scaling capabilities through cross-selling, portfolio reconfiguration, and programmatic M&A approaches in the media sector. It highlights the importance of technological capabilities, management knowledge, and careful consideration of market dynamics and regulatory concerns.
This page discusses various strategies employed by media and telecom companies in M&A activities, including media vertical heroes, beyond-media conglomerates, and digital disruptors. It highlights the importance of adapting M&A approaches due to cautious competition authorities and showcases the success of programmatic M&A in the telecom sector.
The page discusses the top telecom M&A trends in 2023, focusing on EMEA's dominance and themes like consolidation, de-layering, and diversification. It highlights the need for operators to adapt to changing market dynamics and regulatory pressures.
The document discusses the challenges and opportunities in diversification within the TMT sector, emphasizing the demand for new services beyond connectivity. It highlights the growing regulatory scrutiny affecting technology, media, and telecom sectors, detailing specific regulatory concerns and their impacts. The outlook for 2024 and beyond focuses on the dynamic nature of these sectors, the importance of programmatic M&A, and the need for strategic portfolio re-evaluation.
The fact sheet provides a summary of deal values in the life sciences sector from 2020 to 2023, categorized by APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions. The Americas consistently held the highest deal value, with a peak of 517 billion dollars in 2021. The number of deals fluctuated, with the highest count in 2021 at 1224.
The page details the share of activity by subsector for FY 2023, showing Biotech as the dominant sector in both deal value and volumes. It also presents the average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023, highlighting significant fluctuations in the Pharma and Biotech sectors.
The life sciences M&A sector experienced a revival in 2023 after a dip during the pandemic, with pharmaceutical companies focusing on growth and medtech companies on profitability. Deal value peaked at $517 billion in 2021, and the number of deals increased significantly between 2019 and 2021. The sector promises continued activity in 2024.
The document highlights a significant 23% increase in transaction values in 2023 compared to the previous year, surpassing pre-pandemic levels of 2020, indicating a robust recovery and growth in the market.
The life sciences sector experienced increased deal activity in 2023, contrasting with the global M&A market's decline. Biotechs sought financial support from big pharma and PE players, while medtechs optimized portfolios. Large transactions like Pfizer's Seagen acquisition impacted transaction value, but most deals were smaller biotech-related ones. Biotech and pharma deals dominated volume and value, while smaller medtech deals contributed less to value.
The document discusses the programmatic approach to M&A in the life sciences sector, focusing on smaller biotech-related transactions. It highlights the benefits of this approach, such as higher TSR and strategic acquisitions. The pharmaceutical industry is particularly suited for this method, with small deals enabling focused acquisitions and global market access. The document also explores how pharma companies target precommercial biotech assets to accelerate R&D and reduce timelines, emphasizing the importance of thoughtful integration and alignment between acquiring and target companies.
This page discusses the importance of accelerating product launches and scaling commercial presence in pharmaceutical deals. It highlights the role of clean teams in developing plans and the significance of culture and talent retention in successful acquisitions. The text emphasizes the challenges of integrating small companies with large pharmaceutical firms and the need for thoughtful cultural integration.
Medtech companies are adapting to financial pressures by reshaping their portfolios, focusing on digital offerings, and exploring creative transaction structures to enhance value creation and secure higher valuations in the capital markets.
Medtech companies are exploring non-traditional transaction structures like joint ventures and strategic partnerships to fuel growth. The M&A outlook for 2024 is promising due to strong balance sheets and a focus on new technologies. Companies are shedding noncore assets and considering spinning off parts of their portfolio to pursue higher aggregate growth.
The fact sheet presents the total deal value by target region in the financial services sector from January 2020 to December 2023. It shows the deal values for APAC, EMEA, and Americas, along with the number of deals each year. The Americas region had the highest deal value in 2021, while APAC had the highest in 2022. The number of deals peaked in 2021 and declined in subsequent years.
The page details subsector activity in FY 2023, highlighting deal values and volumes across various banking sectors. It also tracks the average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023, with Financing solutions showing the most growth.
The financial services M&A outlook is promising, with a focus on growth and capabilities. Despite fewer deals, average sizes have increased. Notable 2023 deals include UBS acquiring Credit Suisse and JPMorgan Chase's First Republic deal. Most large deals aimed to rebalance portfolios or acquire failing banks' assets, with some focused on scale and technology.
This page discusses the expected trends in M&A activities in the financial services sector for 2024, emphasizing the importance of capability-building and scale efforts. It highlights that while many institutions have M&A strategies, best practices are not yet standardized. The text also explores how scale and capability deals will dominate as banks seek growth avenues, with a focus on building scale, acquiring capabilities, and selective carve-outs. The banking sector's performance and regional differences are also analyzed.
This page discusses how recent advances in banking business models enhance cross-border M&A transactions, focusing on technology adoption, customer service improvements, and strategic acquisitions. It highlights the challenges of integrating fintechs and the role of private equity in the fintech sector.
The document discusses the future of carve-outs in banking, highlighting the challenges and opportunities they present. It also explores the consolidation and capabilities in asset management, emphasizing the need for firms to evaluate their strategies and adapt to changing market conditions.
The page discusses the decline in global assets under management by about 10 percent in 2022, highlighting challenges in asset management valuations and dealmaking. It emphasizes the need for successful acquisitions to focus on retaining top talent and suggests that effective acquirers should institutionalize M&A capabilities and adopt a proactive approach to market scanning for sustained growth.
Private equity firms face decisions on deploying $2 trillion in dry powder, with rigorous due diligence and compelling business cases required. Investors debate capital-heavy vs. capital-light businesses, favoring fintechs over B2Cs. Post-acquisition success hinges on strategic planning, organizational priorities, and long-term execution. Financial services M&A is expected to remain active, driven by growth, innovation, and resilience needs.
The fact sheet presents the total deal value by target region for consumer goods from January 2020 to December 2023. APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions show varying deal values and numbers of deals over the years, with APAC leading in deal value in 2021 and Americas showing a significant increase in deal value in 2023.
The page details subsector activities in FY 2023, showing deal values and volumes across consumer sectors. Consumer Personal Care leads in deal value, significantly influenced by the Kenvue spin-off. Consumer Food has the highest deal volume. The average deal size trends from 2020 to 2023 highlight Consumer Personal Care's substantial growth.
Consumer goods companies have diversified M&A strategies due to economic trends. Success requires tailored integration. Programmatic M&A has shifted focus due to macroeconomic trends. Players moved from large consolidation deals to smaller deals for growth. Recent inflation has led to focus on cost synergies and margin expansion. Future success depends on a hybrid deal approach combining investments in high-growth brands and portfolio consolidation.
Acquirers must adopt new strategies for integrating and supporting their acquisition targets in 2024, emphasizing a shift in approach to achieve successful outcomes.
This page discusses trends in consumer goods M&A, focusing on deal volume and value, deal frequency, and deal strategy. It highlights shifts in deal volume and value post-COVID, the dominance of food in deal volume, and the success of programmatic M&A strategies in delivering higher returns with lower risk.
Programmatic M&A strategies yield higher returns compared to selective and organic approaches. Across sectors, companies with the most programmatic deals outperform peers. Long-term success is linked to consistent programmatic M&A practices, especially among top global firms. Successful consumer goods companies build strong in-house M&A capabilities for strategy, execution, and integration.
The page discusses shifts in consumer goods M&A strategies, highlighting four archetypes: portfolio consolidation, adjacency plays, data and tech enablement, and challenger brands. It explains the transition from growth-focused strategies to a renewed focus on portfolio consolidation due to lower asset valuations and investor priorities. The outlook for the next wave of M&A emphasizes a shift towards cost synergies and integration.
The page discusses M&A trends in consumer goods, showing a shift towards historical norms. It highlights reduced multiples re-invigorating portfolio consolidation and a reduced deal volume compared to 2021-2022, with an expected uptick in 2024 due to higher interest rates and strategic buyers' advantages.
This page discusses successful M&A strategies in consumer goods, emphasizing the shift from gaining to giving in deals, and outlines three integration models: full integration, partial integration, and accelerator, each with its pros and cons.
This page discusses successful integration strategies for consumer goods companies, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding the target company's unique assets and refraining from seeking immediate operational efficiencies. It highlights the need for careful assessment of integration approaches and building unique M&A capabilities, including trend prediction skills.
Companies achieve better M&A results by applying a repeatable playbook, developing in-house M&A skills, and fostering career growth for professionals. A strong M&A engine is crucial for consumer goods companies to succeed in today's market.
The fact sheet provides a breakdown of deal values and number of deals in the travel, logistics, and infrastructure sectors from 2020 to 2023, categorized by APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions. The total deal value peaked in 2021 at $287 billion and declined to $113 billion in 2023. The number of deals was highest in 2022 with 465 deals.
The page presents data on the share of activity by subsector for FY 2023, including total deal value and volumes. Logistics dominates in both value and volume. The average deal size trends show significant fluctuations across subsectors from 2020 to 2023.
This page discusses the evolving landscape of M&A in transportation and logistics, highlighting the impact of the pandemic on supply chain execution and the resulting investment opportunities. It outlines the need for action on new investment priorities and the transformation of the industry by financial, market, and technology forces.
In 2023, the deal activity in the logistics sector slowed significantly, with both the value and volume of transactions declining. Companies with strong deal execution capabilities, like DSV and K+N, performed well. Transportation services remained the most active sector, with North Asia leading in deal numbers.
The TLI deal activity varied significantly across regions in 2022 and 2023, with Europe and North America showing the highest deal values. The average size of top deals dropped by 26%, and only 11 deals crossed the $1 billion threshold in 2023. CMA CGM remained active in dealmaking, expanding its global logistics presence. Disagreements on prices between buyers and sellers reflect differing views on the M&A landscape.
The page discusses the decline in deal value and volume for top logistics companies in 2023 due to tightened capital access and weakened logistics demand. It highlights a 26% drop in total deal value and a 24% decrease in average deal size. Despite these challenges, the outlook for 2024 is promising, with significant opportunities in logistics M&A as investors prepare for clearer market conditions and historic valuation multiples.
The page discusses the major forces transforming logistics and M&A in 2024, including financial, market, and technology forces. It highlights challenges such as rising costs, limited asset demand, and the need for complex supply chain designs. The increasing role of technology is emphasized as a key factor for competitive advantage.
The page outlines five key priorities for M&A investment in transportation and logistics, focusing on opportunistic acquisitions, expanding service portfolios, sustainability investments, integrating fragmented segments, and acquiring transformative technologies. These priorities aim to enhance value and address market dynamics.
This page outlines key strategies for investors in the transportation and logistics industry, emphasizing the acquisition of fragmented market segments and transformative technologies. It advises setting a clear vision, developing a value creation plan, and ensuring robust capabilities for successful M&A investments in 2024 and beyond.
This page discusses the imperative for strong portfolio management in businesses due to several trends. It highlights the need for companies to develop six capabilities to build and manage a winning portfolio using M&A strategically. The text explains how the pandemic and current economic conditions have changed the landscape, emphasizing the importance of thinking like a portfolio manager and adapting to new trends, such as central banks' actions against inflation.
This page highlights four key trends driving the need for tighter portfolio management. It visually represents teamwork and coordination through a rowing team, symbolizing the importance of strategic alignment in managing financial portfolios.
This page discusses trends impacting global business, including macroeconomic challenges, rapid technological disruption, and investor preferences for focused portfolios. It emphasizes the need for portfolio managers to develop six core capabilities, starting with a brutally honest review of their current portfolio to inform strategic decisions.
This page discusses the importance of locating promising playing fields and defining the right portfolio composition to maximize value. It highlights the role of portfolio momentum, the impact of headwinds and tailwinds, and the need for deep market understanding and scenario planning in making strategic decisions.
The document discusses five approaches to value creation in business portfolios, emphasizing the importance of strategic positioning and adaptability. These approaches include core centricity, vertical integration, diversification, transformation, and VC investment, each with specific focuses and rationales for creating value.
This page discusses various portfolio management strategies including core centricity, vertical integration, diversification, transformation, and venture capital investment. Each strategy is explained with examples and their implications for business operations and long-term success.
This page discusses the optimal rate for rotating a company's portfolio, highlighting that a refresh rate between 10% and 30% leads to the best outcomes in terms of excess TSR. It also emphasizes the importance of balancing organic and inorganic strategies for portfolio evolution.
Companies adopting a programmatic M&A strategy with a portfolio refresh rate of 10-30 percentage points achieved an average excess TSR of 6.2%. Boeing and LVMH exemplify successful technology and luxury acquisitions. A steady transaction cadence strengthens capabilities and market insights.
This page discusses strategies for maximizing portfolio value through various ownership models, including partnerships and divestments. It emphasizes the importance of understanding business operations for effective divestment timing and highlights the role of rigorous return logic and tailored KPIs in resource allocation and financial steering. Examples include Microsoft's success in cloud computing and Stellantis's KPI-based financial management.
This section discusses the importance of deploying an operational steering model that balances synergies and autonomy within a portfolio. It highlights the roles of holding companies as either active operators or strategic coordinators, depending on the portfolio's characteristics. The text emphasizes the need for leaders to understand current trends and develop capabilities for effective portfolio management.
Companies can benefit from green M&A by following a compelling rationale and tailored execution. This involves shifting assets to low-emissions models, pursuing deals linked to global energy transition elements, and enhancing integration approaches for better performance.
This page highlights the financial benefits of incorporating green deals in a programmatic approach, emphasizing that such acquirers outperform their peers in total shareholder return.
The document highlights the growing importance of sustainability in corporate strategies, with M&A playing a key role. Since 2013, the volume and value of green deals over $100 million have significantly increased, reflecting companies' efforts to integrate sustainability for competitive advantage and improved financial performance.
The past decade has seen a rise in green deals across various sectors, with significant growth in deal volume. Programmatic M&A, particularly involving green deals, has shown superior performance in terms of TSR and lower volatility. Green deal cultures differ from typical industry consolidations, necessitating active integration efforts.
The document discusses how a programmatic approach to green deals yields better outcomes compared to other M&A approaches. It highlights the importance of a clear deal rationale, considering various factors like acquisition price, market environment, and operational capabilities. Companies need a compelling rationale aligned with their corporate strategy and a tailored integration approach.
This page outlines five strategies for integrating green M&A, including increasing exposure to sustainable markets, pivoting to lower carbon technologies, securing green feedstock, building green energy supply, and enhancing product circularity. It emphasizes the need for a differentiated approach in green M&A due diligence and integration processes.
This page discusses the strategic importance of retaining talent and aligning cultures in green M&A deals. It highlights the need for operational integration, value creation through top-line growth, and addressing cultural differences. Successful integration requires tailored approaches, mutual discovery of business models, and a focus on talent and culture.
This page discusses the challenges of navigating delays in M&A deals, emphasizing the need for dealmakers to anticipate and prepare for contingencies. It highlights the increased delays experienced in major acquisitions over the past two years, attributed to factors like geopolitical tensions, complex integrations, and regulatory scrutiny. The content underscores the importance of a clear execution plan and the evolving nature of M&A deal processes.
This page discusses the growing prevalence and complexity of heightened regulatory reviews, which add significant time and uncertainty, leading to increased risks of extended delays in processes.
This page discusses the increasing complexity of regulatory reviews in M&A deals, highlighting the risks of delays and their negative impacts on value, momentum, and morale. It introduces the '4 Rs' framework—reflect, revise, reframe, and reinvigorate—to manage delays effectively and sustain momentum.
This page discusses the importance of readiness in dealing with potential delays in integration planning. It emphasizes the need for honest assessment, effective resource planning, and contingency plans. The text highlights the benefits of scenario planning and the importance of maintaining integrity and transparency. It also advises on pivoting to value-maximizing actions if delays occur.
This page discusses strategies for managing stakeholder relationships during delays in mergers and acquisitions. It emphasizes the importance of equipping leaders for heavy stakeholder management, reframing narratives to maintain confidence, and engaging employees to sustain momentum. Effective communication and development programs are highlighted as key factors in mitigating risks and ensuring deal success.
This page discusses the importance of performance-based retention programs in M&A deals, emphasizing the need to engage the acquiring company's integration team and manage delays effectively to maintain trust, morale, and focus among employees and leadership.
This page discusses the impact of delays in M&A processes on customer trust and service quality, emphasizing the importance of maintaining business-as-usual operations and clear communication. It concludes by highlighting the need for early planning and effective execution to sustain momentum and achieve value creation despite delays.
Effective people management is crucial for maintaining engagement and momentum during delays. Both verbal communication and actions play a significant role in sustaining this energy.
This page discusses the significant impact of culture on M&A performance, recommending early attention to cultural attributes for successful integration planning. It highlights the importance of addressing cultural fit and friction, and suggests focusing on five cultural attributes, starting with talent, to ensure positive outcomes.
This page highlights the regret of M&A executives who underestimated the importance of cultural integration in their business strategies, emphasizing the need for early and thorough attention to cultural aspects.
This page discusses key attributes for successful integration planning, emphasizing role clarity, performance management, customer focus, and efficient decision-making. It highlights the importance of selecting top talent for integration roles, providing tailored value propositions, and guiding principles for effective interaction with target company leaders.
This page discusses the importance of role clarity, performance management, and customer focus in integration planning. It emphasizes the need for clear leadership roles, aligned performance targets, and customer-centric strategies to ensure successful mergers and acquisitions.
This page discusses how company philosophies on setting targets can vary and highlights the importance of customer focus in integration planning. It also explores the challenges and solutions in decision-making processes during mergers and acquisitions, emphasizing the need for clear communication and collaboration.
This page discusses the importance of using culture to guide integration planning, emphasizing the need for open-minded understanding of cultural attributes and potential sources of friction. It outlines five 'no regrets' actions for a successful cultural integration plan, including selecting the right leaders, learning from customers, defining decision rights, factoring in target-setting differences, and engaging with employees of the target company.
This page discusses how M&A integrations can drive broader organizational transformations beyond mere combinational synergies. It highlights examples of companies using M&A to innovate, reshape business models, and attract talent, emphasizing the strategic importance of M&A in today's challenging business environment.
This page highlights four critical factors leaders should focus on for successful transformational M&A, based on research and experience. The visual metaphor of mixing paints suggests blending different elements for a successful outcome.
This page discusses the importance of focusing on four key factors—strategy, value, execution, and people—to achieve successful transformational M&A. It emphasizes the need for a transformational mindset and outlines opportunities for leaders to transform businesses through M&A at every stage of the M&A lifecycle. The section on strategy highlights the need for leaders to re-imagine the combined business and operating model for long-term value.
This page discusses identifying full-potential value creation opportunities, establishing an execution engine through an ITO, and developing talent and capabilities for successful M&A transformations. It emphasizes the need for bold, long-term views, empowered decision-making, and strategic talent development.
This page discusses key principles for transforming through M&A, emphasizing the need to think expansively about the combined business, build a strategic integration blueprint, and align on goals for faster growth and digital transformation.
This page discusses optimizing a company's portfolio during mergers and acquisitions, emphasizing the importance of assessing and divesting non-core assets. It highlights the benefits of a comprehensive portfolio review and provides an example from the life sciences industry. The text also covers identifying full-potential value-creation opportunities, stressing the need for aggressive action on revenue, cost, and capital, and the importance of long-term strategic planning.
This page discusses strategies for leadership teams to enhance their capability-building through prioritization, problem-solving, and influencing skills. It emphasizes the importance of strong governance, accountability, and speed in M&A integrations, as well as the need for rigorous stage-gate approval processes and talent development to ensure successful transformation.
This page discusses how integration processes in M&A can be leveraged for talent development and functional excellence. It highlights a case study of a chemical company that used a merger to elevate its procurement function through extensive training. The text emphasizes the importance of leaders considering transformation opportunities in M&A deals, balancing immediate needs with long-term strategy, and reimagining the combined business for sustained change.
Despite global M&A volatility, Asia remains attractive for growth opportunities due to its significant contribution to global GDP and economic growth. The region's emerging consumer class and economic resilience make it appealing for acquisitions despite geopolitical risks. APAC deal value declined in 2023 but still represents a quarter of global activity.
The page highlights that 65% of deal value in 2023 was concentrated in four key sectors: energy and materials, advanced industries, tech, media, and telecom (TMT), and financial services, indicating a significant focus on these industries.
The Asia-Pacific region continues to account for about a quarter of global deal activity by value. Domestic in-country activity within the region still accounts for more than 70 percent of M&A value, but the share of activity originating from other regions rose in 2023. Many acquirers in slower-growth regions found promising targets in APAC in the fastest-growing countries and in those with less geopolitical risk. In contrast, GDP growth in the European Union and the United States was low in 2023, and foreign direct investment in China declined partly due to geopolitical tensions and tougher regulatory scrutiny.
The value of inbound acquisitions from the Americas and EMEA increased significantly in 2023, with net-positive deal inflow in Australia and India. Cross-border in-region deal value rose to 12%, driven by large deals in Singapore and Greater China. Investors in the Middle East showed increased interest. About 65% of deal value occurred in energy and materials, advanced industries, tech, media, and telecom sectors.
The page discusses how MNCs are seeking opportunities in APAC through M&A, partnerships, and smaller acquisitions. It highlights the challenges of due diligence in the region and identifies four main trends driving inbound deal activity, with a focus on the energy transition and sustainability-related dealmaking.
This page discusses trends in corporate strategies, focusing on partnerships with Chinese technology firms, the attractiveness of consumer-facing sectors in APAC, and the importance of carve-outs and divestitures for aligning portfolios with overall strategies. It highlights examples such as Stellantis's investment in Leapmotor and Dai-ichi Life Holdings' investment in RenewBuy.
The page discusses the increasing trend of companies in the APAC region responding to activist demands, consolidating, and restructuring to boost efficiencies and growth. It highlights the acquisition of Toshiba and United Malt Group as examples. The text also outlines four key capabilities that will distinguish successful acquirers in APAC in 2024, emphasizing the importance of understanding local markets and building relationships.
This page discusses key M&A trends in 2024, focusing on maintaining constant tabs on acquisition targets, empowering local M&A teams, exploring diverse deal structures, and adapting to cultural nuances during integration. It highlights the importance of trust-building, local expertise, and cultural fit in successful M&A deals.
This page emphasizes the importance of cultural differences in mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the APAC region. It highlights the need for acquirers to understand working norms, governance practices, and decision-making processes at every integration stage. A case study of a US-based manufacturer acquiring a Japanese conglomerate illustrates the value of cultural alignment. The conclusion stresses the unique opportunities and risks in APAC, urging acquirers to invest in deep insights and culturally astute integration for long-term success.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_6.jpg

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the potential for a more sustainable and inclusive world, emphasizing the need for bold action on sustainability, economic efficiency, and innovation. It highlights progress made in reducing child mortality, increasing education, and decreasing extreme poverty over the past 30 years.
pages.title: The world has great potential to be more sustainable and inclusive

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the global disparities in growth, sustainability, and inclusion, highlighting the challenges faced by low- and middle-income countries in meeting the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. It also addresses the significant gaps in achieving net-zero emissions and the varying levels of income inequality and CO2 emissions among G20 countries. The text introduces the concept of the empowerment line as a measure of inclusion and global middle-class status.
