pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents data on global population distribution across countries based on various measures of growth, inclusion, and sustainability. It highlights disparities in GDP per capita, life expectancy, education, child mortality, digital and financial inclusion, and CO2 emissions. The data underscores that most people live in countries that do not meet goals for inclusion and sustainability.
pages.title: In a world where growth varies widely, most people live in countries that do not meet goals for inclusion and sustainability.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: This page compares G20 countries' performance in growth, inclusion, and sustainability using various indicators. It highlights significant differences in outcomes, with a heatmap visualizing the data. The G20 average is provided for reference.
pages.title: Among the G20 member countries, there are considerable differences in outcomes for growth, inclusion, and sustainability.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the relationship between economic growth and sustainability, highlighting the benefits of growth in fostering economic inclusion and capital formation. It also addresses the nuanced trend of growth and sustainability, noting the rise in CO2 emissions in low- and middle-income countries and the decline in high-income countries. The page further explores the potential impacts of achieving global goals, including improvements in life expectancy, education, child survival, internet access, and bank accounts, as well as significant reductions in CO2 emissions.
pages.title: Economic Growth and Sustainability

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_12.jpg
pages.abstract: This page examines the relationship between growth, inclusion, and sustainability in G20 countries over 20 years. It highlights the positive impact of growth on inclusion but notes mixed effects on sustainability. The data, presented as three-year rolling averages, shows trends in GDP per capita, capital formation, CO2 emissions, and population empowerment for both middle-income and high-income economies.
pages.title: Exhibit 3: Growth, inclusion, and sustainability in G20 countries

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the critical choices needed for sustainable and inclusive growth by 2050, emphasizing the need for global cooperation amid economic and social challenges. It highlights the importance of empowering households, educating children, and adapting to technological advancements.
pages.title: Our choices during this decade will determine whether we achieve the goal of sustainable, inclusive growth by 2050

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_14.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the urgency of addressing sustainability and inclusion, highlighting the world's projected depletion of its carbon budget by 2030. It outlines a new growth approach for the decade, aiming to economically empower households and transform energy and land-use systems, leading to net-zero emissions by 2050.
pages.title: This decade will be decisive in laying the foundation for a sustainable, inclusive, and growing future.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the empowerment gap and sustainability gap as measures for achieving inclusive and sustainable growth. It highlights the need for increased household spending and investment in low-emissions technologies to meet basic needs and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. The gaps vary significantly across countries, with sub-Saharan Africa and the United States requiring substantial increases in spending and investment.
pages.title: Reducing climate risks for inclusive and sustainable growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the empowerment gap and sustainability gap, quantifying resources needed for global needs. It shows daily spending across populations and investments in energy and land-use systems, emphasizing the additional money and investment required for empowerment and sustainability.
pages.title: Two measures, the empowerment gap and the sustainability gap, help quantify the resources required to meet the world’s needs.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: This page presents data on the resources needed to address empowerment and sustainability gaps in various regions. It highlights the substantial financial requirements and their impact on GDP, emphasizing the disparities between lower and higher GDP per capita regions. The data underscores the need for significant investments to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth by 2030.
pages.title: Significant resources are needed to fill the empowerment and sustainability gaps by 2030.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: This research defines economic empowerment as the daily spending needed for a decent standard of living, setting an empowerment line above the global poverty line. It uses a hybrid approach to establish thresholds for low, middle, and high-income countries, adjusting for savings and government provisions. The empowerment gap is calculated for each country, revealing that about 4.5 billion people worldwide are not yet economically empowered. The gap is computed by decile and country, with a linear ramp-up in spending to reach universal empowerment by 2030.
pages.title: Measuring economic inclusion: The empowerment gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the sustainability gap, defined as the additional investment needed in low-emissions technologies for countries to achieve net-zero emissions by 2030. It highlights the required capital allocation changes across various sectors and the projected $24.4 trillion investment gap. The text also addresses the role of innovation, policy, and the gradual shift from high-emissions to low-emissions assets, emphasizing the importance of careful planning and technological advancements.
pages.title: Measuring investment toward a net-zero world: The sustainability gap

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: Economic growth is essential for addressing empowerment and sustainability gaps, but it must be complemented by business-led innovation and inclusive policies to ensure a sustainable and inclusive future.
pages.title: Growth can boost sustainability and inclusion, but we need more than growth in its current form

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how growth, business-led innovation, and direct government support are essential to address empowerment and sustainability gaps. It highlights the role of innovation in making sustainability more affordable and presents a visual representation of how these factors contribute to closing these gaps by 2030.
pages.title: Growth, business-led innovation, and direct government support are necessary to fill the empowerment and sustainability gaps.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how innovation, government policies, and philanthropy can contribute to inclusive growth and sustainability. It highlights the need for strategic shifts in business practices and public resources allocation to address income disparities and environmental challenges. The text also explores the trade-offs and choices in implementing such policies and the potential impact of economic growth on closing empowerment and sustainability gaps.
pages.title: Innovation, Government, and Philanthropy for Inclusive Growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: The document illustrates how growth alone varies in narrowing empowerment and sustainability gaps across different regions. It highlights the share of funding covered by baseline growth and the remaining share needed in each region. For instance, Sub-Saharan Africa shows a 6% empowerment gap funded by growth and a 25% gap left to fill, while China shows 88% funded by growth and a 42% gap remaining. The data underscores the need for additional investment in various regions to meet sustainability goals.
pages.title: The ability of growth alone to narrow the empowerment and sustainability gaps varies by country and region.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: Companies play a crucial role in driving baseline growth and achieving sustainability and inclusion. They contribute significantly to GDP, drive productivity, and create jobs. However, to fully close the gaps, companies need to innovate and collaborate with stakeholders, focusing on inclusive and sustainable growth strategies.
pages.title: Companies will be major players in the new growth imperative

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights the significant economic contributions of companies in G20 countries, detailing their investments, employment, revenue, and impacts on stakeholders. It also outlines their potential to contribute to sustainable and inclusive growth through equitable value sharing, environmental protection, empowerment of individuals, health promotion, and infrastructure development.
pages.title: Companies in the G20 member countries are hugely important economic contributors—and they will be equally important contributors to sustainable, inclusive growth.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: Companies face challenges in aligning their financial incentives with global sustainability and inclusion goals. They may hesitate to invest in worker training or innovative products due to uncertain returns. Despite this, companies are crucial partners in addressing these challenges, as they are linked to existing issues like worker income and emissions.
pages.title: Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future: The role of business

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: Companies must prioritize sustainability and inclusion, determining when to act independently or collaborate. They can expand markets through sustainable innovations or reduce costs by improving efficiency. Shifting demographics emphasize sustainability as a key value.
pages.title: A starting point is for companies to sort out what their priorities are, when they can act independently, and when they should collaborate

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how companies can enhance sustainability and inclusion by leveraging existing opportunities or creating new ones. It outlines various business logics for action, including independent action, industry collaboration, public-private partnering, and shaping with government. Examples are provided for each category, demonstrating practical steps businesses can take. The page emphasizes the importance of innovation, convening, partnership, and co-creation with public institutions.
pages.title: Companies can improve sustainability and inclusion by seizing existing opportunities or by helping shape new ones.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of collaboration among companies, governments, and the social sector for sustainable and inclusive growth. It highlights the need for new standards, public-private partnerships, and government intervention in addressing market externalities. The text also emphasizes the role of economic returns, orchestration, and public-private collaboration in achieving societal goals.
pages.title: Collaboration for Sustainable Growth

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges of reducing air pollution and the potential for public and philanthropic capital to catalyze private financing in sustainable and inclusive areas. It highlights the need for collaboration among stakeholders and the role of B20 Indonesia in creating initiatives for carbon trading, women's empowerment, and global vaccination.
pages.title: Where can public and philanthropic capital catalyze larger flows of private financing?

pages.page_path: library_pages\Toward a sustainable, inclusive, growing future_ McKinsey_2022_12_01\page_31.jpg
pages.abstract: This page introduces the authors and acknowledges the contributions of various collaborators, including business leaders, academic advisers, and team members who supported the research on B20 Indonesia's initiatives.
pages.title: About the authors and acknowledgments

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_1.jpg
pages.title: Transforming the EU Retail & Wholesale Sector

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_2.jpg
pages.title: Key authors and Core team

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_3.jpg
pages.title: Contents

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_4.jpg
pages.abstract: This page introduces the transformative changes occurring in the retail and wholesale industry, setting the stage for further discussion on the evolving landscape.
pages.title: INTRODUCTION

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_5.jpg
pages.title: Store Welcome Scene

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_6.jpg
pages.abstract: The EU retail and wholesale sector, comprising nearly 5 million enterprises, faces transformation driven by sustainability, digitalization, and skills. Sustainability involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions, digitalization focuses on e-commerce growth and data analytics, and skills emphasize workforce upskilling. These changes aim to enhance resilience, productivity, and environmental responsibility.
pages.title: Sustainability, Digitalization, Skills – Transforming the EU retail & wholesale sector

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_7.jpg
pages.abstract: European retailers and wholesalers invest less than their counterparts in other regions, particularly in North America. This investment gap, especially in IT spending, could become a liability as competition intensifies globally in the digital age. The sector needs substantial investment to achieve more efficient, robust, and sustainable business models.
pages.title: European retailers and wholesalers invest less than other players.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_8.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector faces significant challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic and supply-chain disruptions. To maintain profitability, investments in sustainability, digitalization, and skills are crucial. Collaboration and policy support are key to achieving long-term goals. A survey of 24 companies highlights the need for transformation in these areas by 2030, with varied actions required for different company sizes.
pages.title: The retail and wholesale sector is important to the European Union—and it will have to invest to keep pace in a dynamic global market.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_9.jpg
pages.abstract: The EU retail and wholesale sector faces challenges due to mature markets, inflation, and declining consumer incomes. Two scenarios estimate the cost of transformation, with large companies bearing most of the investment. Stakeholders must collaborate to achieve EU objectives.
pages.title: INTRODUCTION

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_10.jpg
pages.abstract: The page outlines three key investment areas for the EU retail and wholesale sector by 2030: sustainability, digitalization, and skills. It details ambitious and conservative investment figures for each area, emphasizing net-zero operations, circular business models, seamless customer experiences, and workforce training.
pages.title: FOCUS OF INVESTMENTS THROUGH 2030

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_11.jpg
pages.abstract: The document outlines the cumulative investment needs for sustainability, digitalization, and skills and talent in the EU retail and wholesale sector from 2023 to 2030. It highlights the required investment levels and their impact on the sector's total annual revenue, emphasizing the need for additional investments to achieve the necessary transformations.
pages.title: Each of the three transformations will require additional investments through 2030.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_12.jpg
pages.title: SUSTAINABILITY

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_13.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines key takeaways for achieving green growth in a sector by 2030, emphasizing investments, emission reductions, and collaboration with value chain partners for sustainability and consumer education.
pages.title: Key takeaways

pages.abstract: The EU aims to cut GHG emissions by 55% by 2030 and reach net zero by 2050, requiring significant investment in net-zero operations, sustainable offerings, and circularity. The majority of emissions are Scope 3, linked to the production and consumption of goods. The sector also impacts biodiversity, waste generation, and livelihoods.
pages.title: The status quo

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_15.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the significant contributions of food, home improvement, and fashion and apparel to EU retail and wholesale GHG emissions, highlighting the pressure for sustainability transformation from various stakeholders. It also covers the growing consumer demand for sustainable options, investor adoption of ESG criteria, and regulatory goals set by the UN and EU for decarbonization.
pages.title: Food, home improvement, and fashion and apparel have the largest contributions to EU retail and wholesale GHG emissions.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_16.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the difference between carbon neutrality and net zero, emphasizing the need for comprehensive GHG emission reductions across all scopes. It highlights the current status of European retailers and wholesalers in setting decarbonization targets and the challenges in achieving the EU's overall reduction target. The page also touches on the broader aspects of sustainability beyond decarbonization, including resource efficiency, biodiversity, and health.
pages.title: CARBON NEUTRALITY VERSUS NET ZERO

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_17.jpg
pages.abstract: Retailers and wholesalers can drive sustainability by reducing emissions, improving circularity, and promoting sustainable consumption. They can benefit from cost savings and new revenue streams. Harmonized standards and cross-value-chain collaboration can accelerate transformation. The sector can reduce GHG emissions and support EU sustainability agenda.
pages.title: Potential developments by 2030

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_18.jpg
pages.abstract: Retailers and wholesalers can drive sustainability through net-zero operations, sustainable offerings, and circularity. Cooperation among stakeholders and addressing structural challenges will accelerate the transition to a sustainable sector, with an estimated investment of €135-335 billion by 2030. Two scenarios assess the potential cost and impact of this transformation.
pages.title: If they act fast and decisively, retailers and wholesalers will be able to best combine what’s good for the planet with what’s good for their business.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_19.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the sustainability transformation as a win-win-win opportunity for the sector, the EU, and society. It outlines the required cash-out for net-zero operations, sustainable offerings, and circularity and waste management. The focus is on reducing Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions through renewable energy, net-zero stores and warehouses, net-zero fleets, and sustainable manufacturing. The document emphasizes the importance of optimizing operations and transitioning to green energy for retailers and wholesalers.
pages.title: The sustainability transformation is a win-win-win opportunity for the sector, the EU, and society.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_20.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the challenges and opportunities of switching to green energy for retailers and wholesalers, emphasizing the importance of self-generation of renewable energy, virtual Power Purchase Agreements, and digital solutions for energy optimization. It highlights the potential for significant reductions in GHG emissions and energy costs through decarbonizing stores and warehouses.
pages.title: While making operational changes would require substantial investment, most levers have a positive net present value (NPV) or are at least NPV neutral.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_21.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses strategies for retailers and wholesalers to achieve net-zero emissions through warehouse and fleet decarbonization. Key points include reducing energy consumption, switching to green energy, and adopting electric vehicles (EVs) for fleets. The decarbonization process is multiphased, with different technologies achieving cost parity at various times. The page also highlights the importance of optimizing logistics and infrastructure for sustainability.
pages.title: Electric vehicles will reach total cost of ownership (TCO) parity with diesel across segments by 2025; later for hydrogen.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_22.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses how retailers and wholesalers can contribute to sustainability through sustainable manufacturing, offering, and private-label products. It highlights strategies like green energy, water reduction, and sustainable design. Collaboration with suppliers and clear consumer information are key to accelerating the EU sustainability agenda.
pages.title: In effect, retailers may help to accelerate the transformation of the entire value chain and fulfill the larger EU sustainability agenda.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_23.jpg
pages.abstract: Regenerative agriculture offers sustainable production practices, reducing GHG emissions, enhancing soil health, and improving biodiversity. It faces challenges like potentially lower yields and a lack of consumer awareness but holds high profit potential through carbon credits and cost savings. Retailers and wholesalers can play a crucial role in promoting and supporting regenerative agriculture.
pages.title: REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_24.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the use of marginal abatement cost curves (MACC) to determine the impact and cost of decarbonization levers for branded products. It highlights the importance of understanding GHG emissions and sustainability effects at the product level. The page also presents a global high-level MACC for generic tablets, showing the abatement cost and potential for various levers such as green electricity in aluminum production and low-carbon magnesium sourcing.
pages.title: Most of the emissions from tablets stem from the production of energy-intensive semiconductors.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_25.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the benefits of shifting to plant-based diets in grocery stores, including reduced GHG emissions, decreased deforestation, and improved human health. It highlights a case study showing significant GHG emission reductions when substituting beef and milk with plant-based alternatives. Retailers are encouraged to consider stakeholder needs while implementing such initiatives.
pages.title: Sustainable Offering in Grocery

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_26.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of circularity and waste management in the retail and wholesale sector, emphasizing the shift from linear to circular business models to reduce waste and create value. It highlights potential benefits such as incremental revenues, cost savings, and improved customer relationships. The page also covers circular packaging and products, detailing potential levers and challenges in implementation.
pages.title: Circularity and waste management

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_27.jpg
pages.abstract: The apparel and fashion sector has significant potential for circularity, with current fiber production heavily reliant on virgin feedstock. Opportunities include increasing circular product models, establishing collection infrastructure, and reducing waste across the value chain. Retailers and wholesalers can play a crucial role in promoting sustainability through waste reduction strategies.
pages.title: The apparel and fashion sector has huge potential to become more circular.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_28.jpg
pages.abstract: This page outlines strategies for grocers to reduce upstream food loss by 50-70%, detailing various levers such as minimizing production/processing loss, transit loss, selling more of what is produced, and structurally preventing loss. It emphasizes collaboration with suppliers, optimizing supply chains, and improving crop resilience.
pages.title: Grocers can reduce upstream food loss by 50 to 70 percent.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_29.jpg
pages.abstract: This section discusses the roadblocks faced by European retailers and wholesalers in achieving sustainability targets, including prioritization of other investments, conflicts of interest in digitalization, capability gaps, funding uncertainties, lack of harmonized standards, higher sourcing costs, and technological limitations. It also highlights the challenges faced by SMEs and suggests potential solutions to accelerate sustainability transformation.
pages.title: 4. Roadblocks and potential solutions

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_30.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses direct and indirect cross-sector enablers for sustainability in the retail and wholesale sectors. Direct enablers include harmonized regulation, standardized sustainability metrics, and dedicated financing. Indirect enablers involve infrastructure development, research and innovation, and precompetitive collaboration spaces. These measures aim to support the entire value chain and promote sustainable practices.
pages.title: Direct and Indirect Cross-sector Enablers

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_31.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the challenges and opportunities of the sustainability transformation in the retail and wholesale sector. It highlights the need for collaboration, consumer education, data transparency, and company-specific enablers such as investment, management attention, capabilities, KPIs, and central steering. It also emphasizes the importance of consumer information and the potential benefits of sustainability efforts.
pages.title: The sustainability transformation of the sector is a major challenge, and it will require major investment. However, it could also present an opportunity for companies to save costs, create new business models, and differentiate themselves from the competition.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_32.jpg
pages.title: DIGITALIZATION

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_33.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights key takeaways about the digital transformation, emphasizing the need for substantial investment, the disruption and growth opportunities presented by digital megatrends, and the importance of accelerating digital adoption for resilience.
pages.title: Key takeaways

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_34.jpg
pages.abstract: Digitalization is reshaping the retail and wholesale sector, requiring substantial investment in technology and capabilities. The sector must modernize IT, enhance digital interactions, and integrate brick-and-mortar stores with the digital world. Automation, AI, and advanced analytics will transform the value chain, improving supply-chain management, store operations, and customer experience. The European Commission has set digital targets for the sector, aiming for widespread digital intensity by 2030.
pages.title: Digitalization is reshaping retail and wholesale on the front lines and behind the scenes

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_35.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses the projected growth of e-commerce penetration in EU-27 countries from 15% in 2020 to 30% by 2030, highlighting various retail subsectors. It emphasizes the need for digital transformation in retail and wholesale sectors, including training employees, creating digital touchpoints, and investing in digital channels, automation, advanced analytics, and IT modernization. The ongoing shift from physical to digital channels is driven by increasing consumer demand, and digital interactions are expected to become the norm for purchases.
pages.title: E-commerce penetration is likely to grow from 15 to 30 percent by 2030 within EU-27 countries.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_36.jpg
pages.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the growth of pure-digital players and the expectation for seamless cross-channel experiences. E-commerce will drive top-line growth but disrupt markets with declining profitability in some sectors. The shift to digital channels will necessitate repurposing commercial real estate to prevent obsolescence.
pages.title: The share of pure-digital players keeps growing, and more digitally savvy customers expect seamless experiences across channels.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_37.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the value of advanced analytics in various domains, highlighting that 10 out of 100 use cases account for over 80% of the value at stake. It covers topics like marketing, store operations, supply-chain management, and automation, emphasizing the potential benefits and challenges in the retail and wholesale sectors. The page also mentions the impact of demographic changes and the increasing importance of advanced analytics and AI.
pages.title: Ten of the 100 advanced analytics use cases represent more than 80 percent of the value at stake.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_38.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the increasing value of advanced analytics in the retail and wholesale sector, highlighting its potential for better pricing, personalized promotions, and improved product selection. It emphasizes the need for IT modernization to keep pace with digital-native companies and the importance of attracting and retaining data specialists. The text also mentions the expected growth in data volume and the benefits of a modernized IT architecture for seamless customer experiences.
pages.title: As more companies grow aware of the value at stake, the use of advanced analytics could become the norm for the entire sector in the EU.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_39.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the digital transformation journey of retailers and wholesalers, highlighting the need for investment in IT and digitalization. It emphasizes the importance of digital transformation as a core business strategy and outlines key areas for investment, including digital channels, automation, advanced analytics, and IT modernization. The page also provides insights into the current investment levels in digital transformation and the projected additional investment required by 2030.
pages.title: Actions for consideration

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_40.jpg
pages.abstract: The sector must undertake seven key actions and invest €155–230 billion by 2030 to fully benefit from digital transformation. These actions include expanding digital channels, automating processes, deploying advanced analytics, and modernizing IT infrastructure. The required investment is 0.4–0.6% of the sector's annual revenues, with specific allocations for different areas of the value chain.
pages.title: The sector needs to take seven key actions and invest an additional €155–230 bn by 2030 to get the full benefits of the digital transformation.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_41.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the expansion of digital sales channels in the retail sector, focusing on supply-chain logistics, digital sales channel development, and reinvention of brick-and-mortar stores. It highlights the required investments, the role of SMEs, and the impact on traditional stores. The text also explores the adoption of in-store technologies like RFID and self-checkout solutions to enhance productivity and customer experience.
pages.title: Digital channels

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_42.jpg
pages.abstract: This page highlights the expectation of customers for a seamless shopping experience, bridging online and offline interactions. It emphasizes the importance of integrating digital tools with physical store operations to enhance customer service and satisfaction.
pages.title: Customers expect a seamless experience; for example, they may want to use their online shopping cart as the basis for a discussion with sales personnel in a physical store.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_43.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the potential for automation in retail and wholesale sectors, focusing on warehouses and support functions. It highlights the benefits of advanced analytics and the need for modernizing legacy IT systems to enhance digitalization. The page also emphasizes the importance of upgrading IT architecture for seamless customer experiences.
pages.title: Digitalization in Retail and Wholesale

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_44.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the liberation of data from silos, enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency through robust data technology. It emphasizes the importance of a high-performing IT operating model for speed and agility, modularization of systems, and the transformation of IT architecture in two steps. It also highlights the benefits of reducing IT running costs and investing in internal technological expertise.
pages.title: High-performing operating model

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_45.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses two scenarios for digital transformation in the EU retail and wholesale sector, detailing conservative and ambitious investment strategies. It also highlights the importance of cybersecurity and IT modernization for digital transformation, and identifies roadblocks such as cost-driven mindsets and short-term profitability concerns.
pages.title: SCENARIOS

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_46.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses the challenges of digitalization for retailers and wholesalers, including high costs, lack of scale, talent shortages, and complex regulations. It suggests potential solutions such as stakeholder collaboration, learning programs, access to capital, and regulatory alignment to accelerate digital transformation.
pages.title: As the evolution of the market accelerates, the message is clear: adapt or fall behind.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_47.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses the importance of digitalization in the EU retail and wholesale sector, emphasizing the need for internal commitment, resource allocation, and skill development. It highlights challenges and opportunities, urging companies to adapt to evolving market demands.
pages.title: Digitalization in EU Retail & Wholesale

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_48.jpg
pages.abstract: Retailers and wholesalers need to accelerate skill and talent transformation for employee lifelong learning and competitiveness.
pages.title: SKILLS AND TALENT

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_49.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector employs 26 million EU workers, playing a crucial role in education and training. To address the Triple Transformation, it needs to train 13 million employees and hire 1.5 million new workers annually until 2030. The additional investment required for workforce transformation could reach €25-35 billion by 2030, on top of the €50-70 billion already planned.
pages.title: Key takeaways

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_50.jpg
pages.abstract: The EU retail and wholesale sector faces a significant skills and talent transformation challenge. With only half of the workforce ready for change, the industry must hire millions of new employees and invest in training to meet evolving customer expectations and business dynamics. SMEs face particular challenges in this regard.
pages.title: Skills and Talent in the EU Retail and Wholesale Sector

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_51.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector is a major employer in the EU, with food retail, SMEs, and store operations being key subsectors. The workforce is diverse, offering career opportunities and training, but faces challenges in maintaining its role as an education engine through skill and talent transformation.
pages.title: Food retail, SMEs, and store operations account for the largest share of employees by subsector, company size, and function respectively.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_52.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector faces challenges of increasing productivity, evolving skills and roles, and attracting talent. The shift to e-commerce and omnichannel strategies drive the need for new skills in digital and analytics. The sector may need to upskill millions of employees and hire new talent by 2030, with a focus on data scientists, digital marketing specialists, and user experience experts.
pages.title: 2. The transformation

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_53.jpg
pages.abstract: The page discusses how various roles in retail and logistics are changing due to automation and digitalization, with a focus on new skills and responsibilities in areas like cashiering, sales, warehouse operations, transportation, category management, and HR. It highlights the need for analytical and technical skills to adapt to these changes.
pages.title: How Functions and Roles Could Change

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_54.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector faces a critical talent shortage, with a high job vacancy rate. To remain competitive, companies need clear talent strategies, including role migration plans and a compelling employee value proposition. By 2030, significant upskilling and hiring of skilled employees will be required, with substantial investment in workforce development. SMEs face particular challenges and may need external support.
pages.title: Becoming a magnet for talent has become critical

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_55.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses potential actions for upskilling in the retail and wholesale sector, including skilling, upskilling, reskilling, and attraction and retention. It highlights the importance of vocational education and training (VET) and the need for continuous improvement and adaptation to new skill requirements. The document also mentions the role of internal training programs and the combination of remote and in-person learning methods.
pages.title: Actions for consideration

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_56.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses various upskilling programs, including government-driven, sector-driven VET, company training, cooperation with educational institutions, scholarships, and reskilling. It highlights the importance of training for employee transition and the need for flexible work models and diverse inclusion programs to attract and retain talent in the retail and wholesale sector.
pages.title: Examples of Existing Upskilling Programs

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_57.jpg
pages.abstract: European retailers and wholesalers face challenges in optimizing people development models and attracting top talent due to limited workforce readiness and difficulties in recruitment and retention.
pages.title: Skills and Talent

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_58.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses roadblocks and potential solutions in the European retail and wholesale sector, focusing on workforce readiness, training investment, talent scarcity, and the increasing need for higher qualifications. It highlights challenges such as high attrition rates and low training investment in SMEs, emphasizing the need for continuous learning and sector-specific measures to address these issues.
pages.title: 4. Roadblocks and potential solutions

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_59.jpg
pages.abstract: The document discusses cross-sector enablers for skill and talent transformation in the EU retail and wholesale sector, focusing on professional education systems. It outlines two scenarios for estimating the potential cost of transformation, considering changes in roles and skills, and investments in up-/reskilling. The conservative scenario assumes 40% employee development and 800,000 new jobs annually, while the ambitious scenario assumes 50% development and 1,500,000 new jobs annually until 2030.
pages.title: 4.1 Cross-sector enablers

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_60.jpg
pages.abstract: The retail and wholesale sector can benefit from higher education, partnerships, and funding for internal training to support workers' transitions to new roles. Collaboration with educational institutions, sector-wide campaigns, and skills-as-a-service models can enhance employee skills and appeal.
pages.title: The sector could benefit from funding for internal training to support workers' transitions to new roles.

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_61.jpg
pages.abstract: This page discusses company-specific enablers for retailers and wholesalers, focusing on HR resources and technological infrastructure. It highlights the need for proactive training and recruitment strategies, as well as the importance of investing in upskilling and reskilling the workforce. The retail and wholesale sector's role in providing career opportunities and lifelong learning is emphasized.
pages.title: Company-specific enablers

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_62.jpg
pages.title: Glossary

pages.page_path: library_pages\Transforming the EU retail and wholesale sector_McKinsey_2025_01_01\page_63.jpg
pages.title: Glossary

The EU retail and wholesale sector, comprising nearly 5 million enterprises, faces transformation driven by sustainability, digitalization, and skills. Sustainability involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions, digitalization focuses on e-commerce growth and data analytics, and skills emphasize workforce upskilling. These changes aim to enhance resilience, productivity, and environmental responsibility.
European retailers and wholesalers invest less than their counterparts in other regions, particularly in North America. This investment gap, especially in IT spending, could become a liability as competition intensifies globally in the digital age. The sector needs substantial investment to achieve more efficient, robust, and sustainable business models.
The retail and wholesale sector faces significant challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic and supply-chain disruptions. To maintain profitability, investments in sustainability, digitalization, and skills are crucial. Collaboration and policy support are key to achieving long-term goals. A survey of 24 companies highlights the need for transformation in these areas by 2030, with varied actions required for different company sizes.

Automation, AI, and advanced analytics will transform the value chain, improving supply-chain management, store operations, and customer experience. The European Commission has set digital targets for the sector, aiming for widespread digital intensity by 2030.

It emphasizes the need for digital transformation in retail and wholesale sectors, including training employees, creating digital touchpoints, and investing in digital channels, automation, advanced analytics, and IT modernization. The ongoing shift from physical to digital channels is driven by increasing consumer demand, and digital interactions are expected to become the norm for purchases.
The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the growth of pure-digital players and the expectation for seamless cross-channel experiences. E-commerce will drive top-line growth but disrupt markets with declining profitability in some sectors. The shift to digital channels will necessitate repurposing commercial real estate to prevent obsolescence.

These actions include expanding digital channels, automating processes, deploying advanced analytics, and modernizing IT infrastructure. It also highlights the benefits of reducing IT running costs and investing in internal technological expertise.

To address the Triple Transformation, it needs to train 13 million employees and hire 1.5 million new workers annually until 2030. The additional investment required for workforce transformation could reach €25-35 billion by 2030, on top of the €50-70 billion already planned.

The workforce is diverse, offering career opportunities and training, but faces challenges in maintaining its role as an education engine through skill and talent transformation.
The retail and wholesale sector faces challenges of increasing productivity, evolving skills and roles, and attracting talent. The shift to e-commerce and omnichannel strategies drive the need for new skills in digital and analytics. The sector may need to upskill millions of employees and hire new talent by 2030, with a focus on data scientists, digital marketing specialists, and user experience experts.

It highlights the need for analytical and technical skills to adapt to these changes.

To remain competitive, companies need clear talent strategies, including role migration plans and a compelling employee value proposition. By 2030, significant upskilling and hiring of skilled employees will be required, with substantial investment in workforce development. SMEs face particular challenges and may need external support.

It highlights the importance of vocational education and training (VET) and the need for continuous improvement and adaptation to new skill requirements. The document also mentions the role of internal training programs and the combination of remote and in-person learning methods.

This page compares traditional and tech-enabled approaches in product management, sales, customer experience, and field service, highlighting how generative AI transforms B2B service delivery through advanced analytics, personalized content, and real-time support.
This page compares key functions in traditional and tech-enabled worlds, covering failure root cause, self-service, remote first, support services, and performance management. It highlights the shift from manual and historical data-based approaches to real-time, AI-driven, and augmented reality solutions.
This page discusses how AI can enhance aftermarket and service organizations by supporting the sales force through market to order, order to delivery, and delivery to cash processes. It highlights five key capabilities: granular view of customer opportunities, offers tailored to customer needs, relentless pursuit of sales opportunities, optimal pricing strategies, and outstanding customer experience.
The page discusses the challenges industrial companies face in deploying digital tools, including data preparation, cybersecurity, and software development. A 2022 McKinsey survey highlights the difficulty in identifying suitable software partners. As digital capabilities grow in importance, more attention will be needed in this area.
This page outlines ten pivotal lessons for service industries, emphasizing the importance of B2C-like customer experiences, servitization, data monetization, softwarization of features, sustainability, remotization, and localization paradigms in driving growth and resilience.
The page discusses the importance of offering a B2C-like customer experience in the aftermarket and service sector. It highlights the shift towards personalization and hyperpersonalization in marketing, sales, and products, which is seen as a key differentiator for successful B2B companies. The content also mentions the role of online marketplaces, product ecosystems, and handling workforce disruptions in enhancing customer satisfaction and business growth.
This page discusses how training sessions and servitization strategies enhance customer satisfaction and internal processes. It highlights a case study of a heavy-equipment OEM that used digital apps to reduce order deviations and improve communication. The concept of servitization is explained, emphasizing its benefits in converting one-off sales into recurring revenue and providing access to capital-intensive products. Examples like Rolls-Royce's pay-by-the-hour contracts illustrate the value of servitization in expanding business scope and tapping into new customer segments.
This page highlights the significance of adopting a customer-centric approach in the aftermarket due to the rise of servitization, emphasizing the need for OEMs to excel in service and aftermarket strategies.
Servitization benefits OEMs and customers by providing stable revenue streams, reducing operational costs, and improving customer satisfaction through predictive maintenance and service contracts.
This page discusses the benefits and challenges of subscription models and advanced contract schemes in industrial servitization, emphasizing the importance of data collection, analysis, and monetization for future success.
This page discusses the application of predictive maintenance using AI models in aerospace and manufacturing industries, highlighting cost reductions and operational efficiencies. It also introduces the concept of 'softwarization,' where traditional hardware technologies are transformed into software-based solutions.
This page discusses the transition from physical to software-based solutions in the automotive industry, highlighting Tesla's pioneering role and the shift towards sustainability as a key to unlocking new value pools.
This page discusses sustainability initiatives in the automotive aftermarket, focusing on green parts, recycling programs, and remanufactured parts. It highlights the role of OEMs, green logistics, and advanced technologies in promoting sustainability. Additionally, it explores the healthcare sector's shift towards sustainable anesthesia machines, emphasizing flexibility, cost-effectiveness, and environmental benefits.
The services sector is witnessing increasing maturity in remotization, especially in workforce management (WFM). This trend affects various functions like forecasting and scheduling, and has been accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Innovations in WFM tools and technologies are enhancing efficiency and consistency in field services.
This page highlights the significant development of fully remotized offerings for field services, emphasizing the transformative impact of remotization in this sector.
The document discusses the growing importance of localization in service businesses, emphasizing the automotive industry's experience with local partnerships. It highlights the need for standardized training programs and partnerships with training vendors to ensure consistent service delivery. Additionally, it explores the growth of B2B online marketplaces, exemplified by Aero-Bay, which streamline procurement and distribution for greater efficiency and transparency.
This page discusses the importance of online marketplaces and building ecosystems around products for aftermarket offerings. It highlights the opportunities and threats of marketplaces, the value creation through integrated customer journeys, and examples from various industries like telcos and mobility.
This page discusses the expansion of services beyond traditional car-buying offers, including third-party services and digital platforms in various sectors. It highlights the transformation of industries through ecosystems, customer experiences, and cross-sector collaborations. The page also addresses anticipated disruptions in the service workforce due to technological advancements, emphasizing the need for skill transformation and automation.
The document discusses the necessity of upskilling and reskilling the current workforce due to skill shortages and the influx of new generations. It highlights the cost-effectiveness and future-proofing benefits of training existing employees. The rapid adoption of AI in aftermarket processes offers efficiency but requires highly skilled workers to manage these technologies.
The aftermarket is crucial for durable goods manufacturers, offering high-profit margins and operational benefits. Companies must tailor strategies based on market dynamics and integrate services into core operations. Contributions by experts are acknowledged.

pages.title: 洞察消费结构变化中的行业新趋势
目录

pages.abstract: 2024年消费市场企稳回升，生活方式类赛道受资本市场青睐，新型消费渐入人心。居民收入增长推动消费提质升级，部分赛道保持高景气度，家电、乳制品行业需探索新增量。电商通过业态创新保持增长，线下零售业态恢复偏弱，未来增长机遇在于消费结构变化。
pages.title: 主要发现

pages.abstract: 本页面主要介绍研究范围与方法论，强调研究的边界和采用的方法，为后续研究提供理论基础和实践指导。
pages.title: 研究范围与方法论

pages.abstract: 德勤研究了近600家消费品零售上市企业的绩效，通过对比细分行业头部企业，洞察行业发展趋势和驱动因素。研究企业共580家，2022年总体业绩规模达7.9万亿人民币，其中A股、港股和中概股企业分别贡献3.79万亿、3.76万亿和0.32万亿元。
pages.title: 研究范围
消费品零售行业宏观分析

pages.abstract: 2024年1-2月，实物消费复苏，社零增速提升两个百分点，实物线上零售和餐饮收入实现两位数增长，成为消费复苏的关键驱动。社会消费品零售总额及增速显示，2024年1-2月社零增长5.5%，快于去年同期。
pages.title: 2024年消费市场起步平稳

pages.abstract: 2024年，大部分消费品类和零售业态增长加快，烟酒类消费保持两位数增长，粮油食品、饮料、化妆品增速高于去年同期。限额以上消费品和零售业态同比增速显示，烟酒类、粮油食品类、饮料类等消费品类和专业店、便利店等零售业态增速显著。
pages.title: 进入2024年，大部分细分消费品类和零售业态增长加快。烟酒类消费保持两位数增长，粮油食品、饮料、化妆品增速高于去年同期水平

pages.abstract: 该页面展示了实物消费与服务消费的回暖速度对比，以及消费者信心指数的变化趋势。数据显示，服务消费增速显著高于实物消费，且消费者信心指数持续处于低位，表明消费信心有待进一步回升。
pages.title: 实物消费回暖速度仍不及预期，且消费信心有待进一步回升

pages.abstract: 2024年作为消费促进年，政策聚焦新型消费、传统消费和服务业，推动消费结构升级。从2023年1月到2024年3月，政府出台多项政策，包括扩大内需、促进品牌消费、乡村振兴、绿色智能家电消费、降低房贷利率、旅游消费、个人所得税调整、即时配送、支付服务优化等，旨在激发消费潜力，促进消费稳定增长。
pages.title: 促消费政策效应的持续释放有望持续激发消费潜力，促进消费稳定增长

pages.abstract: 2023年全国居民人均可支配收入实际增速达到6.1%，居民收入稳步上升，消费结构升级，食品烟酒、居住、交通通信等消费支出全面转正，其中三项服务消费支出较2019年增长26.9%。
pages.title: 全国居民人均可支配收入增长加快，2023年实际增速达到6.1%。居民收入稳步上升将为消费结构升级提供动力

pages.abstract: 2023年以来，服务消费市场持续升温，旅游出行市场增速加快，国内旅游收入和出游人数显著增长。全国重点零售和餐饮企业销售额同比增速提升，春节期间零售企业品类销售表现强劲，尤其是骑行装备、滑雪装备和绿色有机食品销售额大幅增长。
pages.title: 2023年以来服务消费市场持续升温，拉动社交出行相关实物消费

pages.abstract: 该页面展示了电商直播用户规模的快速增长、新型消费销售额的显著增长以及线上服务消费用户规模的持续扩大，反映了新业态新模式对新消费规模增长和消费提质扩容的推动作用。
pages.title: 新业态新模式持续助力基于兴趣和生活方式的新消费规模增长，并推动消费提质扩容

pages.abstract: 本页介绍了绿色可持续消费理念的发展历程和相关政策，展示了消费者对可持续产品特征的认知和可持续生活方式的意愿分布，以及二手交易相关新设企业数量的增长趋势。
pages.title: 绿色可持续消费理念与政策推动

pages.abstract: 中国正经历人口老龄化、新生儿人数和结婚率下降以及工作时长增加带来的消费结构变革，影响家庭结构和生活方式。
pages.title: 当前，中国正在经历由人口代际、家庭结构和生活方式变化影响下的新一轮消费结构变革

pages.abstract: 2019-2023年新消费企业投资数量和金额在2021年达到顶峰，随后下降。2023年食品饮料和化妆品领域投资活跃，部分获投企业包括太阳、CODE MINT等。
pages.title: 在新的消费结构变化中，我们看到过去一年，消费领域投资更加理性。资本市场对确定性更高的食品饮料、化妆品等细分领域持续保持较高的关注度

pages.abstract: 过去一年消费品企业上市步伐放缓，A股主板注册制改革后审核收紧，上市数量下降。2023年A股、港股、中概股上市数量分别为23、8、4家，首发募资额分别为16642、8885、无数据百万元。代表企业包括Haismart、ZJLD珍酒李渡集团等。
pages.title: 从二级市场来看，过去一年消费品企业上市步伐有所放缓，特别是A股主板注册制改革落地以来，审核日趋收紧，全年消费品企业上市数量有所下降

pages.abstract: 2023年零售业新上市企业数量和募资额较2022年略有回升，跨境电商迎来发展契机，相关企业加快上市步伐。2023年上市代表企业包括百果园、赛维时代、友宝和三态股份。
pages.title: 反观零售业态，2023年新上市企业数量和募资额较2022年略有回升。国货出海趋势下，跨境电商迎来发展契机，相关企业加快上市步伐

pages.abstract: 2024年初消费品零售企业加快IPO步伐，涉及鞋包配饰、二手电商、茶饮等多个细分行业。1-3月投融资集中在餐饮、食品饮料和化妆品领域，投资数量和金额显著，反映了资本对情绪价值类消费和生活方式类赛道的关注。
pages.title: 来到2024年，国内零售消费领域资本活跃度稳步提升，情绪价值类消费和生活方式类赛道受资本市场的持续关注

pages.abstract: 该页面分析了消费市场未来趋势，指出生育率下降导致母婴消费转向宠物和陪伴类消费，银发经济推动老年消费，一代户生活方式促进速食和便利店发展，女性悦己需求带动护肤和运动消费，折扣化运营满足品质和性价比需求，亚健康状态促进健康化消费。
pages.title: 展望消费市场未来趋势，机遇蕴藏于结构变化之中
主要消费品和零售行业上市细分领域概览

pages.abstract: 过去两年，消费品细分赛道业绩分化明显，社交、悦己、即时需求的生活方式类消费快速增长，金银珠宝、化妆品、白酒等实现两位数增长，家电、乳制品等保持个位数增长，运动鞋服行业分化，宠物食品受海外影响降速，畜牧养殖恢复正增长，调味品和时尚服饰面临挑战。
pages.title: 回看过去两年上市公司业绩，消费品细分赛道业绩分化明显。符合消费者悦己、社交、即时需求的生活方式类消费保持快速增长

pages.abstract: 该页面分析了2021至2023年上半年不同零售业态的营收增速，电商保持稳定增长，百货购物中心增速缓慢，超市和专业专卖店受线下客流影响营收下滑。电商在新业态和下沉市场的布局加快，百货企业需注重差异化竞争，超市和专业专卖店需优化运营策略。
pages.title: 在零售业态端，消费者多渠道购物的行为偏好进一步加深。包括专业专卖店、超市在内的传统线下业态恢复不及预期

pages.abstract: 主要消费品细分行业头部企业业绩保持韧性，但线下零售业态整体恢复偏弱。消费品中，宠物、白酒、运动鞋服等表现较好，而时尚服饰、调味品等出现负增长。零售业态中，电商表现较好，而百货/购物中心、超市、专业专卖店等线下渠道增速下滑。
pages.title: 总体来看，主要消费品细分行业头部企业业绩保持韧性。相较之下，线下零售业态整体恢复偏弱，企业应关注店型的优化、差异化产品和精细化运营

pages.abstract: 本页介绍了食品饮料领域的细分市场驱动因素及趋势，包括白酒、啤酒、软饮、乳制品、休闲食品、调味品、速食和宠物食品等类别。

pages.abstract: 该页面详细分析了白酒行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。行业产能过剩，向提质减量时代迈进，多元化营销推动企业打入年轻人市场，市场竞争加剧，产业地域性强，优势产能集中，酒企下游渠道商议价能力呈差异化，持续提升渠道力，打造独特的品牌故事，产区优势明显。

115.file_desc:
2024年消费市场企稳回升，生活方式类赛道受资本市场青睐，新型消费渐入人心。居民收入增长推动消费提质升级，部分赛道保持高景气度，家电、乳制品行业需探索新增量。电商通过业态创新保持增长，线下零售业态恢复偏弱，未来增长机遇在于消费结构变化。
本页面主要介绍研究范围与方法论，强调研究的边界和采用的方法，为后续研究提供理论基础和实践指导。
德勤研究了近600家消费品零售上市企业的绩效，通过对比细分行业头部企业，洞察行业发展趋势和驱动因素。研究企业共580家，2022年总体业绩规模达7.9万亿人民币，其中A股、港股和中概股企业分别贡献3.79万亿、3.76万亿和0.32万亿元。
2024年1-2月，实物消费复苏，社零增速提升两个百分点，实物线上零售和餐饮收入实现两位数增长，成为消费复苏的关键驱动。社会消费品零售总额及增速显示，2024年1-2月社零增长5.5%，快于去年同期。
2024年，大部分消费品类和零售业态增长加快，烟酒类消费保持两位数增长，粮油食品、饮料、化妆品增速高于去年同期。限额以上消费品和零售业态同比增速显示，烟酒类、粮油食品类、饮料类等消费品类和专业店、便利店等零售业态增速显著。
该页面展示了实物消费与服务消费的回暖速度对比，以及消费者信心指数的变化趋势。数据显示，服务消费增速显著高于实物消费，且消费者信心指数持续处于低位，表明消费信心有待进一步回升。
2024年作为消费促进年，政策聚焦新型消费、传统消费和服务业，推动消费结构升级。从2023年1月到2024年3月，政府出台多项政策，包括扩大内需、促进品牌消费、乡村振兴、绿色智能家电消费、降低房贷利率、旅游消费、个人所得税调整、即时配送、支付服务优化等，旨在激发消费潜力，促进消费稳定增长。
2023年全国居民人均可支配收入实际增速达到6.1%，居民收入稳步上升，消费结构升级，食品烟酒、居住、交通通信等消费支出全面转正，其中三项服务消费支出较2019年增长26.9%。
2023年以来，服务消费市场持续升温，旅游出行市场增速加快，国内旅游收入和出游人数显著增长。全国重点零售和餐饮企业销售额同比增速提升，春节期间零售企业品类销售表现强劲，尤其是骑行装备、滑雪装备和绿色有机食品销售额大幅增长。
该页面展示了电商直播用户规模的快速增长、新型消费销售额的显著增长以及线上服务消费用户规模的持续扩大，反映了新业态新模式对新消费规模增长和消费提质扩容的推动作用。
本页介绍了绿色可持续消费理念的发展历程和相关政策，展示了消费者对可持续产品特征的认知和可持续生活方式的意愿分布，以及二手交易相关新设企业数量的增长趋势。
中国正经历人口老龄化、新生儿人数和结婚率下降以及工作时长增加带来的消费结构变革，影响家庭结构和生活方式。
2019-2023年新消费企业投资数量和金额在2021年达到顶峰，随后下降。2023年食品饮料和化妆品领域投资活跃，部分获投企业包括太阳、CODE MINT等。
过去一年消费品企业上市步伐放缓，A股主板注册制改革后审核收紧，上市数量下降。2023年A股、港股、中概股上市数量分别为23、8、4家，首发募资额分别为16642、8885、无数据百万元。代表企业包括Haismart、ZJLD珍酒李渡集团等。
2023年零售业新上市企业数量和募资额较2022年略有回升，跨境电商迎来发展契机，相关企业加快上市步伐。2023年上市代表企业包括百果园、赛维时代、友宝和三态股份。
2024年初消费品零售企业加快IPO步伐，涉及鞋包配饰、二手电商、茶饮等多个细分行业。1-3月投融资集中在餐饮、食品饮料和化妆品领域，投资数量和金额显著，反映了资本对情绪价值类消费和生活方式类赛道的关注。
该页面分析了消费市场未来趋势，指出生育率下降导致母婴消费转向宠物和陪伴类消费，银发经济推动老年消费，一代户生活方式促进速食和便利店发展，女性悦己需求带动护肤和运动消费，折扣化运营满足品质和性价比需求，亚健康状态促进健康化消费。
过去两年，消费品细分赛道业绩分化明显，社交、悦己、即时需求的生活方式类消费快速增长，金银珠宝、化妆品、白酒等实现两位数增长，家电、乳制品等保持个位数增长，运动鞋服行业分化，宠物食品受海外影响降速，畜牧养殖恢复正增长，调味品和时尚服饰面临挑战。
该页面分析了2021至2023年上半年不同零售业态的营收增速，电商保持稳定增长，百货购物中心增速缓慢，超市和专业专卖店受线下客流影响营收下滑。电商在新业态和下沉市场的布局加快，百货企业需注重差异化竞争，超市和专业专卖店需优化运营策略。
主要消费品细分行业头部企业业绩保持韧性，但线下零售业态整体恢复偏弱。消费品中，宠物、白酒、运动鞋服等表现较好，而时尚服饰、调味品等出现负增长。零售业态中，电商表现较好，而百货/购物中心、超市、专业专卖店等线下渠道增速下滑。
本页介绍了食品饮料领域的细分市场驱动因素及趋势，包括白酒、啤酒、软饮、乳制品、休闲食品、调味品、速食和宠物食品等类别。
该页面详细分析了白酒行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。行业产能过剩，向提质减量时代迈进，多元化营销推动企业打入年轻人市场，市场竞争加剧，产业地域性强，优势产能集中，酒企下游渠道商议价能力呈差异化，持续提升渠道力，打造独特的品牌故事，产区优势明显。
该页面详细分析了啤酒行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。指出供给端量稳价增，需求端多元个性化，市场高端化发展，行业垄断程度高，上游成本敏感，以及产品结构升级、全渠道营销和数字化供应链的重要性。
该页面详细分析了软饮行业的市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局和关键成功要素，包括消费者对绿色健康产品的需求增加、品牌推陈出新、新媒体营销的影响、行业竞争激烈、上游供应商议价能力弱、新进入者威胁小以及多元化产品矩阵、品牌效益打造和全链路数字化运营的重要性。
该页面详细分析了乳制品行业在2022年的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局及关键成功要素，强调了功能性乳制品需求增加、电商渠道的推动作用、渠道下沉策略以及多样化销售渠道和全球供应链的重要性。
该页面详细分析了休闲食品行业的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局及关键成功要素，指出消费者需求多元化、健康化和理性消费趋势，市场竞争激烈且区域特色明显，强调供应链整合、全渠道运营和生产工艺的重要性。
本页内容涵盖了调味品行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局和关键成功要素。行业趋势包括“零添加”健康产品需求增加、产品复合化和即时零售渠道布局。竞争格局显示行业集中度提升和消费细分推动品类分化。关键成功要素涉及智能化生产、成本优势和核心技术提升。
该页面详细分析了速冻食品行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模的增长趋势，行业竞争格局的稳定性和市场参与者的增多，以及行业发展的关键成功要素，如产品创新、销售渠道和冷链技术。
该页面详细分析了宠物食品行业的市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局和关键成功要素，包括2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利同比增速，以及行业集中度低、品牌竞争激烈、进入壁垒低等特点，强调了品牌营销、研发能力和全渠道布局的重要性。
本页介绍了农业领域的驱动因素及趋势，包括农作物产品加工、畜牧养殖和水产品，强调了这些细分领域的发展方向和关键驱动因素。
该页面详细分析了农作物产品加工行业的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局及关键成功要素，强调了绿色低碳转型、消费者对绿色健康农产品的需求增长以及企业需通过技术创新和全产业链布局提升竞争力。
畜牧养殖行业在2022年和2023年上半年表现出营收与净利的同比增长，市场规模预计以5.2%的复合年增长率增长。行业竞争充分，价格随行就市，但规模化程度较低。关键成功要素包括深耕大客户、数字化管理和全产业链联动。
该页面详细分析了水产品行业的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局及关键成功要素，指出健康化消费趋势、养殖技术发展和预制菜兴起为行业带来新机遇，同时强调了全产业链优势和全渠道营销的重要性。
本页介绍了服装鞋帽领域的驱动因素及趋势，包括运动鞋服、时尚服饰和鞋包配饰，强调了这些细分市场的发展方向。
该页面详细分析了运动鞋服行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。行业集中度上升，国产品牌崛起，市场向多场景需求发展，品牌影响力和研发设计能力是成功的关键。
该页面详细分析了时尚服饰行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素，强调了女性消费力量的崛起、本土品牌的发展、行业细分化趋势以及柔性生产、多品牌战略和供应链管理的重要性。
该页面详细分析了鞋包配饰行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。指出情绪价值和绿色可持续需求的增长，市场竞争的激烈，以及差异化体验、DTC模式和全渠道营销的重要性。
本页介绍了奢侈品和化妆品领域的驱动因素及趋势，具体包括金银珠宝和化妆品两个细分市场。通过分析这些细分市场的特点和趋势，可以更好地理解其发展动力。
该页面详细分析了金银珠宝行业的营收与净利增速、市场规模、行业趋势、竞争格局和关键成功要素，强调了市场需求扩大、年轻消费群体推动、渠道广泛布局、行业集中度提升、产业聚集效应以及黄金首饰的市场主导地位，同时指出全域营销、全产业链整合和工艺创新的重要性。
该页面详细分析了化妆品行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利同比增速，市场规模预测，行业趋势，竞争格局和关键成功要素。数据显示，行业市场规模预计将持续增长，竞争格局较为分散，大众市场竞争激烈，研发能力和品牌矩阵是成功的关键。
本页面介绍了家电领域的驱动因素及发展趋势，通过图形和图标展示了相关概念，如目标、齿轮和数据图表，强调了家电行业的发展动力和未来方向。
该页面详细分析了家电行业的2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素。行业正向高端化智能化发展，政策促进绿色智能家电发展，新兴小家电需求提升。头部企业市场地位稳定，生产规模化和核心产业链整合提升上游议价能力。产业链一体化、全渠道覆盖和产品技术创新是关键成功要素。
本页介绍了零售业态的细分领域驱动因素及趋势，包括电商、超市、专业专卖店和百货购物中心，强调了这些领域的发展动力和未来走向。
电商行业在2023年保持稳定增长，即时零售和社交化多场景带来新增量，全域运营推动电商发展。竞争格局中，新模式层出不穷，B2C电商占据绝对优势。关键成功要素包括社群运营、内容化电商运营和提升履约能力。
超市行业在2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利同比增速显示了不同企业的表现。市场规模在2018年至2021年保持在8000亿元。行业趋势包括高性价比商品的受欢迎和小型综合体的发展。竞争格局显示行业集中度低和渠道多元化导致的竞争激烈。关键成功要素包括优化供应链、全渠道平台发展和自有品牌建设。
该页面详细分析了专业专卖店在2022年和2023年上半年的营收与净利同比增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素，指出需求导向选品、线上化消费、极致性价比折扣店崛起等趋势，以及多元化渠道竞争加剧、不同品类专卖店竞争态势、数字化提升运营效率、聚焦下沉市场和调整业务适应即时化折扣化零售格局等关键成功要素。
该页面详细分析了百货/购物中心行业的2022年和2023年上半年营收与净利同比增速，市场规模，行业趋势，竞争格局及关键成功要素，指出行业正向高质量发展，需精细化数字运营和提升性价比购物需求，同时面临同质化竞争，需从多方面改造原有业态。

pages.abstract: 2022年零售新上市企业数量和募资额均显著下降，与过去三年相比，企业数量从2018年的22家降至2022年的3家，募资额也从2019年的90,000百万元降至2022年的100百万元。代表企业包括ZIBUYU、MINISO、大健云仓和YUWA，显示新业态新模式回归零售本质，聚焦产品和供应链效率提升。
pages.title: 2022零售新上市企业不及过去三年，募资额也有所下降。新业态新模式回归零售本质，聚焦产品和供应链效率提升

pages.abstract: 2022年新消费领域投资理性化，主要聚焦食品饮料、化妆品、新国货服装及零售新业态，投资数量和金额在2021年达到高峰后回落，食品饮料和化妆品领域投资较高。
pages.title: 2022年，新消费领域流量红利逐渐退却，资本投资更加理性，行业正常回调

pages.abstract: 疫后消费者回归理性消费，注重真实需求和社交体验，务实和理性成为主流消费观念，实体门店体验和短视频对决策影响最大。
pages.title: 疫后消费者回归消费理性、追求悦己体验

pages.abstract: 疫后消费者更倾向于多元化购物方式，如直播和即时零售，且愿意为绿色环保产品支付溢价，特别是在营养健康、美妆护肤、食品饮料和个人护理领域。消费者在直播间购物的主要原因是价格便宜、促销力度大和能直观了解商品。
pages.title: 疫后消费者拥抱多元创新、要绿色可持续
主要消费品和零售行业上市细分领域概览

pages.abstract: 该页面详细分析了疫后多个消费行业的趋势展望，包括运动鞋服、化妆品、金银珠宝、食品、乳制品、农产品、粮油加工、肉制品、软饮、啤酒、调味品、宠物食品、白酒、餐饮、超市、专业专卖店等。指出在消费升级、原料成本改善、社交场景恢复和新业态新模式推动下，各行业将呈现复苏和增长态势。
pages.title: 趋势展望

pages.abstract: 随着线下消费场景加快修复，各类消费将迎来复苏。宠物食品、白酒、调味品、速食、乳制品、休闲食品、农产品、啤酒和软饮、运动鞋服、化妆品、金银珠宝等行业在疫情期间表现各异，未来在消费升级和消费场景恢复的推动下，预计市场将持续增长。
pages.title: 随着线下消费场景加快修复，升级类必选消费和可选消费将迎来复苏

pages.abstract: 疫情加速了消费者购买行为的改变，线下业态营收持续走弱，电商保持稳定增长，百货和超市受疫情影响较大，专业专卖店在政策激励下有望稳定增加，行业迫切需要数字化转型。
pages.title: 疫情加速了消费者购买行为的改变。包括专业专卖店、百货在内的线下业态营收状况持续走弱，行业迫切需要数字化转型

pages.abstract: 该页面分析了2021年和2022年上半年不同行业（如金银珠宝、宠物食品、白酒、啤酒、运动鞋服、食品、农产品、粮油加工、化妆品、速食）的营收和净利增速情况，指出原料价格上涨导致食品和农产品盈利分化，品牌溢价推动运动鞋服和酒类盈利能力提升。同时，疫情对各行业的影响也有所体现。

116.file_desc:
2023年消费市场在政策推动下复苏，居民收入增长提供动力，消费赛道投资回归理性，疫后需求多元化，线下社交场景推动消费升级。
本页面主要介绍研究范围与方法论，强调研究的边界和采用的方法，为后续研究提供理论和实践指导。
本页详细介绍了德勤对550多家消费品零售上市企业的研究范围，涵盖A股、港股和中概股上市企业，总结了2021年的总体业绩规模，并指出研究数据来源和时间范围。
2023年1-2月，社会消费品零售总额实现正向增长，各类零售额和增速均有所回升，显示消费市场复苏迹象。随着政策支持，未来消费市场有望加快复苏。
2022年消费者消费热情受疫情影响下降，可选类消费品销售大幅下滑，必选类消费增速放缓但仍保持韧性。各类消费品在2020-2022年的销售同比增速变化显著，数据来源为国家统计局。
2022年全国居民人均可支配收入保持正向增长，必选类消费持续增长，但受疫情影响，可选类消费品支出下降。农村居民消费支出增速远超整体居民，后疫情时期消费潜力有望进一步释放。
2023年1-2月，消费在政策推动下逐步复苏，餐饮及限额以上消费品销售回暖，各地出台多项促消费政策，涵盖内需战略、品牌消费、乡村振兴、市场信心提振等方面。
2022年消费企业业绩受疫情影响表现不佳，新上市企业数量和募资额减少，行业回归理性，更加注重产品打磨。尽管如此，消费品零售行业上市企业数量仍超过疫情前水平，代表企业包括DeRUCCI慕思、Ever-tie恒太照明等。
2022年零售新上市企业数量和募资额均显著下降，与过去三年相比，企业数量从2018年的22家降至2022年的3家，募资额也从2019年的90,000百万元降至2022年的100百万元。代表企业包括ZIBUYU、MINISO、大健云仓和YUWA，显示新业态新模式回归零售本质，聚焦产品和供应链效率提升。
2022年新消费领域投资理性化，主要聚焦食品饮料、化妆品、新国货服装及零售新业态，投资数量和金额在2021年达到高峰后回落，食品饮料和化妆品领域投资较高。
疫后消费者回归理性消费，注重真实需求和社交体验，务实和理性成为主流消费观念，实体门店体验和短视频对决策影响最大。
疫后消费者更倾向于多元化购物方式，如直播和即时零售，且愿意为绿色环保产品支付溢价，特别是在营养健康、美妆护肤、食品饮料和个人护理领域。消费者在直播间购物的主要原因是价格便宜、促销力度大和能直观了解商品。
该页面详细分析了疫后多个消费行业的趋势展望，包括运动鞋服、化妆品、金银珠宝、食品、乳制品、农产品、粮油加工、肉制品、软饮、啤酒、调味品、宠物食品、白酒、餐饮、超市、专业专卖店等。指出在消费升级、原料成本改善、社交场景恢复和新业态新模式推动下，各行业将呈现复苏和增长态势。
随着线下消费场景加快修复，各类消费将迎来复苏。宠物食品、白酒、调味品、速食、乳制品、休闲食品、农产品、啤酒和软饮、运动鞋服、化妆品、金银珠宝等行业在疫情期间表现各异，未来在消费升级和消费场景恢复的推动下，预计市场将持续增长。
疫情加速了消费者购买行为的改变，线下业态营收持续走弱，电商保持稳定增长，百货和超市受疫情影响较大，专业专卖店在政策激励下有望稳定增加，行业迫切需要数字化转型。
该页面分析了2021年和2022年上半年不同行业（如金银珠宝、宠物食品、白酒、啤酒、运动鞋服、食品、农产品、粮油加工、化妆品、速食）的营收和净利增速情况，指出原料价格上涨导致食品和农产品盈利分化，品牌溢价推动运动鞋服和酒类盈利能力提升。同时，疫情对各行业的影响也有所体现。
该页面分析了疫情对线下供应链的影响，特别是对专业专卖店、百货和超市等业态的盈利压力。2021年和2022年上半年的营收和净利增速显示，电商行业表现强劲，而传统线下业态面临挑战。专业专卖店和超市受疫情影响较大，百货业则因城市封闭而营收下滑。
该页面详细列出了2020年至2022年上半年各类消费品的营收同比增速，显示大部分品类在低基数影响下实现正增长，整体消费趋势向好，但部分品类如啤酒、软饮等出现负增长。
该页面展示了疫后电商行业的增长趋势，电商在2020年和2021年均保持较高增速，但在2022年上半年增速明显放缓。线下零售业态如超市、百货和专业专卖店在2020年和2021年出现负增长，且在2022年上半年负增长态势加剧。

该页面详细分析了软饮行业的2021年和2022年上半年的营收与净利同比增速，市场规模的增长趋势，以及关键成功要素和消费者趋势。同时，还探讨了行业面临的机遇与挑战，包括多场景消费需求、消费者需求变化和产品情绪价值。

该页面详细分析了休闲食品行业的2021年和2022年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，关键成功要素，消费者趋势以及面临的机遇与挑战。通过产品创新、全渠道运营和数字化供应链等策略，企业需应对市场竞争加剧、食品安全成本上升和渠道创新等挑战。

该页面详细分析了肉制品行业的2021年和2022年上半年的营收与净利增速，市场规模，关键成功要素，消费者趋势以及面临的机遇与挑战。强调了生产技术创新、线上渠道拓展的重要性，以及健康化、细分化和便携预制菜的消费需求。同时指出受上游影响大和市场增长空间大的行业特点。

该页面详细分析了化妆品行业的营收与净利增速、市场规模、关键成功要素、消费者趋势及机遇与挑战，展示了各公司在2021年和2022年上半年的业绩表现，市场规模逐年增长，强调了产品创新、用户运营优化和数字供应链的重要性，并指出消费者趋势和行业面临的机遇与挑战。

该页面详细分析了百货行业在2021年和2022年上半年的营收与净利同比增速，市场规模变化，关键成功要素，消费者趋势以及面临的机遇与挑战。数据显示，部分企业营收增速显著，但净利增速存在较大波动。市场规模在2017年至2020年间有所下降。成功要素包括沉浸式购物体验、数字化转型等。消费者趋势表现为线下体验需求升级、性价比和品质兼具、数字化需求增大。行业面临同质化竞争和场景创新的挑战。

本报告深入剖析连锁经营企业面临的风险挑战，强调风险管理的战略重要性，倡导从被动防御转向主动创造价值，以推动行业高质量、可持续发展。
本文探讨了企业在复杂多变的全球环境中面临的系统性风险挑战，强调了建立主动型风险治理体系的重要性，并提出了通过组织、技术和人员三个维度的协同提升企业应对风险的能力。
本章概述了2025年全球及各地区的经济增长预测，重点分析了亚洲新兴市场和中国的零售行业机遇，包括社会消费品零售总额的增长、网上零售额的提升以及零售业景气指数的回升，展示了消费市场的回暖趋势。
2025年消费市场政策推动升级与扩容，零售业前景看好；2023年中国对外直接投资多元化，批发和零售业增长显著，主要流向多个国际和地区。
本页内容分析了在宏观环境下零售企业面临的经济和行业风险，强调了全球经济前景的不确定性、各国经济分化以及保护主义抬头对全球增长的威胁。同时，指出2025年报告将重点关注供应链、出海和人工智能转型三大风险领域，为零售企业风险管理提供策略建议。
本章探讨了地缘经贸波折下供应链风险的结构化应对策略，强调了多层次能力建设的重要性，包括供应链风控体系建设、数字化手段的应用和供应链人员能力的重塑，以应对不确定性风险，保障企业运营效率和市场竞争力。
本页详细分析了供应链风险中的主要风险领域，包括供应商端、物流与运输、仓储与库存、分销与销售等方面的风险，并强调了供应链话语权失衡和替代方案缺失的成本过高的问题，提出企业应通过多元化供应商策略来降低风险。
本页内容主要讨论了物流与运输风险，包括溯源体系失效导致的风险失控和政策性关税变化带来的供应链中断风险。企业需通过供应链多元化、优化物流网络和加强风险管理等策略来应对这些风险，保障供应链稳定和企业持续发展。
本页内容主要讨论了极端气候与自然灾害对运输线路的破坏，以及仓库选址和运营中的风险，包括自然灾害风险评估不足、存储规范执行松散、温湿度监控失效和安防系统维护滞后等问题。同时，还提到了需求预测差异和促销效果不确定性风险对库存和销售的影响。
本页介绍了构建三维框架的全链风险管控，强调组织韧性、技术使能和人才升级的重要性，通过系统化治理、跨职能协作和动态风险监测，培养复合型人才，利用AI和IoT技术实现风险实时感知与响应，形成预防-识别-应对的闭环。同时，提出供应商管理策略，包括多元化供应链网络布局和本地化产能渗透，以保障供应链的稳定性和响应速度。
本页内容涵盖智能库存动态管理、数据驱动防损分析、全链路风险预警技术手段以及人员能力培养的多元化和数字化，强调通过数字化技术提升库存管理效率和人员技能，以应对供应链风险。
德勤的AI工具通过收集供应商基础信息，对直接和间接风险进行持续监控和分析，识别影响供应链稳定性的风险因素，有效防控供应商风险，缓解潜在风险。
